- Layers (Y1): fx and New Fill or Adjustment footer buttons, F7 for the panel, collapsed folders saved (`Doc.collapsed`, `collapsedFolders`), vector mask thumbnails, drag an effect row to delete, a bit depth tag, Convert Bit Depth in the menu; Negation, Reflect, Glow and Xor as layer-only modes (`EXTRA_BLEND_MODES`, `LAYER_BLEND_MODES`; saved to PSD as Normal); an artboard lock.
- Other layers (Y2): Auto-Blend Multiband, a Laplacian pyramid blend along the panorama seams into a new layer (not gradient-domain); Move tool hover outline for Auto-Select; arranging below the Background refused; a new frame takes the pixel layer under it; Reload Frame for video layers.
- Masks and channels (Y3): brush, pencil, eraser and fills paint a targeted alpha channel (`beginAlphaStroke`, `alphaRaster`, `rasterMask`, the alpha branch in `regionEdit`); Gradient refuses a channel target with a notice; Color Range Luminosity Range.
- Non-destructive (Y4): the Gradient tool edits the active Gradient Fill layer with its handles and can make a fill layer (`gradientFillTarget`, `gradientFillAlong`, `gradientFillAddStop`, `gradientAsFillLayer`); a new fill layer takes the work path as its vector mask; a Live Content section in Properties; `reorderSmartFilter` and `transferSmartFilter` (engine side).
- Transform (Y5): Liquify on smart objects kept as an editable smart filter (`runLiquifySmart`); Adaptive Wide Angle focal length and crop factor; Auto-Align Spherical and Collage (backend log).
- Paths (Y6): Pen Alt-convert and Ctrl-move, a Pixels mode; Curvature Pen point drag and corner toggle; Freeform Pen straight segments with Alt; even-odd fill rule (`path-fill-rule`); custom dashes, dash offset and stroke opacity on shapes; the clipping path written to PSD (resource 2999).
- Type (Y7, Y8): per-range attributes (`RunAttrs`: family, size, colour, weight, bold, italic, baseline shift, tracking, language; `withRunAttrs`, `runAttrsOver`, `styleSegments`) with `type-range-style`, `type-range-character-style` and `type-angle`; per-script fallback fonts; JetBrains Mono as a text font; South Asian language options and a paragraph Text Direction; a face picker that previews on hover and restores on Escape (`facePicker`, `previewTextLayer`); per-letter colours and faces from the editor selection.
- Adjustments (Y9): a Normalise adjustment (`normalisePixels`); text blend gamma applied (`setTextBlendGamma`); Multichannel from Lab; HDR ghost removal (backend log); grading wheel double-click reset.

- Themes, notices, palette (W1): eleven new profiles (Pro Dark, Pro Medium Grey, Pro Light Grey, Pro Light, Classic, Solarized Dark, Adwaita Light, Adwaita Dark, Breeze Dark, Soft Light, Soft Dark) in `themes.ts` and the first-paint tables in `index.html`, text contrast at least 7.33 and secondary at least 5.55, border-light at least 3.06; Theme moves to the Window menu; notices built once with actions, a close button and a history (Window > Notices); in-window question dialogs fall back to the native ones when the overlay root is missing; a busy line on the working tab; tool variants and On or Off states in the palette.
- Window and panels (W2): Tile All Vertically and Horizontally, 3-up Vertical and Horizontal for any number of documents; `panel-options`, `panel-float`, `panel-dock`, `panel-activate`, `panel-group` commands; panels float in movable frames (`Dock.float`, `dockBack`, positions kept in `formvis.dock.floats`); double-click a group header to fold it; a Remember panel layout preference.
- Guides (W3): select guides with Move, Shift to add, Delete, Escape; a guide context menu; Edit Selected Guides (`guide-edit-dialog.ts`); guide colours and artboard guides saved; Guide Layout column width, centring, artboard target, units and colour; New Guides From Shape centre; Snap To Slices; Show Artboard Guides; Show Target Path.
- View (W4): View > Flip Horizontal as a viewport transform (pixels and history untouched); a zoom ladder to 12,800%; one edge auto-scroll hook for every drag tool (`Stage.edgeScroll`, the marquee's own copy removed); flick panning and Scroll All Windows; zoom to a dragged rectangle; optional canvas scrollbars (off by default); a no-tool mode; zoom, flip and rotation pills; per-tool canvas context menus; interface zoom commands; Export As preview zoom levels.
- Fields and dialogs (W5): arithmetic in number fields through a small parser (`ui/number-fields.ts`, no eval); Tab between fields, undo inside dialogs and Alt turning Cancel into Reset in the shared base (`ui/dialog-history.ts`); label scrubbing and pop-up sliders on number fields; menu keyboard navigation (F10, Alt+letter, arrows, type-ahead); View > Show Brush Preview, Mesh, Edit Pins and Show Extras Options; `cycle-tool-mode`; `developer-tools`. The lead changed the Tab handling so focus leaves the fields at either end instead of wrapping, keeping buttons and checkboxes reachable from the keyboard.
- Type and languages (W6): OpenType features per character range (`FeatureRun`, `withRunFeature`, `featureSegments`, `shiftRuns`) with a Type > OpenType menu and ten `type-ot-*` commands; Commit and Cancel on the Type bar; Arabic and Hindi tables (machine drafts, marked for native review) for the main table, right-to-left shell layout, Arabic plural categories.
- Tools (W7): the selected tool and View switches remembered; Include Colour in tool presets and a Tool Presets button on every bar; pressure for size and opacity on every painting tool; Build-up section and interval; Shape Dynamics size control, minimum diameter, tilt scale, flip jitter and projection; Expand and Contract in the selection bars; Select Subject on Object Selection.
- Transform and the rest (W8): Free Transform reference point, skew and interpolation fields (`setTransformRefPoint`, `setLayerTransformAbout`, `skewBox`); Artboard orientation, Add New Artboard, Alt-click copy; note author and colour; a histogram data point in Record Measurements; `apply-edit` and `cancel-edit` commands.
- Files and desktop chrome (W9): Save a Copy writes a copy through the save panel and keeps the document's path; `menus-in-window` (macOS) and `custom-title-bar` with caption buttons (Windows and Linux; `capabilities/default.json` window permissions); a ComfyUI dock panel framing the user's ComfyUI address after a status check (`credentialless` frame). - Plugin folders (U1): a second plugin kind beside the sandboxed single-file host (`plugins/host.ts`, untouched): a folder with `plugin.json` and an ES module exporting `activate(formvis)` and `deactivate`, imported in the window from a Blob URL (`FolderPlugins`, API shape in the file header). The API is gated by the manifest permissions, approved by the person on enable and asked again when the version or permissions change; documents and pixels, CPU and GLSL filters (`runGlsl`), panels, tools (`unregisterTool`), box sources, events, per-plugin storage, dialogs. This code runs in the window, not a sandbox: the permission gate limits the API, not window globals. Sample in `examples/plugins/formvis-sample`.
- Packs (U2): EU AI label (a badge layer plus `DocMeta.aiLabel` written into the XMP of PNG, JPEG, WebP and TIFF exports, even with Metadata set to None); Film Look adjustment with ten generic stocks (`engine/film-stocks.ts`) and film curve points with copy and paste; Chromatic Shift adjustment; Glass ribbed, reeded, wavy and pebbled; GLB placement and re-posing in the session (`io/glb-scene.ts`); commands under Layer > Film Pack and Layer > EU AI Label; the MCP tools ailabel_*, film_*, glb_* (`automation/pack-tools.ts`).
- WebAssembly filter plug-ins (U3): ABI v1 documented in `docs/WASM_PLUGINS.md`; a fresh Worker per run with `env.progress` the only import, a 1 MB module cap, a memory cap and a wall-clock kill; a dialog generated from the schema with live preview; Filter > Plug-ins (WebAssembly) with Manage, Install, Install Example; plug-ins kept in IndexedDB and loaded at startup; usable as a smart filter (`wasm:<id>`); a Rust example in `examples/wasm-filter` and its prebuilt `public/wasm-plugins/tint-mix.wasm` (1,637 bytes).
- MCP and the UI control channel (U4, U5): apply_preset (adjustment presets moved to `engine/adjust-presets.ts`), realism_pass, match_edges, compare, depth_from_layer, set_status (`setAgentNote`), command_job; place_image fit and smart object; new_document mode, depth and colours; export to PSD, PSB and ORA; ui_state, ui_screenshot, ui_menu_list, ui_menu_invoke, ui_set, ui_dialog, ui_pointer (pressure, tilt, twist), ui_key, ui_window, control_call, file_roots (`automation/ui-control.ts`); Render Video progress and cancel. 134 tools.
- Actions and scripts (U6): nested Play Action, Button Mode with colours, function-key shortcuts, sets, Insert Menu Item; .atn import keeps unmapped steps greyed with their bytes and export writes the mapped kinds (`io/atn.ts`); Script Events Manager with Everything, scripts, per-binding switch and a results log; File > Scripts > Browse runs a JavaScript file in a Worker sandbox (`automation/script-sandbox.ts`) with only `run` and `log`.
- Automate and CLI (U7): a `.fvdrop` droplet data file run by `./formvis droplet`; Contact Sheet mode and depth; `fit-image`, `load-files-stack`, `stack-statistics`, `photomerge`, `merge-hdr` take parameters; `setup/cli_offline.py` (stack, contact, fit, photomerge, hdr without the window) and `image.*` methods in `serve`; per-recipe Edit in ComfyUI and Update.
- Retouching (V1): Content-Aware Move Sample All Layers and Transform On Drop (scale, angle, flips; applied on commit, the hole is filled only then); Remove falls back to the patch fill when LaMa is missing; Clone Source commands; Content-Aware Fill Sample All Layers and a sampling brush Add or Subtract. No Poisson blending and no live fill during the drag.

- Brush Settings (Q1): Dual Brush with its own spacing, hardness, angle, roundness, flips and Multiply or Subtract (`layDual`, `walkDual`); Brush Pose (tilt, rotation, pressure override); a Lock per section through `mergeShape` and `SECTION_KEYS` (preset apply and Reset keep locked sections); Protect Texture; a drawn Pen Pressure Curve (`ui/panels/pressure-curve.ts`); New Brush Preset dialog (`addMadeBrushPreset`); Color Dynamics purity, per-tip, fg/bg by pressure or fade; Transfer by pressure, fade, tilt or rotation with Fade Steps; angle by fade or initial direction, roundness by rotation or fade, a Scatter Control.
- Brush tool (Q2): every layer mode plus Behind and Clear in Brush and Pencil (modes the canvas lacks blend per pixel through `pixelBlend`); the pen eraser end switches to the Eraser (`Stage.isPenEraser`, button 5 or buttons and 32); on-canvas resize with vertical hardness (`updateTipDrag`, 6 px dead zone) and Ctrl+Option-drag on the Mac; `ui/brush-picker.ts` on right-click (option `engine.brushRightClick`); 13 built-in presets in Dry Media, Wet Media and Special Effects groups; preset folders, move, rename, delete; commands `set-brush`, `get-brush`, `save-brush-preset`, `rename-brush-preset`, `delete-brush-preset`, `move-brush-preset`, `rename-brush-group`; an .abr becomes a folder.
- Colour (Q3): Background Eraser Background Swatch sampling and Find Edges limits (`BgEraseOpts`, `bgDab`); the Color Picker's nine axes (H, S, B, R, G, B, L, a, b) with Lab fields, Pick from Screen (EyeDropper where present), web-safe and gamut buttons, Add to Swatches; gradient stops and midpoints edited on the canvas (`addGradientStop`, `moveGradientStop`, `moveGradientMid`, `removeGradientStop`, `setGradientStopColour`); swatch names, groups and order (`entries()`, `addColor()`); New Gradient and rename; New Pattern and pattern groups (`setPatternGroup`).
- Adjustments (R1a, R1b): an adjustment, Invert or Equalize applies to a targeted alpha channel (`engine/alpha-target.ts` `alphaPlane`, `planeMask`; `alphaTargeted`, `setAlphaTarget`, `previewAlphaEdit`, `applyAlphaEdit`; clicking an alpha row in Channels targets it); Levels histogram handles; scrubbable slider labels (`sliderRow`); Curves targeted adjustment; adjustment dialogs non-modal (Hand, Zoom, wheel work; other tools ignored while open); Replace Color localized clusters and range; Match Color from another document or layer, with source and target selections; Equalize the selected area (`equalize-layer-from-selection`); Histogram panel cache levels and hover statistics; Merge to HDR Pro align switch and entered exposure times.
- Modes and colour (R2): Convert Mode dialog (`mode-convert`, `ModeConvertDialog`) with profile, intent, BPC and dither; Color Settings ask on mode change, ask on paste (`askPasteProfile`), monitor profile, text gamma (stored, not yet applied); CMYK to RGB goes to the working RGB; TIFF tag 34675 and PSD resource 1039 profiles read and prompted; 32-bit Highlight Compression preview (`previewCompression`, `compressedRendition`).
- Writers (S1, S2): PSD colour labels on every layer; adjustment layers read from their nested settings (`flatten`, `nestedKey`), fixing live layers written as defaults; gradient map stops and dither; scaled or rotated shapes keep a vector mask; alpha and spot channels in the merged data with resources 1006, 1045, 1053 and 1077 (`addExtraChannels`); save steps recorded into actions (`kind: 'save'`); TIFF Options prompt (`TiffOptionsDialog`); Image Assets for groups (`renderGroupAlone`) in a folder; Render Video as JPEG or WebP sequences; data set file name templates; Package rewrites links to `Links/`.
- Save for Web and files (S3): Perceptual and Selective reduction, Web Snap, a colour table with pick, edit and lock; Optimized JPEG and Convert to sRGB; .aco and .ase names (and .ase groups) through `parseAco`, `parseAse`.

- Document and canvas (M1 to M3): Image Size scales the selection and adds Bilinear, Bicubic, Bicubic Smoother, Bicubic Sharper and Lanczos (`engine/resample.ts`); Canvas Size keeps proportions and estimates memory; the Crop tool gets Classic mode, drag-rotate outside the frame, Auto Adjust Opacity, a fill for opened edges, a custom ratio, a snap grid, double-click to apply, starting from a selection; Straighten on the Background crops to the largest rectangle; Perspective Crop takes an output size. Tabs: a context menu, pin, close to the right; File > Exit walks unsaved documents; closing waits for a save in flight; New Document saved presets, model sizes, black and custom backgrounds. EXIF and XMP travel through open and export with a strip option; File Info custom fields; slice type, target, message and cell options in the HTML; a status bar readout (document size, profile, resolution, efficiency, timing) in a fixed slot.
- Preferences (N1a, N1b): Edit > Preferences submenu for each page; Scratch Disks page; gamut warning colour and opacity; guide and grid line styles; slice colour and numbers; the system colour picker; animated zoom; zoom resizes floating windows; docking floating windows onto the tabs; image interpolation default; beep when done; canvas colour; tool tips, Shift tool switch, zoom to the clicked point; lower-case extensions; recent file count; cursors (crosshair while painting, precise other cursors, brush preview colour); custom checker colours; column width and gutter units; extension panels; type options (smart quotes, Esc commits, placeholder text); enhanced controls (pinch, rotate, scrub acceleration, touch).
- Shortcuts, menus, presets (N2): alternate shortcuts, saved sets, export and import; Edit > Menus (hide and colour items); preset bundle export, import and migrate; an animations switch; a tablet pressure switch.
- Settings (N3): DirectML, model folder scan, a download token, local files stats and clean, user skin files with Reload, the 90s and Duck themes, a tile engine switch, About details, API key last four and Clear, an Updates section, size placeholders in templates.
- Generation (O1, O2): Fill, Expand and Upscale stop with Escape or the status bar; seeds and negative prompts in Generative Fill; Upscale into the document or the selection (`upscaleInDocument`, `upscaleSelection`); ComfyUI recipe readiness; a multi-turn help chat; Undo This Turn across documents; ComfyUI probe report and progress bar; quick sky without a model; Object Selection edge offset; LaMa warm-up; an upscale workflow result size choice.

## Assistant: tool exclusions, waits while you drag or type, saved chats, token counts, where the words go, other agents' notice, pictures with a budget, attention when it asks · _v1.88.3 (ui/panels/assistant.ts, styles/dialogs.css, src-tauri/capabilities/default.json)

- `api.ts` removed:

```ts
  /** Content-Aware Scale (1.55.4, M4): the layer's PNG, a target size, skin protection and an optional protect mask
   *  PNG (white protects) go to the engine's seam carver; the carved PNG comes back. */
  async contentAwareScale(image: Blob, width: number, height: number, skin: boolean, mask: Blob | null): Promise<Blob> {
    const body = form({ width: String(width), height: String(height), skin: skin ? 'true' : 'false' }, [{ name: 'layer.png', blob: image }], 'file');
    if (mask) body.append('mask', mask, 'mask.png');
    return (await request('/seam/content-aware-scale', { method: 'POST', body })).blob();
  },
```

- `command-meta.ts` removed `'content-aware-scale': ['Image', 'Opens Content-Aware Scale.', 'Use when you want to resize while protecting subjects.', 'm'],`. `index.ts` keeps `rescaleLayerPixels` (Adaptive Wide Angle uses it); its comment was `/** Content-Aware Scale (1.55.4, M4): the layer's pixels replaced at a new size, its box resized in place. */`. The manual's sentence from `- Image > Content-Aware Scale changes a layer's width or height` to `goes from a quarter to twice the size in one step.` is gone. The i18n strings stay (unused, for a warp-based version later); the 1.55.4 entries stay as history.
- Warnings for future work, from the same review: do not add gradient-domain (Poisson) blending after the adaptive Selection-Aware Fill (rotation, scale, mirror, colour adaptation); do not add a live fill of the vacated area during the Content-Aware Move drag.

```ts
  if (!p || !p.selection || delta === 0 || Math.abs(delta) > 500) return;
  const sel = p.selection;
  const pad = delta > 0 ? delta : 0;
  const x0 = Math.max(0, sel.x - pad);
  const y0 = Math.max(0, sel.y - pad);
  const x1 = Math.min(p.doc.width, sel.x + sel.w + pad);
  const y1 = Math.min(p.doc.height, sel.y + sel.h + pad);
  const w = x1 - x0;
  const h = y1 - y0;
  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) return;
  const data = new Uint8Array(w * h);
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) data[y * w + x] = sel.valueAt(x0 + x, y0 + y);
  const out = resizeMask(data, w, h, delta);
  host.applySelection(SelectionMask.cropped(x0, y0, w, h, out), 'replace', delta > 0 ? 'Expand Selection' : 'Contract Selection');
```

- `layer-structure.ts` `stampDown(host)`: one layer merges a copy into the pixel layer below (a locked or non-pixel layer below is refused); several merge into a new Stamp layer above the top one. `mergeLayers` refuses layers locked all or pixels. `stepSibling` holds the old one-layer reorder; `moveActive` steps every selected layer. Replaced body of `moveActive` (now inside `stepSibling`):

```ts
    const layers = p.doc.layers;
    const i = layers.findIndex((l) => l.id === act.id);
    let j = i + by;
    while (j >= 0 && j < layers.length && layers[j].parentId !== act.parentId) j += by;
    if (j < 0 || j >= layers.length) return false;
    const lo = layers[Math.min(i, j)];
    const hi = layers[Math.max(i, j)];
    const loSet = subtree(layers, lo.id);
    const hiSet = subtree(layers, hi.id);
    const start = layers.findIndex((l) => loSet.has(l.id));
    const end = layers.findIndex((l) => l.id === hi.id);
    const seg = layers.slice(start, end + 1);
    const next = [
      ...layers.slice(0, start),
      ...seg.filter((l) => hiSet.has(l.id)),
      ...seg.filter((l) => loSet.has(l.id)),
      ...layers.slice(end + 1),
    ];
    p.setLayers(normalizeClips(next));
```

CLOSE_GAPS P26 first pass, the owner's rule: every message, note and command description a person or an agent reads names the file format (PSD, PSB, .abr, .grd, .ggr, .aco, .ase, .asl, .csh, .atn, .kra, .afphoto, .act, .pat, .tpl) instead of a product. Examples of what was replaced: `'Not a Photoshop gradient file.'`, `'Not a GIMP gradient file.'`, `(only version 5, Photoshop CS and later)`, `'Not a Photoshop file.'`, `'This Krita file is not 8-bit RGBA; it opened as its merged image, one layer.'`, `'This is not a Photoshop swatch (.aco) file.'`, `'This is not an Adobe Swatch Exchange (.ase) file.'`, `'That is not an Affinity file.'`, `'This Affinity file carries no preview formvis can read.'`, `|| 'Affinity'`, `Affinity files cannot be read layer by layer;`, `'Not a Photoshop custom shape (.csh) file.'`, `'not a Photoshop actions file'`, `'not a Photoshop styles file'`, `This is not a Photoshop brush file this reader knows`, `'Not an Adobe Color Table (.act) file.'`, `(Photoshop keeps 50 by default, up to 1000)`, `. ```ts
  private async fill(): Promise<void> {
    const names = this.d.recent();
    let modified = new Map<string, number>();
    try { modified = new Map((await api.library()).map((i) => [i.name, i.modified])); } catch { /* names alone */ }
    const key = JSON.stringify(names.map((n) => [n, modified.get(n) ?? 0]));

    if (key === this.listKey) return;
    this.listKey = key;
    this.list.textContent = '';
    for (const name of names) {
      const row = el<HTMLButtonElement>(`<button class="cv-home-item" type="button">${icon('image', 18)}<span class="cv-home-name"></span><span class="cv-home-date"></span></button>`);
      setText(row.querySelector('.cv-home-name') as HTMLElement, name);
      const t = modified.get(name);
      setText(row.querySelector('.cv-home-date') as HTMLElement, t ? new Date(t * (t < 1e12 ? 1000 : 1)).toLocaleString() : '');
      row.addEventListener('click', () => this.d.openRecent(name));
      this.list.appendChild(row);
    }
  }
```

The owner: only Move and Transform are slow and glitchy in the app. In WebKit 26 at scale 2 (Playwright's), a 60-step Move drag: the stage drew twice, then a 3.5 to 3.7 s frame gap after release (0.4 s at scale 1, 0.65 s after a brush stroke). ## Desktop app speed: no double monitor conversion, the view table on the GPU, readable canvases on WebKit · _v1.86.2 (ui/colour-display.ts, ui/colour.ts, ui/stage.ts, engine/lut.ts, engine/surface.ts, src-tauri/src/main.rs)

The owner sent the built formvis.app (1.86.0): the browser build is quick, the app slow and glitchy. What only the app does:

- `stage.ts` `renderScene`: any `engine.viewTransform` returned the reason `'Proof Colors and colour-managed viewing are drawn on the CPU'`, and on a Mac the desktop app always has one: `ColourView.refresh` builds a document-to-monitor table from the ColorSync profile (`useDisplay` defaults to true; a browser has no profile). So every frame was composed on the CPU, read back, passed through `applyLut` in JavaScript and written again. Now `const vt = this.engine.viewTransform, viewTable = vt && !vt.gamut ? viewLut3(vt.lut) : null` and the reason is only `'the gamut warning is drawn on the CPU'` (replaced the line above); with a table the GPU layers gain a last `DisplayLayer` `{ image: null, lut: viewTable, lut3: true, ... }`, unless the display's `unsupported` names it (the native renderer). `reason` is now `let`.
- `lut.ts` `viewLut3(lut)`: the `ColourLut` sampled at the 52-cube lattice into the packed 3D table, cached per table. Checked on 20,000 colours against `applyLut` for P3-like tables on 17 and 33 grids: worst 1 level, mean 0.11 to 0.15. In Chromium (WebGPU and WebGL2 on SwiftShader) the GPU frame matches the CPU frame, mean 0.14, 99th percentile 1 level.
- `colour-display.ts`: `DisplayInfo.managed`, true in the desktop app on macOS and Windows, whose web views convert the page's sRGB to the monitor already; `displayLine` says the system converts. `colour.ts`: `monitor = c.useDisplay && this.display?.icc && !this.display.managed ? ...` (replaced `c.useDisplay && this.display?.icc ? ...`).
- `surface.ts` `createSurface`: on WebKit (`READS_ON_CPU`: AppleWebKit and not Chrome, Chromium or Edge) the new surface's first context is `getContext('2d', { willReadFrequently: true })`. Replaced `if (typeof OffscreenCanvas !== 'undefined') return new OffscreenCanvas(width, height);` and the element branch's direct `return canvas;`. Chrome is left to its own readback heuristic.
- `main.rs` `kill_backend`: on Unix, `kill -TERM` and up to 1.5 s of `kill -0` before `child.kill()` (was `child.kill()` alone). Checked standalone with rustc against a real child.

## Relight in camera space · _v1.84.0 (engine/relight.ts, gpu/relight-gl.ts, io/local-gen.ts, ui/relight-session.ts; patterns also automation/catalogue.ts)

The owner on 1.83.0: "you need to actually re-think about this and stop doing the same thing over and over again.... I literally gave you the road map". The screen-space renderer (pixels in x and y, a fudged `relief` in z, a `reach` falloff behind the aim, a tanh-bent pattern plane) is replaced by a camera-space one built on the engine's metric scene.

- `RelightGeometry` gains `bg`, `focal`, `thickness`, `zNear`, `zFar`; `.data[3]` is now distance along the camera axis (subject at 1), not 0 to 1 nearness. `relightGeometry` turns relative depth into distance (`1 / (0.3 + 0.7 d)`, the middle at 1, focal 1.2). New `sceneGeometry` (engine scene), `zSpan`. `withNormals` keeps the extra fields (replaced `return { width: geo.width, height: geo.height, data };`).
- New: `Camera`, `rayAt`, `toPx`, `sphereLambert`, `lightLift`, `goboPx`, `visibility` (eight light samples, 3D march, thickness), `shadeLayer`; `shadeRelight` rewritten as the shader's twin (two layers blended by the cut-out, dark-pixel chroma floor, dark-background cap `photo x 6 + 0.02`, spec roll-off `s / (1 + s)`). Intensity `1.4 x i^2` (was `0.95 x i^2`).
- `relight-gl.ts`: uniforms `uBg`, `uFocal`, `uThick`, `uZRange`; texture unit 5 for the background layer; `rayAt`, `toPx`, `texAt`, `zAtPx`, `sphereLambert`, `lightPos`, `goboPx`, `visibility`, `shadeLayer` and a new `main`; compile errors are logged. Removed the GLSL `zAt`, `sunTo`, `goboPlaneUV`, `goboUV` and the old `main` body, the GLSL twins of the TypeScript quoted below, as at tag v1.83.0 (`frontend/src/gpu/relight-gl.ts` lines 46 to 78 and 141 to 244).
- `local-gen.ts`: `LightSplit` gains `bgDepth`, `bgNormals`, `focal`, `thickness`, read after the texture when the header has `focal`. `relight-session.ts`: `splitGeometry` at the three split sites (replaced the `relightGeometry(sp.depth, ...)` plus `withNormals` pairs).
- Patterns 5 to 9 (caustics, lattice, arch, dapple, circle) in both `patternAt` twins, `RELIGHT_PATTERNS`, `PATTERN_CODE`, the sub-slider `shown` record and the catalogue's `kind` list.

Removed constants: `export const SHADOW_TAPS: readonly number[] = [-1, -0.33, 0.33, 1];`, `export const ALBEDO_FLOOR = 0.006;`, `export const GLINT = 0.06;`, `export const SCENE_DEPTH = 1.2;`.

Removed (TypeScript), the screen-space light:

```ts
export function sunTo(dx: number, dy: number, distance: number): [number, number, number] {
  const k = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1, e = (20 + 40 * distance) * Math.PI / 180, c = Math.cos(e), sn = Math.sin(e);
  const x = dx / k * c, y = dy / k * c - 0.35 * sn, z = 0.9 * sn + 0.6, n = Math.hypot(x, y, z);
  return [x / n, y / n, z / n];
}
export interface Gobo { to: [number, number, number]; f: [number, number, number]; r: [number, number, number]; d: [number, number, number]; sun: boolean }
export function goboBasis(type: number, pos: readonly number[], aim: readonly number[], distance: number, s: number): Gobo {
  const sun = type === 2, dx = pos[0] - aim[0], dy = pos[1] - aim[1];
  let to: [number, number, number];
  if (sun) to = sunTo(dx, dy, distance);
  else to = [dx, dy, (0.12 + 0.9 * distance) * 0.5 * s];
  const tl = Math.hypot(to[0], to[1], to[2]) || 1, f: [number, number, number] = [-to[0] / tl, -to[1] / tl, -to[2] / tl];
  const rl = Math.hypot(f[2], f[0]), r: [number, number, number] = rl < 1e-4 ? [1, 0, 0] : [-f[2] / rl, 0, f[0] / rl];
  return { to, f, r, d: [r[2] * f[1], r[2] * f[0] - r[0] * f[2], r[0] * f[1]], sun };
}
export function goboUV(G: Gobo, x: number, y: number, z: number): [number, number] | null {
  if (G.sun) return [x * G.r[0] + y * G.r[1] + z * G.r[2], x * G.d[0] + y * G.d[1] + z * G.d[2]];
  const ax = x - G.to[0], ay = y - G.to[1], az = z - G.to[2], t = ax * G.f[0] + ay * G.f[1] + az * G.f[2];
  if (t < 1e-3) return null;
  const k = Math.hypot(G.to[0], G.to[1], G.to[2]) / t;
  return [(ax * G.r[0] + ay * G.r[1] + az * G.r[2]) * k, (ax * G.d[0] + ay * G.d[1] + az * G.d[2]) * k];
}
export function goboPlaneUV(G: Gobo, x: number, y: number, z: number): [number, number] | null {
  if (G.sun) { const k = z / Math.max(0.15, G.to[2]); return [x - G.to[0] * k, y - G.to[1] * k]; }
  const dz = G.to[2] - z;
  if (dz < 1e-3) return null;
  const t = G.to[2] / dz;
  return [G.to[0] + (x - G.to[0]) * t, G.to[1] + (y - G.to[1]) * t];
}
export function goboPoint(G: Gobo, u: number, v: number): [number, number] | null {
  const gx = u * G.r[0] + v * G.d[0], gy = u * G.r[1] + v * G.d[1], gz = u * G.r[2] + v * G.d[2];
  if (G.sun) { if (Math.abs(G.f[2]) < 1e-4) return null; const t = -gz / G.f[2]; return [gx + t * G.f[0], gy + t * G.f[1]]; }
  const dz = gz - G.to[2];
  if (Math.abs(dz) < 1e-4) return null;
  const k = -G.to[2] / dz;
  return k > 0 ? [G.to[0] + (gx - G.to[0]) * k, G.to[1] + (gy - G.to[1]) * k] : null;
}
export function lightAt(L: PackedLight, px: number, py: number, pz: number, nx: number, ny: number, nz: number, s: number, relief: number, steps: number, zAt: (x: number, y: number) => number, shadowAmt = 1, subj = -1): { diffuse: number; spec: number; sss: number; glint: number } {
  const zAim = zAt(L.aim[0], L.aim[1]), hL = zAim + (0.12 + 0.9 * L.distance) * 0.5 * s;
  let lx: number, ly: number, lz: number, atten = 1, maxRun = 0.45 * s;
  if (L.type === 2) {
    [lx, ly, lz] = sunTo(L.pos[0] - L.aim[0], L.pos[1] - L.aim[1], L.distance);
  } else {
    let qx = L.pos[0], qy = L.pos[1];
    if (L.type === 4) {
      const dx = L.aim[0] - L.pos[0], dy = L.aim[1] - L.pos[1], d = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1, tx = -dy / d, ty = dx / d, half = 0.25 * s;
      const t = clamp((px - L.pos[0]) * tx + (py - L.pos[1]) * ty, -half, half);
      qx += tx * t; qy += ty * t;
    }
    const vx = qx - px, vy = qy - py, vz = (L.type === 5 ? relief + 0.6 * s : hL) - pz, dist = Math.hypot(vx, vy, vz);
    lx = vx / dist; ly = vy / dist; lz = vz / dist;
    const R = (0.25 + L.distance) * s, dA = Math.hypot(L.aim[0] - L.pos[0], L.aim[1] - L.pos[1], hL - zAim), g = (q: number): number => 1 / (1 + (q / R) ** 1.6);
    atten = 2.2 * Math.min(2.5, g(dist) / g(dA));
    maxRun = Math.min(maxRun, Math.hypot(vx, vy));
    if (L.type === 1) {
      const ax = L.aim[0] - L.pos[0], ay = L.aim[1] - L.pos[1], az = zAim - hL, ad = Math.hypot(ax, ay, az) || 1;
      const cosA = -(lx * ax + ly * ay + lz * az) / ad, cone = Math.cos((18 + 22 * L.softness) * Math.PI / 180), edge = Math.cos((30 + 30 * L.softness) * Math.PI / 180);
      atten *= smooth(edge, cone, cosA);
    }
  }
  const dzA = zAim - pz, sun = L.type === 2, behind = subj < 0 ? dzA : dzA * (1 - subj) + Math.min(0, dzA) * subj, reach = (sun ? 0.06 + 0.6 * L.distance : 0.05 + 0.4 * L.distance) * relief, rr = behind > 0 ? behind / reach : -behind / (reach * 2.5);
  atten = atten / (sun ? 1 + rr * rr : (1 + rr * rr) ** 3) * (sun ? 2.7 : 1);
  const wrapExtra = L.type === 3 ? 0.35 : L.type === 5 ? 0.5 : 0.3, wr = clamp(L.diffusion + wrapExtra + 1.2 * L.softness, 0, 1.5);
  const ndl = nx * lx + ny * ly + nz * lz, lam = clamp((ndl + wr) / (1 + wr), 0, 1);
  if (ndl < -0.6 || atten <= 1e-4) return { diffuse: 0, spec: 0, sss: 0, glint: 0 };
  let shadow = 1;
  if (L.type !== 5 && steps > 0 && lz < 0.999) {
    const flat = Math.hypot(lx, ly) || 1e-6, k = (1.5 + 4.5 * (1 - L.softness)) * (L.type === 3 ? 0.5 : 1), run = Math.max(4, maxRun), bias = relief * 0.004;
    const spread = (0.04 + 0.22 * L.softness) * (L.type === 3 ? 1.6 : 1), dx = lx / flat, dy = ly / flat, ox = -dy, oy = dx;
    let total = 0;
    for (const o of SHADOW_TAPS) {
      let sh = 1;
      const sx = dx + ox * o * spread, sy = dy + oy * o * spread, sl = Math.hypot(sx, sy) || 1, ux = sx / sl, uy = sy / sl, uz = lz / flat * (1 + Math.abs(o) * spread * 0.5);
      for (let j = 1; j <= steps; j++) {
        const t = (j / steps) * (j / steps) * run, occ = zAt(px + ux * t, py + uy * t) - (pz + uz * t) - bias;
        if (occ > 0) sh = Math.min(sh, clamp(1 - k * occ / Math.max(1, t), 0, 1));
        if (sh <= 0) break;
      }
      total += sh;
    }
    shadow = total / SHADOW_TAPS.length;
  }
  shadow = 1 - (1 - shadow) * shadowAmt;
  let pattern = 1, frame = 1;
  if (L.pattern !== 0) {
    const C = L.center, zC = zAim, band = 0.06 * relief;
    const uv = goboPlaneUV(goboBasis(L.type, L.pos, L.type === 2 ? L.aim : C, L.distance, s), px - C[0], py - C[1], subj >= 0 ? (pz - zC) * (1 - subj) + 0.3 * band * Math.tanh((pz - zC) / (0.3 * band)) * subj : band * Math.tanh((pz - zC) / band));
    const spread = L.softness + (Math.abs(L.pattern) === 2 ? 0 : 4 * Math.max(0, behind) / relief);
    pattern = uv ? patternAt(L.pattern, uv[0], uv[1], s, L.pat, L.pat2, spread) : 0;
    frame = uv ? patternAt(L.pattern, uv[0], uv[1], s, L.pat, L.pat2, spread, true) : 0;
  }
  const amount = L.intensity * 3.2 * atten * shadow * pattern, hx = lx, hy = ly, hz = lz + 1, hl = Math.hypot(hx, hy, hz) || 1;
  const nh = Math.max(0, (nx * hx + ny * hy + nz * hz) / hl), gloss = 8 + 56 * (1 - L.softness);
  const nxy = Math.max(1e-3, Math.hypot(nx, ny)), lxy = Math.max(1e-3, Math.hypot(lx, ly));
  const rim = subj > 0 ? RIM * subj * clamp(1 - nz, 0, 1) ** 2 * Math.max(0, (nx * lx + ny * ly) / (nxy * lxy)) : 0;
  return { diffuse: amount * (lam + rim) * (1 - L.diffusion) + L.intensity * 3.2 * atten * L.diffusion * 0.3 * frame * clamp(0.5 + 0.5 * ndl, 0, 1), spec: ndl > 0 ? Math.pow(nh, gloss) * amount * 0.15 : 0,
    sss: amount * (1 - L.diffusion) * SSS * Math.max(0, clamp((ndl + 0.6) / 1.6, 0, 1) - lam), glint: amount * clamp((ndl + 0.3) / 1.3, 0, 1) };
}
```

The old `shadeRelight` loop called `lightAt` per light with `relief = SCENE_DEPTH * s`, added `c.diffuse * ALBEDO_FLOOR` and `c.glint * GLINT` lifts, and multiplied by `pow(S0, 1 - takeOut)`; it is at tag v1.83.0 lines 374 to 405 of `engine/relight.ts`.

Verified: the shader and the CPU twin agree within one level on a sphere for point, sun with blinds, spot and strip; tsc clean; 194 tests pass.

## Relight on a solved scene · _v1.82.0 (engine/relight.ts, gpu/relight-gl.ts, io/local-gen.ts, ui/relight-session.ts)

The owner supplied a description of the reference's method (a scene from MoGe-2 and a subject cut-out, two layers, the original light estimated from brightness against surface direction and divided out, brightness matching, lights exposed at their aim with a gentler capped falloff, a sized source, warm light past the terminator, `photo x kept + surface x added`). The engine now solves the scene (backend HASHOUT 1.82.0); the frontend takes it.

- `local-gen.ts` `LightSplit` gains `depth`, `mask`, `level`, `geometry`; `relightSplit` reads the scene's f16 depth and u8 mask after the normals when `head.scene`. Replaced: the one-line `LightSplit`, the `headLen, head` line and the return.
- `relight.ts`: `SplitMaps.gain`; `LEVEL_REF` (0.135, the benchmark portrait's level calibrated against the reference) and `levelGain` (clamped 0.5 to 3). `TAKE_OUT` 100 (was 0): with the scene's split the pixel is `photo x Original + surface x light`. `shadeRelight` multiplies added light by the gain and adds `sss` (red, a third into green) scaled by the pixel's warmth (replaced `er += L.color[0] * c.diffuse * win; ...`). `lightAt` returns `sss` (`SSS` 0.6 times the wrap beyond the terminator); the early out is `ndl < -0.6` (was `lam <= 0`, which also dropped the warm spill); a local light is exposed at its aim, `atten = 2.2 x min(2.5, g(dist) / g(dAim))` with `g(q) = 1 / (1 + (q / R)^1.6)` and `R = (0.25 + d) s` (replaced `const R = (0.4 + L.distance) * s;` and `atten = 2.6 / (1 + (dist / R) * (dist / R));`); the wrap gains `1.2 x softness` (the source's size; replaced `wr = clamp(L.diffusion + wrapExtra, 0, 1.5)`).
- `relight-gl.ts`: the same falloff, wrap, early out, gain (`uGain`) and warm spill; imports `SSS`. Replaced lines as quoted above in GLSL form, plus `E += add;` and the uniform list.
- `relight-session.ts`: when the split carries a scene, the geometry is built from its depth and normals at every site (`loadSplit`, `apply`, `commit`), the gain is passed, and `loadDepth` no longer overwrites a scene's geometry (`proxy.scene`). Replaced: the proxy type, the three `split = { shading, residual }` lines, the `loadDepth` geometry line and the import.

Benchmark (seven frames, values read off the reference's panels; frame 26's aim taken from its visible aim tip): mean error 0.27 to 0.54 stops each.

The owner on 1.80.0: "not how light and shadows actually works and is not a true parity". Read every value off the reference's panels instead of guessing: frame 26 is Intensity 82 and frame 28 is 31 (the benchmark had them swapped since 1.78.0), frame 40 is Intensity 53, Softness 18, Width 38, Feather 30, Rotation 12, frame 33 Rotation -78, Close about 30 for every sun; and the reference draws a pattern-centre reticle apart from the aim. Replaced: `const band = 0.06 * relief, uv = goboUV(goboBasis(...), px - L.aim[0], py - L.aim[1], ...)` and GLSL `bool hit = goboUV(type, pos, aim, ...)`. `goboUV` and `goboPoint` stay exported for a perspective projector.

On the canvas a ringed reticle; Shift-drag places it, then it drags. `relight.apply` documents `pattern.center`. Replaced in `tools/relight.ts`: `Drag`, `docOf`, the `['pos', 'aim']` hit loop, the `down` fallback, the projected-quad overlay and its import; in the session `moveLight` and the canvas note.
- Strip feather is a fraction of the strip's width, centred on its edge (feather 30 on width 38 was a strip at 0.2 strength, invisible). Replaced: `m = smooth(hl, hl - feather, Math.abs(y)) * smooth(hw, hw - feather, Math.abs(x));` and its GLSL twin.

## Slat shadows that look like light · _v1.80.0 (engine/relight.ts, gpu/relight-gl.ts)

The owner on 1.79.0: "how god awful it looks". At 100 percent beside the reference's face: the stripe edges were razor hard, torn and jagged through the hair, and the lit stripes pale, like a translucent sheet laid over her. Three causes, found by looking:

- The slat phase wrapped: `smooth(-hf, hf, ph)` jumped from 0 to 0.5 where `ph` wrapped from 1 to 0, so one edge of every slat was a hard step whatever the feather. Now the distance to the slat's centre, cyclic: `q = |fract(ph - open / 2 + 0.5) - 0.5|`, `m = smooth(open / 2 + hf, open / 2 - hf, q)`. Replaced: `const hf = Math.min(f, 0.45) * 0.5, wash = ...;` and `m = frameOnly ? frame : frame * (smooth(open + hf, open - hf, ph) * smooth(-hf, hf, ph) * (1 - wash) + open * wash);` (GLSL: `float hf = min(f, 0.45) * 0.5, ...;` and the `sstep` twin). Edge cap 0.3 of a period, so the gaps still reach dark.
- The projection read raw depth: Depth Anything's noise in the hair tore the slats into ragged patches. `relightGeometry` keeps a smoothed depth (box blur s/150, 3 passes) in `.a` (normals still from the lightly blurred depth), and the projection soft-clamps the depth difference to the aimed surface at `0.06 relief` (`band * tanh(dz / band)`), so a far wall no longer gets a displaced ghost band. Replaced: `const data = new Float32Array(n * 4);`, `data[i * 4 + 3] = clamp(sm[i], 0, 1);`, `const uv = goboUV(..., pz - zAim);` (GLSL `vec3(p - aim, pz - zAim)`).
- Light colour is the sRGB swatch to the power 1.5: the reference's lit skin is a saturated peach (219, 148, 113), formvis gave (220, 163, 130). Replaced: `color: [l.color.r / 255, l.color.g / 255, l.color.b / 255],`.
- Depth Anything's 1 to 2 pixel border is often wrong (0.83 at x 0 against 0.02 beside it), which lit a pink line down the picture's edge in Neon: the outer 3 pixels copy the depth just inside. Replaced: `const s = Math.max(w, h), n = w * h, sm = new Float32Array(depth), relief = NORMAL_RELIEF * s;`.
- The Neon Look's lights moved in from the edges (pink 0.2, 0.62; cyan 0.8, 0.35; were 0.08, 0.7 and 0.92, 0.3).

Lit face (219, 155, 119) against the reference's (219, 148, 113); lit hair (188, 145, 115) against (188, 142, 114); Blinds mean gain error 0.55 stops, subject 90th percentile 1.03 against 1.02.

## Gobos projected onto the depth surface · _v1.79.0 (engine/relight.ts, gpu/relight-gl.ts, extensions/tools/relight.ts)

The owner on 1.78.0: the blinds must follow "the contours of the body/subject/objects/environment". Studied the reference's close-ups (frames 13, 15, 21): the slat shadows rise about 20 to 25 degrees to the right, curve around the arm like contour lines on a cylinder, jump at the arm's and face's silhouettes, and the frame the reference draws is a quadrilateral, a projected rectangle. 1.78.0 drew the pattern flat in picture space with a 0.05 nudge by depth, and the nudge had the wrong sign.

- New `sunTo` (a sun's direction toward the light: the handle's side, raised toward the top of the picture and toward the camera by Close to Far, so its slat planes tilt in depth as daylight through a window does), `goboBasis` (the light as a projector: throw `f`, gobo axes `r` and `d`, `d` nearest the picture's down; for a sun a direction, otherwise the light's offset from the aim with its height), `goboUV` (orthographic for a sun, perspective from the light for the rest), `goboPoint` (a gobo corner back onto the aimed surface's plane, for the overlay). GLSL twins `sunTo` and `goboUV` (identical formulas; `d.x` sign as the TS).
- `lightAt`: the sun's direction is `sunTo` (replaced `const dx = L.aim[0] - L.pos[0], ..., elev = (30 + 50 * L.distance) * Math.PI / 180;` and `lx = -dx / d * Math.cos(elev); ly = -dy / d * Math.cos(elev); lz = Math.sin(elev);`, GLSL `vec2 dd = aim - pos; ... float elev = radians(30.0 + 50.0 * distance_);` and `l = vec3(-dd / dl * cos(elev), sin(elev));`); the pattern is sampled at the surface point's gobo coordinates (replaced `const par = (pz - zAim) * 0.05 / Math.max(0.25, lz), gx = px + lx * par, gy = py + ly * par;` and the two `patternAt(L.pattern, gx - L.aim[0], gy - L.aim[1], ...)` calls; GLSL `float par = ...; vec2 gp = p + l.xy * par;` and the two `patternAt(D.x, gp - aim, ...)` calls); a point the projector cannot reach gets no patterned light. The sun is 1.5 times a local light (was 1.9) since it now falls more frontally.
- `packLights`: rotation as given for every pattern (replaced `((l.pattern.kind === 'strip' ? 1 : -1) * l.pattern.rotation * Math.PI) / 180`); the projection's own tilt now does what the per-pattern sign did.
- `patternAt` (and GLSL): Blinds frame half `0.28 x scale` (was 0.33); the slat edge cap 0.45 of a period (was 0.3), softer as the reference's.
- `tools/relight.ts`: the pattern frame is drawn as the projected quadrilateral through `goboPoint` (replaced `g.save(); g.translate(b.x, b.y); g.rotate(rot); g.strokeRect(-hw, -hh, hw * 2, hh * 2); g.restore();`, the `rot` line and the import `import type { RelightLight } from '../../engine/relight';`).

Benchmark (six frames): Blinds 0.52 stops mean (was 0.62), subject 90th percentile 1.03 against 1.02, wall -0.03 against 0.01; the other five unchanged within 0.05. Close-ups beside frame 15 show the stripes curving round the arm and stepping at the silhouettes.

## Relight at parity with the reference, depth-mapped light · _v1.78.0 (engine/relight.ts, gpu/relight-gl.ts, extensions/tools/relight.ts)

The owner on 1.77.0: "it is behind... match full parity, and the depth mapping is definitely a way to map the lighting properly". The benchmark grew from three reference frames to six (23 Blinds, 27 and 26 Candlelight at two light places, 40 and 33 Strip at two angles, 31 Neon); mean gain-map error now 0.41 to 0.72 stops on all six, subject 90th percentile within 0.2 stops for Blinds, Strip and Candlelight 27.

Depth now maps the light four ways: reach (a light stops at the depth of what it is aimed at: quadratic falloff behind for a sun, quartic for a local light, so a lamp floods her and leaves the wall dark, frame 27); gobo sharpness (a Blinds, Window or Leaves pattern blurs with the depth behind the aimed surface and washes to its open fraction on the wall, frame 23; a Strip stays sharp, frame 33); height (a light stands above the aimed surface); and the split's finer normals (backend).

- `packLights`: colour is the sRGB value (the 0.2 floor gave a khaki cast on dark hair). Replaced: `color: [0.2 + 0.8 * l.color.r / 255, ...]`. Rotation keeps Photon's sign per pattern: Strip as given, the others negated. Replaced: `(-l.pattern.rotation * Math.PI) / 180`.
- `kelvinToRgb`: blue at least 40 below 6600K (Photon's 1800K keeps some blue). Replaced: `const b = t >= 66 ? 255 : t <= 19 ? 0 : 138.5177312231 * Math.log(t - 10) - 305.0447927307;`.
- `lightAt` and the shader: `hL = zAim + (0.12 + 0.9 d) x 0.5 s` (was `(0.3 + 0.9 * L.distance) * 0.5 * s`); sun elevation `30 + 50 d` degrees (was `12 + 58 * L.distance`); local lights `R = (0.4 + d) s`, `atten = 2.6 / (1 + (dist / R)^2)` (was `R = (0.08 + 0.5 * L.distance) * s`, `atten = 1 / (...)`); reach `(sun ? 0.18 + 1.8 d : 0.05 + 0.4 d) x relief`, falloff `1 + rr^2` for a sun and `1 + rr^4` otherwise, a sun 1.9 times stronger (was `reach = (0.06 + 0.6 * L.distance) * relief` and `atten /= 1 + rr * rr;`); the pattern softness grows by `4 x behind / relief` except for a Strip (was `L.softness` alone); Diffusion fill 0.3 (was 1.2); Shine 0.15 (was 0.3); a light also adds `ALBEDO_FLOOR` (0.006) times its diffuse amount, so dark hair catches light as in Photon's frame 33 (the spec line `sr += L.color[0] * c.spec * shine * win; ...` became `const lift = c.spec * shine + c.diffuse * ALBEDO_FLOOR;` plus the three sums; GLSL `E += ...` became `vec3 add = ...; E += add; S += add * ALBEDO_FLOOR;`).
- `patternAt` and GLSL: the Blinds frame half is `0.33 x scale` (was 0.5; Photon's 18 slats at 164 percent span her height); the slat edge is centred and capped, and washes to `open` when the feather passes 0.3 of a period (replaced `m = frameOnly ? frame : frame * smooth(open, open - f, ph) * smooth(0, f, ph);` and its GLSL twin); the Strip is `0.58 x length` long and `0.14 x width` wide (was 0.5 and 0.11).
- `TAKE_OUT` 0 (was 50): Photon uses the photo as its own albedo; Take out old light reshapes hard shadows when raised. The Light Strip Look's rotation is 12 again under the new sign.
- `tools/relight.ts` overlay follows the frame sizes and the sign.

The owner on 1.76.0: "still nowhere near". The per-pixel log gain (result over original) showed the gaps: point lights about 25 times too strong (subject +3.5 stops against Photon's -0.2), light colours far more saturated than Photon's, the back wall lit as much as the subject, patterns rotated the other way and sliding across the wall, the Light Strip four times too wide, and no unpatterned fill. Rotation is negated so a positive angle turns counter-clockwise as Photon's does. Replaced: `pat2: [l.pattern.length / 100, l.pattern.feather / 100, (l.pattern.rotation * Math.PI) / 180, 0],`.
- `lightAt` (and the shader): local lights fall off with `R = (0.08 + 0.5 x distance) x s`, `atten = 1 / (1 + (dist / R)^2)`. Replaced: `const wrapExtra = L.type === 3 ? 0.35 : L.type === 5 ? 0.5 : 0, wr = clamp(L.diffusion + wrapExtra, 0, 1.5);` (GLSL `... : 0.0);`). ## Relight keeps the subject · _v1.76.0 (engine/relight.ts, gpu/relight-gl.ts, io/local-gen.ts, ui/relight-session.ts, automation/catalogue.ts)

The engine's split now keeps every original detail (see backend HASHOUT 1.76.0); the frontend changes are where lights sit and how the choice reads.

- `relight.ts` `lightAt`: replaced `const hL = relief + (0.05 + 0.9 * L.distance) * s;` with `const zAim = zAt(L.aim[0], L.aim[1]), hL = zAim + (0.3 + 0.9 * L.distance) * 0.5 * s;` and the spot cone's `az = relief * 0.5 - hL` with `az = zAim - hL`. Why: the light stood above the nearest point of the picture (often a table in front), so on a subject further back it fell almost from the camera and shaded flat; anchored to the depth under its aim it rakes across the face. `(0.05 + ...)` gave grazing light and long hard nose shadows at short distances, hence the 0.3 floor.
- `relight-gl.ts`: the same two lines in GLSL (`float hL = relief + (0.05 + 0.9 * distance_) * s;` and `vec3 ax = vec3(aim - pos, relief * 0.5 - hL);` replaced).
- `local-gen.ts` `RelightEngines`: `regions: 'sam' | 'colour'` replaced by `regions: 'parts' | 'colour'; faces: boolean`.
- `relight-session.ts`: `loadSplit` loses `learned` (replaced: `const learned = engine === 'marigold' || (engine === 'auto' && this.engines.marigold);`) as Auto never runs Marigold; notes name the per-material split; Old light options `Take out, keep the subject`, `Take out with Marigold (repaints surfaces)`, `Keep, add on top` (replaced `Take out (best available)` and `Take out with SAM 2.1 regions`); new `getParts` and a `.cv-relight-parts` button shown by `syncSplit` while the parts or face model is missing.
- `catalogue.ts` `relight.apply`: `split` description and the result message no longer name SAM 2.1.

## Relight re-shades · _v1.75.0 (engine/relight.ts, gpu/relight-gl.ts, io/local-gen.ts, ui/relight-session.ts, automation/catalogue.ts)

The owner: "relighting is also reshading"; 1.74.1 multiplied new light over the photo, so the photo's own split-face shadow survived every Look. The image model is now `albedo x (Original x S0 + sum of new light) + Original x residual + highlights`, with albedo, S0 (old shading, per channel) and the residual from the engine's light split (`backend/app/localgen/relight_split.py`). Tried first and dropped, by looking at the albedo: an SH light fit on depth normals (the fit landed frontal; monocular depth makes a face a blob), Retinex gradients classified by chromaticity plus a screened Poisson solve (kept the shadow), chroma k-means normalisation (hair turned skin-coloured). Careaga and Aksoy's intrinsic model is academic-use only, so not used.

- `engine/relight.ts`: `RelightContent.split`, `SplitMaps`, `withNormals`; in `shadeRelight` the ambient term is multiplied by S0 per channel and the residual times Original starts the highlight sum; `delight` does nothing while a split is in use. Replaced: `let er = sc.ambient[0], eg = sc.ambient[1], eb = sc.ambient[2], sr = 0, sg = 0, sb = 0;` and `const k = shade ? 1 / (1 + (shade[y * w + x] - 1) * sc.delight) : 1;`.
- `gpu/relight-gl.ts`: `uS0`, `uRes` (RGBA32F, units 3 and 4), `uSplit`; `rgba` packs three channels; `uploaded.split` caches by identity. Replaced: `vec3 E = uAmbient, S = vec3(0.0);` and `gl.uniform1f(loc.uDelight, shade ? sc.delight : 0);`.
- `io/local-gen.ts`: `RelightEngines`, `LightSplit`, `relightEngines`, `halfToFloat`, `relightSplit` (4-byte header length, JSON, albedo uint8 RGB, then float16 shading, residual and normals).
- `ui/relight-session.ts`: proxy carries `albedo`, `split`, `normals`; `splitUsed`, `source` (the composite's PNG, made once), `engines`; `sourceBlob`, `loadSplit` (after `loadDepth`), `getMarigold` (installs both models), `syncSplit`; the Old light row and the licence-naming button in Scene; `commit` and `apply` fetch the split at full size. `loadDepth` keeps the model's normals on its rebuilt geometry.
- `automation/catalogue.ts`: `split` parameter; the result names the split.

Verified with the real engine and both models: point key at the right and at the left over the Marigold split move the face's shadow side and the nose shadow and the original split shadow is gone; Window Blinds and Candlelight over it; classic split; Keep equals 1.74.1; the panel under 4x CPU throttling; tsc; 194 unit tests. Known: dark hair is a little noisy in the albedo, a faint seam can remain where the old shadow was deepest, and Rembrandt's default Original lighting reads flatter over a split.

## Relight from real geometry · _v1.74.1 (engine/relight.ts, gpu/relight-gl.ts, io/local-gen.ts, ui/relight-session.ts)

The owner: the 1.74.0 output "doesn't look like relighting, more a layer effect on top of an image". True, and visible at a glance: an orange wash inside an oval. Causes, found by looking at the pixels: (1) no model in the test run, so `estimateDepth` returned a centred dome, and the depth band cut it into an oval; (2) even with depth, a 0.25 x side relief gave slopes of about 12 degrees, so Lambert was nearly uniform, a tint; (3) the 8-bit depth PNG stepped about 5 px per level at a useful relief. Fixed with the real model in the loop (Depth Anything V2 Small, pinned file, hash checked), prototyped in numpy first, then ported, and judged on full-size renders of six Looks.

- `estimateDepth`: flat 0.5 plane. Removed:

```ts
  const s = Math.max(w, h), lum = heightField(rgba, w, h, Math.max(2, Math.round(s / 30)), false), out = new Float32Array(w * h);
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
    const dx = (x / w - 0.5) * 2, dy = (y / h - 0.45) * 2, dome = clamp(1 - (dx * dx * 0.8 + dy * dy * 0.6), 0, 1);
    out[y * w + x] = clamp(0.75 * dome + 0.25 * lum[y * w + x], 0, 1);
  }
  return out;
```

- `relightGeometry` rebuilt: `boxBlur` (s/900, 2 passes), gradient x `NORMAL_RELIEF` (0.7) x side, cliff mask (gradient magnitude 1.2 or more) eroded by s/600 (`erodeMask`), gradient and mask blurred by s/130 (3 passes) and divided (normalised convolution). The old body (two box passes of s/400 and central differences at 0.25 x side) is in git at 2eb4c77.
- `SCENE_DEPTH` 1.2 for positions, falloff and shadows (was the same 0.25 relief). Light height `relief + (0.05 + 0.9 d) s` (was `0.08 + 1.4 d`), range `(0.25 + 1.5 d) s` and gain 2 (was `0.3 + 2.2 d`, 1.6), shadow `k` `1.5 + 4.5 (1 - softness)` (was `1 + 7`), bias `0.004 relief` (was `2/255 relief`), pattern parallax 0.1 (was 0.35), specular weight 0.3 (was 0.6), default Shadows 55 (was 70).
- Soft shadows: `SHADOW_TAPS` [-1, -0.33, 0.33, 1], each ray turned across the light by `(0.04 + 0.22 softness)` (x1.6 for Area), averaged; the shader repeats the taps in a fixed four-iteration loop.
- CPU `zAt` floors like the shader's `floor(p) + 0.5` lookup; before, it rounded, and shadow edges differed by up to 30 levels. Now 1 at most.
- `resampleDepth` (bilinear) for the preview copy of the model's depth.
- `io/local-gen.ts`: `localDepthValues` (float32 from `?fmt=f32`), `installModel` (the model download job, polled every 800 ms).
- `ui/relight-session.ts`: `depthFull` replaces `depthBitmap`; `readDepth`; `loadDepth` states plainly when there is no shape and shows `.cv-relight-get` (Download Depth Anything), `getDepthModel` installs then reloads the shape; `apply` uses `readDepth`. The old bitmap path through `depthFromGrey(scaled(...))` is gone (`depthFromGrey` stays exported for others).
- Neon Club: original 22, shine 18, intensities 55 and 45 (were 20, 35, 70, 60): the old values streaked the hair.

Verified: real backend with the model; six Looks rendered through `relight.apply` at 736 by 1326 and compared with the original at full size (face crops for Rembrandt and Candlelight); CPU against GPU on the model's depth: max 1, mean 0; under 4x CPU throttling the panel read the shape from Depth Anything and Done made one step; tsc clean; 194 unit tests. Not run: the no-model download button end to end (needs an engine without the model), a real GPU, the browser suite.

## Relight, second pass · _v1.74.0 (engine/relight.ts, gpu/relight-gl.ts, engine/index.ts, ui/relight-session.ts, extensions/tools/relight.ts, styles/relight.css, automation/catalogue.ts, app.ts)

The owner: "expand the relight capability even further". Chosen for what a lighting artist misses first: control over where light lands (depth bands), getting rid of the photo's baked light (flatten), saved setups, keyboard placement, and agent access.

- `engine/relight.ts`: `RelightLight.near`, `far` (0 to 100, optional; absent is no limit); `RelightContent.delight`, `shadows` (default 70), `ambient`; `relightFrom` reads them. `shadingField` (broad luminance blur over s/40, linear, divided by its mean, clamped 0.25 to 4) is the photo's own light; Flatten divides the albedo by `1 + (shade - 1) * delight`. `depthWindow` feathers a band by 0.04. `sceneTerms` gives ambient times Original, delight and shadows to both paths. `PackedLight.range`. `lightAt(..., shadowAmt)`. Replaced lines:

```ts
export interface ShadeOptions { shadowSteps?: number }
  const lights = packLights(content, w, h), orig = content.original / 100, shine = content.shine / 100, steps = opts.shadowSteps ?? 16;
    let er = orig, eg = orig, eb = orig, sr = 0, sg = 0, sb = 0;
      const c = lightAt(L, x + 0.5, y + 0.5, pz, nx, ny, nz, s, relief, steps, zAt);
      er += L.color[0] * c.diffuse; eg += L.color[1] * c.diffuse; eb += L.color[2] * c.diffuse;
      sr += L.color[0] * c.spec * shine; sg += L.color[1] * c.spec * shine; sb += L.color[2] * c.spec * shine;
    out[i] = Math.round(linearToSrgb(tone(lut[base[i]] * er + sr)) * 255);
    out[i + 1] = Math.round(linearToSrgb(tone(lut[base[i + 1]] * eg + sg)) * 255);
    out[i + 2] = Math.round(linearToSrgb(tone(lut[base[i + 2]] * eb + sb)) * 255);
  return { lights, original: num(o.original, 0, 100, 60), shine: num(o.shine, 0, 100, 20), ...(typeof o.look === 'string' ? { look: o.look } : {}), ...(o.depth === 'model' || o.depth === 'estimate' ? { depth: o.depth } : {}) };
```

- `gpu/relight-gl.ts`: `uF[8]` (bands), `uShade` (R32F, a 1 by 1 of 1.0 when absent), `uDelight`, `uShadows`, `uAmbient`; `renderRelight(..., shade)`; `uOrig` is now unused in the shader (kept bound, harmless). Replaced: `vec3 E = vec3(uOrig), S = vec3(0.0);`, the two `E +=` and `S +=` lines without `win`, and `vec3 lin = vec3(toLin(base.r), toLin(base.g), toLin(base.b));`.
- `engine/index.ts`: `setRelight(id, content, image, amendNew = true)`; the session passes `this.isNew`. Replaced `if (p.history.last?.name === 'New Relight Layer' && !this.stroke) {`.
- `ui/relight-session.ts`: `apply(content)` (headless, Depth Anything when ready, one step); proxy carries `shade`; rows `near`, `far`, `delight`, `shadows`, `ambient`; `lookButton`, `userLooks`, `storeLooks`, `saveLook` (storage key `formvis.relight.looks`, 28 at most, read through `relightFrom`, try/catch both ways); `applyLook` takes user Looks; host `nudge` and `cycle`; `sphere` is a field. The span fix: the title, the fold headings and the pill set their text on `span:last-child`; the first `span` was the icon's own, which took the text and clipped it. Replaced:

```ts
    setText(q(this.pill, 'span'), t('Edit Lighting'));
    setText(q(root, '.cv-relight-title span'), t('Relight Properties'));
      if (labels[k]) setText(q(b, 'span'), t(labels[k]));
```

- `extensions/tools/relight.ts`: `RelightHost.nudge`, `cycle`; arrows (0.005, Shift 0.05 of the canvas), Alt for the aim, Tab and Shift+Tab.
- `automation/catalogue.ts`: `relight.apply` entry and `relightApply` (look validated against `RELIGHT_LOOKS`, `kelvin` turned into a colour, ambient as `#rrggbb`, everything through `relightFrom`); `CatalogueDeps.applyRelight`. `app.ts`: `applyRelight: (content) => relight.apply(content)`.
- Skills: `formvis-driving` adjustments-and-filters gains "Relight a photo"; `formvis-harness/references/relight.md` rules 9 to 13. The `.agents` copy of the driving sub-skill was refreshed by copying the edited `.claude` file over its identical mirror, which is what `./formvis agents sync` does (not runnable here, no venv); the harness reference was edited by hand in both places.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean; 194 unit tests pass; CPU and GPU with every new control differ by 0.016 levels on average and 7 at most (pixels at a hard depth step); a near-only band darkened only the far half; in Chromium under 4x CPU and slow network throttling (network after load): `relight.apply` with a Look, with lights as data, and with an unknown Look (refused); Edit Lighting, Flatten 85, Lights from depth 40, Shadows 100, an arrow and a Shift+arrow nudge, a saved Look, Done as one Modify Relight Layer step; no page errors. ## Relight layers · _v1.73.0 (engine/relight.ts, gpu/relight-gl.ts, ui/relight-session.ts, extensions/tools/relight.ts, styles/relight.css, engine/index.ts, engine/types.ts, io/project-io.ts, app.ts, ui/layers.ts, ui/icons.ts, ui/tool-groups.ts, ui/command-palette.ts, extensions/registry.ts, extensions/tools/index.ts, automation/command-meta.ts, index.html)

The owner asked for a real Relight, modelled on the behaviour shown in a desktop editor's launch video (studied from frames only; no code, names of internals or assets taken). Decision: a Relight layer is a pixel layer that also holds `relight: RelightContent`, its raster baked from the composite beneath it at Done. It is not composited live like an adjustment layer: that matches the reference behaviour (a generated layer, reopened to change), it keeps the GPU display, PSD export, rasterize guards and every older build working with no new branch in `renderer.ts`, and a relight costs one render per edit rather than one per frame.

- `engine/relight.ts` (new, no DOM): types `RelightLight`, `RelightPattern`, `RelightContent`; `kelvinToRgb` (the widely used Kelvin curve fit); `RELIGHT_LOOKS` (14); `relightFrom` (validator, clamps every field, caps at `MAX_RELIGHT_LIGHTS` 8); `estimateDepth` (a centre dome 0.75 plus blurred luminance 0.25, used when Depth Anything is absent); `depthFromGrey`; `relightGeometry` (float RGBA: normal xyz from the depth gradient over a 0.25 * long-side relief, depth in w; floats because 8-bit normals banded under strong highlights); `packLights`; `patternAt` (blinds, strip, window, leaves by value noise); `shadeRelight` (the CPU reference) and `lightAt`.
- Shading: linear light; per light, Lambert with wrap (Diffusion, plus 0.35 for Area and 0.5 for Ring), inverse-square-like falloff whose range grows with Close to Far, a spot cone widened by Softness, a strip as the nearest point on a segment across the aim line, a sun as a direction whose elevation follows Close to Far; screen-space shadows marched toward the light over the depth field with a 2/255-relief bias (contour banding without it); the pattern sampled in the plane at the aim point with a small depth parallax; Blinn-Phong highlight scaled by Shine. Result `base * (Original + sum diffuse) + sum spec`, soft shoulder above 0.8, back to sRGB.
- `smooth(a, b, x)` divides by the signed span: the first version used `max(1e-6, b - a)`, which inverted every falling edge and put pattern light outside its frame. Replaced in both files:

```ts
const smooth = (a: number, b: number, x: number): number => { const t = clamp((x - a) / Math.max(1e-6, b - a), 0, 1); return t * t * (3 - 2 * t); };
```

```glsl
float sstep(float a, float b, float x) { float t = clamp((x - a) / max(1e-6, b - a), 0.0, 1.0); return t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t); }
```

- Cast shadows only with the model's depth (`content.depth === 'model'`): the luminance estimate made bright walls "near" and shadowed the subject.
- `gpu/relight-gl.ts` (new): WebGL2 fragment shader with the same maths, lights as five `vec4[8]` uniforms, base RGBA8 and geometry RGBA32F textures cached by array identity (`forgetRelightUploads`); larger than `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE` or no WebGL2 falls back to `shadeRelight`. CPU and GPU matched a strip's lit centroid and pixel count exactly.

      if (!data) { data = source(family, bold, italic); bytes.set(key, data); }
      if (!data) { data = source(family, bold, italic); bytes.set(fk, data); }
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`No font file for ${family}`);
```

- `io/api.ts`, `api.fontFile`: a 204 answer throws `ApiError` with status 204 instead of reading an empty body. Replaced:

```ts
    return (await request(`/fonts/file?family=${encodeURIComponent(family)}&bold=${bold ? 1 : 0}&italic=${italic ? 1 : 0}`)).arrayBuffer();
```

```ts
  /** The documents shown as tiles: the next ones after the active one, in open order. */
  private pick(): Project[] {
    const n = COUNT[this.layout], list = this.engine.projects, cur = this.engine.current;
    if (!n || list.length < 2) return [];
    const at = Math.max(0, cur ? list.indexOf(cur) : 0);
    const out: Project[] = [];
    for (let i = 1; i < list.length && out.length < n; i++) out.push(list[(at + i) % list.length]);
    return out;
  }

  private sync(): void {
    const want = this.pick();
    const ids = new Set(want.map((p) => p.id));
    for (const [id, t] of this.tiles) {
      if (ids.has(id)) continue;
      t.ro.disconnect();
      t.root.remove();
      this.tiles.delete(id);
    }
    want.forEach((p, i) => {
      let t = this.tiles.get(p.id);
      if (!t) { t = this.make(p); this.tiles.set(p.id, t); }
      if (t.title.textContent !== p.name) t.title.textContent = p.name;
      if (this.box.children[i] !== t.root) this.box.insertBefore(t.root, this.box.children[i] ?? null);
    });
    this.col.dataset.tiles = String(want.length);
    this.queue();
  }

  private make(p: Project): Tile {
    const root = document.createElement('div');
    root.className = 'cv-view-tile';
    root.dataset.id = p.id;
    const title = document.createElement('div');
    title.className = 'cv-view-tile-title';
    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    canvas.className = 'cv-view-tile-canvas';
    root.append(title, canvas);
    const tile: Tile = { id: p.id, root, title, canvas, drawn: false, ro: new ResizeObserver(() => this.fit(tile)) };
    tile.ro.observe(canvas);
    return tile;
  }

  /** The canvas box changed: match the backing store to it (only when different) and redraw. */
  private fit(t: Tile): void {
    const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;
    const w = Math.max(1, Math.round(t.canvas.clientWidth * dpr)), h = Math.max(1, Math.round(t.canvas.clientHeight * dpr));
    if (t.canvas.width !== w) t.canvas.width = w;
    if (t.canvas.height !== h) t.canvas.height = h;
    t.drawn = false;
    this.queue();
  }
```

```ts
  /** Encodes a canvas in the chosen format. PNG-8 is written as a normal PNG for now: a true 8-bit palette is not built yet. */
  private async encode(c: HTMLCanvasElement): Promise<Blob | null> {
    switch (this.fmt) {
      case 'jpeg': return toBlob(c, 'image/jpeg', this.quality / 100);
      case 'webp': return toBlob(c, 'image/webp', this.quality / 100);
      case 'gif': {
        const ctx = c.getContext('2d');
        if (!ctx) return null;
        const data = ctx.getImageData(0, 0, c.width, c.height);
        const bytes = encodeGif([{ data, delayMs: 0 }], c.width, c.height);
        return new Blob([bytes as BlobPart], { type: 'image/gif' });
      }
      default: return toBlob(c, 'image/png');
    }
  }

  private async refresh(token: number): Promise<void> {
    const flat = flatCanvas(this.engine);
    if (!flat || flat.width < 1 || flat.height < 1) return;
    const blob = await this.encode(flat);
    if (token !== this.token || !blob) return;
    const bmp = await createImageBitmap(blob);
    if (token !== this.token) { bmp.close(); return; }
    this.drawBox(this.opt, bmp);
    bmp.close();
    setText(this.optCap, `${LABEL[this.fmt]} · ${size(blob.size)}`);
    const png = await toBlob(flat, 'image/png');
    if (token !== this.token) return;
    setText(this.origCap, `Original · ${png ? size(png.size) : ''}`);
    setText(this.status, 'Encoded preview at 100 percent, centre of the image.');
  }
```

            n++;
            sa0 += px[a]; sa1 += px[a + 1]; sa2 += px[a + 2]; sb0 += px[b]; sb1 += px[b + 1]; sb2 += px[b + 2];
            qa0 += px[a] * px[a]; qa1 += px[a + 1] * px[a + 1]; qa2 += px[a + 2] * px[a + 2]; qb0 += px[b] * px[b]; qb1 += px[b + 1] * px[b + 1]; qb2 += px[b + 2] * px[b + 2];

          for (let c = 0; c < 3; c++) {

Removed `hidden`, `applyHidden`, `setHiddenGroups`, the `formvis.railHidden` storage (the old group-level hide is not migrated) and the `EditToolbar` class, which was:
```ts
class EditToolbar extends Dialog {
  private readonly list = el('<div class="cv-edit-toolbar"></div>');
  private onChange: ((keys: Set<string>) => void) | null = null;
  constructor() {
    super('Edit Toolbar', 420);
    this.body.append(el('<p class="cv-note">Tools you hide stay one click away in the toolbar\'s ••• list.</p>'), this.list);
    this.button('Done', 'primary', () => this.close());
  }
  show(groups: ToolGroup[], hidden: Set<string>, onChange: (keys: Set<string>) => void): void {
    this.onChange = onChange;
    this.list.textContent = '';
    const now = new Set(hidden);
    for (const g of groups) {
      const r = el(`<label class="cv-edit-tool"><input type="checkbox"><span class="cv-edit-tool-name"></span><span class="cv-flyout-key"></span></label>`);
      const box = r.querySelector('input') as HTMLInputElement;
      box.checked = !now.has(g.key);
      setText(r.querySelector('.cv-edit-tool-name') as HTMLElement, g.tools.map((t) => t.label).join(', '));
      setText(r.querySelector('.cv-flyout-key') as HTMLElement, g.key);
      box.addEventListener('change', () => { if (box.checked) now.delete(g.key); else now.add(g.key); this.onChange?.(new Set(now)); });
      this.list.appendChild(r);
    }
    this.open();
  }
}
```
- ui/panels/toolbar-dialog.ts (new): `ToolbarDialog`, `openToolbarDialog(engine)`. Two columns (groups, Extra Tools), rows dragged in place, a drop zone for a new group, Restore Defaults, Clear Tools, Cancel, Done (saves null when the layout equals the built-in one).
- styles/shell.css: `.cv-tb-*` rules.
- app.ts: command `customize-toolbar` ("Toolbar...") in the Edit menu before `shortcuts`; import. automation/command-meta.ts: its words.

The owner asked for the whole app in 26 languages with English the default. Built and checked: tsc clean; unit 194 of 194.

The page translator (`startPageTranslator`, `walk`, `translateText`, `translateAttrs`): a MutationObserver translating, by exact match, text nodes and title, aria-label and placeholder attributes that do not go through `t`, keeping the English per node for later changes; it never touches inputs, text areas, editable text, the canvas, `[data-no-i18n]` or the person's own names (layer, document, comp, path, style, recent file and timeline names). Its callbacks run before paint, so no English flashes. In English it does nothing.
- ui/i18n/{fr,de,nl,da,fi,nb,sv,pt-BR,ru,pl,cs,hu,uk,tr,zh-TW,ja,id,th,vi}.ts (new, three Sonnet builders): each with all 670 keys of the existing tables, checked key for key against the master list (none missing, none extra, no em dash). ui/i18n/es-MX.ts and fr-CA.ts (new): only the words those variants say differently.

## Outline tracing, Create Work Path and Convert to Shape from type, DEV_PLAN 32.7 part b · _v1.70.3 (engine/trace-outline.ts, engine/index.ts, app.ts, automation/command-meta.ts)

The outlines are traced from the rendered pixels, not read from the font: `traceAlpha` thresholds a layer's alpha, chains the boundary into closed loops (outer contours clockwise, holes counter-clockwise), places points at the sub-pixel threshold crossing, simplifies with Ramer-Douglas-Peucker and fits Catmull-Rom handles, keeping sharp corners sharp. Layer > Type > Create Work Path puts the result in the Work Path, and Convert to Shape adds a shape layer in the text colour and hides the type layer, as one undo step. Rotation of the type layer is not applied yet.

## Extruded 3D type and shapes, DEV_PLAN 32.9 · _v1.70.3 (ui/panels/extrude3d-dialog.ts, engine/types.ts, app.ts, automation/command-meta.ts)

Layer > 3D > New 3D Extrusion from Selected Layer pushes a shape, type or pixel layer into depth. A shape layer's path is used directly; a type or pixel layer has its alpha traced to a path. Closed subpaths become three.js shapes, and a subpath wound against the largest one and lying inside another becomes that shape's hole. The dialog previews live with depth, bevel, turn, tilt, size, light and material sliders and a colour, and Place renders at the document's size into a layer named 3D: plus the source name. The layer keeps its settings in `extrude3d`, so running the command on it again re-opens the dialog and re-renders its pixels in place as one undo step.

## Release 1.70.2: Trap, Pixel Aspect Ratio, Modifier Keys · _v1.70.2 (engine/trap.ts, app.ts)

Joined and checked: tsc clean; unit 194 of 194; the window opened and `agents sync` run (915 catalogue ids). No builder added a type cast.

Fixes at the join:
- **Trap read the ink at the wrong stride.** `trapInk` assumed 4 floats per pixel, but `ChannelPixels` keeps C, M, Y, K and alpha (n + 1 = 5), as `channelGrey` and the other ink readers do. The first run altered 512 values across the whole layer. The stride is now read from the data's length.
- **Conditional Mode Change skipped plain RGB documents.** On the CMYK, Bitmap and Indexed route, `conditionalMode` tested `doc.mode !== 'rgb'`. A document never converted has no mode, so it tried `convertMode('rgb')`, which refused, and the whole change silently did nothing. The test now reads an absent mode as RGB, here and on the Lab route. The 1.69.2 probe had only reached this route from Bitmap.

Probes in Chromium:
- **Trap:** a 40 by 10 document, red on the left and yellow on the right, converted to CMYK and trapped at 2 px. It changed exactly 40 values: the two yellow columns next to the red took magenta 0.97 and yellow 0.98 from the red side. The red side stayed as it was, and K stayed 0.
- **Modifier Keys:** one tap of Shift held for one gesture and cleared at its end. A latched Alt survived a gesture and cleared on the next tap.
- **Pixel Aspect Ratio:** Anamorphic 2:1 set an aspect of 2, which survived a save and read. With correction on, the status bar read "PAR 2, corrected in the Navigator", and the Navigator drew the document's circle as a 2:1 ellipse.
- No page errors.

Removed lines taken after the version edit. Removed from frontend:

## Modifier Keys panel, DEV_PLAN 35.3 part c · _v1.70.2 (ui/modifier-keys.ts, ui/stage.ts, ui/dock.ts, app.ts, automation/command-meta.ts, styles/panels.css)

Window > Modifier Keys is a small docked panel (hidden by default) with Shift, Alt (Option) and Ctrl (Cmd) buttons, so pen and touch users can hold a modifier for a canvas gesture. The new `ui/modifier-keys.ts` holds the shared sticky state (`stickyModifiers`, with a tiny subscribe API) and `ModifierKeysPanel`, which builds its three buttons once and only flips aria-pressed and the `is-latched` class. One tap holds a modifier for the next gesture; a double tap within 350 ms latches it until tapped again. `Stage.pointer` ORs the sticky flags into shift, alt and mod, and the stage's pointerup handler calls `stickyModifiers.endGesture()` to release the one-shot flags. Keyboard shortcuts and wheel zoom are unchanged. The panel has a dock entry and a hidden default, an app.ts construction, and a `panel-modifier-keys` command row.

## Trap, DEV_PLAN 31.5 · _v1.70.2 (engine/trap.ts, engine/index.ts, ui/panels/trap-dialog.ts, app.ts, automation/command-meta.ts)
Image > Trap for CMYK documents. `trapInk` in engine/trap.ts is a pure two-pass separable filter over interleaved CMYK floats: each pixel's C, M and Y rise to the value of the darkest (most total ink) neighbour within the radius, only when that neighbour is darker than the pixel; K never spreads. `Engine.trap(widthPx)` refuses non-CMYK documents and documents with more than one pixel layer with a notice, otherwise writes a new ink record and redraws the layer rendition through the document table as one 'Trap' undo step. TrapDialog takes a Width (1 to 10) and a unit (Pixels, Points, mm) converted by the document resolution; the `trap` command runs straight from `width` and `unit` params and shows the dialog otherwise.

## Pixel Aspect Ratio, DEV_PLAN 35.4 part b · _v1.70.2 (engine/types.ts, engine/index.ts, io/project-io.ts, io/psd.ts, app.ts, automation/command-meta.ts, ui/navigator.ts, ui/status.ts)

A document now carries an optional `pixelAspect` (width over height of one pixel, absent when square), set by Image > Pixel Aspect Ratio (square, D1/DV NTSC 0.91, PAL 1.09, the two widescreen ratios, Anamorphic 2:1, HDV 1.33 and a custom value) as one undo step through `engine.setPixelAspect`, saved in the project manifest and read and written as the PSD pixel aspect ratio resource. View > Pixel Aspect Ratio Correction (`engine.view.parCorrection`) is honest about its reach: the main canvas is not stretched yet, because about twenty files read the viewport's zoom for their coordinate mapping. The correction shows only in the Navigator, whose preview and red view rectangle are widened by the ratio, and a status bar note reads, for example, "PAR 0.91, corrected in the Navigator". Exports stay square-pixel and offer nothing new.

On read, the document's layerComps list becomes formvis comps with fresh ids (captured-info bits 1, 2 and 4 map to visibility, position and appearance), each layer's comps settings fill the comp's per-layer entries with visibility and, for position comps, x and y as the layer's own position plus the stored offset, and lastApplied sets the active comp. The maths moved into a shared `calcCore`, and a pure `calculationsPreview` returns the grey as RGBA ImageData scaled to at most 220 px, which the dialog paints into a fixed 220 px canvas 150 ms after any change without touching the document. Affinity files (.af, .afphoto, .afdesign, .afpub) now open as their embedded preview, one layer. ## Paint.NET .pdn read, DEV_PLAN 34.5 part b · _v1.69.8 (io/pdn.ts, io/images.ts, app.ts)
`io/pdn.ts` opens Paint.NET 3.x and 4.x files with their layers, in TypeScript. `readPdn` checks the PDN3 magic, reads the XML header (size, thumbnail), then walks the .NET BinaryFormatter stream with a small record reader (class, array, string, reference and null records) to collect each BitmapLayer's name, visibility, opacity byte, blend op and surface size. After MessageEnd it reads each MemoryBlock's pixels (raw, or gzip chunks placed by chunk number through `DecompressionStream`) in serialized order, skipping blocks that match no layer, and converts BGRA to RGBA, bottom layer first. Reflect, Glow, Negation and Xor open as Normal with a note. Anything unreadable, including gzip-wrapped streams, falls back to the header thumbnail as one layer with a note. `isPdnFile` is wired into `openFiles` beside Krita and `.pdn` joins `PROJECT_ACCEPT`.

`readKra` in `io/kra.ts` opens a Krita file as a layered document: it unzips the file, parses maindoc.xml, and walks the layer tree recursively (Krita lists the top first, so the walk is reversed to formvis's bottom-first order). Paint layers decode Krita's 64 by 64 tiles (LZF or raw, planar B, G, R, A) into a raster placed at the layer's x and y; group layers become formvis groups; opacity is the attribute over 255, visibility comes from `visible`, and `compositeop` maps to a formvis blend mode (unknown ones open as Normal, with a note). Filter, adjustment, clone, vector and file layers are left out with a note naming them. A file that is not 8-bit RGBA, or holds no usable paint layers, opens as its mergedimage.png in one layer, with a note. `.kra` joined PROJECT_ACCEPT in `io/images.ts`, and `openFiles` in app.ts routes it beside OpenRaster and PSD. Paint.NET .pdn is deferred.
