## Split Warp, DEV_PLAN 32.3 · _v1.69.4 (engine/mesh-warp.ts, engine/index.ts, app.ts, automation/command-meta.ts)

The mesh Warp grid can now grow and shrink while it is pending. Split Warp Horizontally adds a row, Vertically a column and Crosswise both, at the middle of the largest cell; Remove Warp Split drops the row or column added last (or the last interior line), never the border lines. `meshWarpImage` takes optional `us` and `vs`, the source positions of the grid columns and rows, and maps grid parameters to the source by piecewise-linear interpolation, so an inserted line no longer assumes an evenly divided source. `splitGrid` places each new point on the current surface (`meshSurfacePoint`) at the matching interpolated source position, which leaves every existing point of the picture where it was; between control points the Catmull-Rom surface is refit through the denser grid, so a bent mesh can shift very slightly there while a still-linear grid is exact. A split that would fold a cell is refused with a notice. The move tool's overlay and point picking read `gw` and `gh` and already draw the lines along the surface, so they follow with no change.

Image > Mode > Multichannel (`mode-multichannel`): the document becomes grey spot channels with ink colours, shown overprinted on white. From RGB: Cyan, Magenta, Yellow as 255 minus R, G, B ink (black is full ink); from CMYK: Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black; from Grayscale: one Black channel; from Duotone: the duotone's inks through their curves. `engine/multichannel.ts` holds the split and the composite (start at white, multiply each RGB channel by 1 - amount * (1 - ink / 255), amount = (255 - grey) / 255 times solidity). `Engine.compose` and `flattened` draw the composite for a multichannel document, so the canvas, the Navigator and export follow; the Stage keeps such documents on the CPU. Image > Mode > RGB Color bakes the composite into one pixel layer. Saved as `multichannel` in the manifest with one PNG per channel. The Channels panel does not list the channels yet.

## Auto-Align and Auto-Blend Layers (DEV_PLAN 32.1) · _v1.68.3 (src/ui/panels/align-blend-dialog.ts, src/engine/index.ts, src/engine/layer-masks.ts, src/io/api.ts, src/app.ts, src/automation/command-meta.ts, docs/MANUAL.md)

Commands `auto-align-layers` (param projection) and `auto-blend-layers` (params method, seamless), enabled with two or more selected plain pixel layers; no params opens `AlignBlendDialog`. `AlignBlendDialog.execute` renders each layer alone (`renderLayerAlone`, bottom-most of `doc.layers` first, assumed to be index 0) as a document-size PNG and posts to `api.mergeAlign` / `api.mergeBlend`. `engine.applyLayerEdits` then does every layer in one `edit` step: align draws the layer through the returned matrix (inverse map, premultiplied bilinear) onto a document-size raster with `docTransform`; blend sets `LM.maskFromImage` masks (document-size, so a layer whose box is not the document gets a mask that is not in its own space) and multiplies pixels by the Seamless Tones gains. Layers with text, shapes, smart objects or adjustments are skipped. Cylindrical runs as Perspective and Vignette Removal is not applied; both said in the dialog. Not exercised in a browser, only type-checked.

## Export Artboards to PDF (DEV_PLAN 29.4) · _v1.68.3 (src/ui/panels/artboard-pdf-dialog.ts, src/app.ts, src/io/api.ts, src/engine/index.ts, src/automation/command-meta.ts)

Command `export-artboards-pdf` (params name, jpeg, quality, icc, contents_only; no params opens `ArtboardPdfDialog`) renders each artboard with `engine.artboardImage(id, bare)` in the order of `engine.artboards` (top of the Layers panel first, checked) and sends the PNGs to `api.pdfPages`, which posts to the engine's `/io/pdf-pages`. `artboardImage` gained `bare`, which drops the artboard's own background colour (Contents Only). Page size comes from `doc.resolution` (72 default). Lossless is the engine's choice of reversible JPEG 2000, since Pillow's PDF writer has no Flate for RGB. The ICC profile is sent and validated but not embedded in the PDF; the dialog row is shown disabled. Artboard names as page labels are not written.

## Edit > Purge and Layer > Smart Filter, DEV_PLAN 32.5 and 33.2 (part) · _v1.68.0 (engine/history.ts, engine/index.ts, app.ts, automation/command-meta.ts)

Edit > Purge (Clipboard, Histories, All), as Photoshop's. `History.clear()` empties the done and undone steps and hands each to `History.onDrop`, so the pixels a step keeps in the engine's undo store go too; it does nothing while a step is open. `Engine.purgeHistories(all)` clears the current document or every open one, empties the queued undo and redo ops and emits `history`; the current state and the History panel's snapshots (kept on the project, not in `History`) are untouched, and the revision is not changed, so the saved mark stays true. `Engine.purgeClipboard()` sets `engine.clipboard` to null (the system clipboard and the layer-style clipboard are not touched). Histories and All ask first through `confirmAction` (danger style) that it cannot be undone. Commands `purge-clipboard`, `purge-histories`, `purge-all`, each disabled when it has nothing to clear.

Layer > Smart Filter submenu. `Engine.toggleSmartFilters()` sets every filter of the active smart object to the opposite of "all are off" in one `setSmartFilters` step (named Disable Smart Filters or Enable Smart Filters), the command label following `Engine.smartFiltersOff`; `clearSmartFilters()` sets an empty stack, one step named Clear Smart Filters. Commands `smart-filters-disable`, `smart-filters-clear`, enabled only when the layer has filters. The dialog and `smart-filters` are as they were. No layout change: the entries are new menu rows.

## Workspace charter: optional Home, nothing over the canvas, settings that stick, Help > What's New, DEV_PLAN 35.1 · _v1.67.9 (ui/prefs.ts, ui/home.ts, ui/option-memory.ts new, ui/dialogs.ts, ui/toast.ts, ui/app-dialogs.ts, ui/panels/whats-new.ts new, ui/panels/whats-new-data.ts new, ui/panels/filter-panel.ts, ui/panels/background-panel.ts, ui/panels/brush-settings.ts, ui/panels/export-dialog.ts, about forty dialogs under ui/panels/ that call `remember()`, styles/panels.css, styles/dialogs.css, app.ts, automation/command-meta.ts, docs/MANUAL.md)

Home screen. `Prefs.autoShowHome` (existing, now labelled "Show Home screen at launch", default on) gates the launch path; the new `Prefs.homeOnLastClose` (default off) gates the path taken when a session that had a document closes its last one. `Home` keeps a `hadDocument` flag and decides `on = forced || (n === 0 && (hadDocument ? deps.afterClose() : deps.autoShow()))`, so the old behaviour of Home returning after the last close is now the opt-in, and closing the last document leaves the empty workspace with its panels as they were. Both are commands (`pref-home-launch`, `pref-home-last-close`) that call `home.sync()`, and rows in Preferences > General.

Audit of what appears over the canvas uninvited. Method: with a browser open, every element positioned absolute or fixed whose box meets `.cv-stage`, outside the modal scrims, with no document, with one, and with the Crop, Type, Move and Brush tools. Found: the two canvases (scene and overlay), the empty-state `.cv-welcome` (only while no document is open, and it is the canvas's own empty state), the dock's resize grips (edge handles, not over the picture), and the toast stack. Everything else that opens (menus, flyouts, the panel flyouts `cv-props-fly`, the assistant, the Agent and Connect panels, the dialogs) opens only when asked for and docks to an edge or to the control that opened it. So one thing floated over the picture on its own: the toasts, in the bottom right of the window, which cover the document at that corner whenever it is zoomed to fit. Decision: they stay, as corner toasts that fade are allowed, but now never cover the document under the pointer. `.cv-toast` is `pointer-events: none` (it was `auto`, so a toast swallowed clicks and strokes at the corner), and `toast.ts` watches `pointermove` once (passive, one rAF per frame): when the pointer is over `.cv-stage` and within 24 px of a toast's box, the toast gets `.is-away` (opacity 0, a 120 ms fade; nothing moves, so no layout shift), and shows again when the pointer leaves. No new preference: nothing else needed one. The Crop, Type and Brush overlays are drawn on the overlay canvas in answer to the tool in use and are invited.

Settings stick, in the one existing mechanism (`formvis.prefs`, `Prefs`), not a second. `loadPrefs` rebuilds the object from known keys only, so the new fields `toolOptions`, `dialogValues`, `whatsNewAuto`, `whatsNewSeen`, `homeOnLastClose` are cleaned there (`cleanToolOptions`, `cleanDialogValues`; strings at most 2000 characters), and `updatePrefs(patch)` is the one writer; the Preferences dialog's `change()` carries them through when it saves. Reset All Preferences clears every `formvis.*` key, so it clears these too.
- Tools (`ui/option-memory.ts`, `installOptionMemory(engine)`, installed before the options bar is built): wraps every registered tool's `options(engine)`, so a change made by the options bar, the command catalogue (`tool.options.<tool>.<option>`), an agent or a key is kept under `tool.option`, and puts the kept values back at start (oldest change first, so where tools share a setting such as the brush size the latest change wins). A value equal to the tool's own default is not kept, so a default that changes later still reaches everyone who never moved it. `NEVER` lists what describes the document or the gesture: Move's X, Y, W, H, Scale, Angle, Sampling and Perspective Warp, all of Rotate View, Crop's Straighten and Perspective, Clone Stamp's Source, Type's Color. A sweep of all 48 tools (change every option, reload, compare) found no option lost other than those.
- Dialogs: `Dialog.remember(skip, extra)` keeps every slider, number, check box, colour and select in the body (not text fields) under the dialog's title and the control's label, restores them when the app has built (a microtask after the constructor, so handlers find everything defined) and again on each `open()`, by firing the controls' own `input` and `change` events so the dialog's state follows; a disabled option is never selected on restore. `skip` names controls that show the document (sizes, positions); `extra` carries a value no form control holds (Canvas Size's anchor, Liquify's tool). Opted in: Canvas Size, Image Size, Fit Image, Amount, Load Selection, Fill, Stroke, Stroke Path, Fade, Trim, Replace Color, Color Range, Color Match, Content-Aware Scale, Content-Aware Fill, Focus Area, HDR Toning, Wide Angle, Vanishing Point, Liquify, Select and Mask, Matting, Scale Effects, New Layer, Export GIF, Render Video, Video, Large Picture, Save a Copy, Export Layers to Files, Generate Image, Generative Fill, Neural Filters, Assign and Convert Profile, Tween, Film Layers, Photomerge and Merge to HDR, Guides (orientation only), TIFF Pages and Batch (format and quality; the action is chosen from the list). Stroke's colour starts at the foreground colour by design and is not kept. New Document (explicit `recall`/`keepValues`: size, unit, resolution, mode, background, artboards, link and category, not the name), Export As (`recalled`/`remembered` for its settings object and preset), Remove Background (`BackgroundPanel`, the quality, refine, contrast and shift settings as one JSON value), the Filter panel (per filter, only the settings that differ from `defaultFilterSettings()`, written at OK and read in `show`, skipped past 1900 characters) and Brush Settings (the whole `engine.brushShape`, read when the dialog is built so the first stroke uses it) use `recalled`/`remembered` directly. Select Subject and Mask All Objects have no processing choice of their own (the Select Subject button runs the model, and Mask All Objects takes the layer); the choices that govern them are Remove Background's settings above, and the engine device, which is already a preference. Left as they were: dialogs that edit an existing object and so show its values (Warp Text, Corner Radii, Layer Style, Type, Paragraph Styles, Artboard, Note, Smart Filters, Fill Layer), and the JPEG sheet, which already kept its quality in `formvis.jpegQuality`.

Help > What's New (`ui/panels/whats-new-data.ts`, `whats-new.ts`). A data table of releases, newest first, each with additions of a title, a sentence and a command id: 1.67.9 (File Info, QOI/PNM/TGA/ICO, this workspace work) and 1.67.8 (the Clarity, Dehaze, Texture and Light adjustment layers, File > Scripts, Export Layers to Files, Export Artboards to Files). The dialog builds every row once; Show Me closes the dialog first and then runs the command through the command catalogue; a command that cannot run now (it needs a document) has its button disabled with the reason as its title, patched in place on `show`. It opens once after an update (`Prefs.whatsNewAuto`, default on; `whatsNewSeen` holds the last version shown), after the crash-recovery offer in the final frame of `startApp`, and not on a fresh profile, not under `navigator.webdriver`, and not while another dialog is open. Commands added: `whats-new`, `pref-home-launch`, `pref-home-last-close`, `pref-whats-new-auto`, each with words in `command-meta.ts`.

Checked: tsc clean; vitest 194 passed; `counts --check` and `counts --commands --check` pass. In a browser: both Home prefs in both states across reloads; closing the last document with the pref off and on; layout shift 0 after the last close and when What's New opens; What's New lists 10 rows and each Show Me closes it first and runs its command (Export Artboards to Files is disabled with no artboard); tool options across a reload for all tools; Canvas Size, Fill, Stroke, New Layer, New Document, Gaussian Blur and Brush Settings values across a reload. The nearest e2e files (home screen, preferences, menus, no scrollbars, shortcut editor, panel menus, GPU prefs, New Document, crop size, edit toolbar, export, fill, filters, options) pass except what is named here. Not mine: `test_layer_dialogs` Ctrl+J (Mod+J is bound to Terminal and to Layer via Copy; Terminal wins), `test_every_colour_mode_offered_changes_the_mode` (Lab mode added elsewhere), and the 422 and 500 responses in `test_offered_options` from the engine. `test_new_document` timed out once under load and passed alone.

## File > File Info, DEV_PLAN 29.2 · _v1.67.9 (engine/doc-meta.ts new, engine/types.ts, engine/index.ts, io/xmp.ts new, io/exif.ts new, io/embed-icc.ts, io/ai-label.ts, io/images.ts, io/project-io.ts, io/psd.ts, ui/panels/file-info-dialog.ts new, ui/tabs.ts, styles/dialogs.css, app.ts, automation/command-meta.ts, docs/MANUAL.md)

Photoshop's metadata dialog. `Doc.meta` (`DocMeta`, in `doc-meta.ts`, pure rules with no DOM) holds Document Title, Author, Author Title, Description, Rating (1 to 5; 0 is stored as none), Description Writer, Keywords, Copyright Status (`unknown` is stored as none, `copyrighted`, `public`), Copyright Notice, Copyright Info URL, the read-only `camera` record and the `created` and `modified` stamps. `cleanMeta` bounds every value read from a project, an XMP packet or an agent (text lengths in `META_TEXT`, at most 100 keywords of 64 characters, repeats in any case dropped); `mergeMeta` applies a patch and returns the same object when no editable field changes, so `Engine.setMeta` records one History step called File Info only when OK changed something (the camera and the created date are never set from there; `modified` is stamped when something changed). Keywords split on commas, semicolons and line breaks.

Project: `serialize` writes a top-level `meta` object (keywords as a list, camera as an object) only when the document has one, and `deserialize` reads it through `cleanMeta`; an older project has no `meta` and opens as before. The engine's project validator passes unknown top-level fields, so `project_format.py` is unchanged.

XMP (`io/xmp.ts`): `buildXmp` writes one packet with dc:title, dc:creator (Seq), dc:description, dc:subject (Bag), dc:rights (lang alts), xmp:Rating, xmp:CreateDate and ModifyDate, xmpRights:Marked (True for Copyrighted, False for Public Domain, absent for Unknown) and WebStatement, photoshop:AuthorsPosition and CaptionWriter, the camera as tiff:Make, tiff:Model, aux:Lens, exif:ExposureTime, FNumber, ISOSpeedRatings, FocalLength and DateTimeOriginal, and xmp:CreatorTool. `withXmp(blob, format, meta, now, ai)` post-processes the encoded file whichever side made it (the page for PNG and JPEG, the engine for TIFF, and for WebP when tagged), so no engine change was needed and no dependency was added: PNG gets an iTXt chunk `XML:com.adobe.xmp` after IHDR (an earlier one dropped); JPEG an APP1 segment with the `http://ns.adobe.com/xap/1.0/` header after the JFIF and Exif segments (refused with a message past the 64 KB a segment holds); WebP an `XMP ` chunk after the image, a plain file first given its VP8X header with the XMP flag; TIFF tag 700 (BYTE) added to the first directory, the packet and the rewritten directory appended and the header pointed at it (classic TIFF only, as the engine writes; BigTIFF is left as it is); PSD image resource 1060 through ag-psd's `imageResources.xmpMetadata`. A document with nothing to write (no field filled in, no camera record) exports exactly as before. The AI label (`ai-label.ts`, which now exports `SOURCE`) goes inside the same packet as Iptc4xmpExt:DigitalSourceType when File Info is written, so a file never holds two XMP packets; with no File Info the label is written alone as before. `crc32` in `embed-icc.ts` is exported for the PNG chunk. Wired into Export As (`exportAs`), the quick exports (`exportImage`, also the 16 and 32-bit TIFF and PNG from the engine) and PSD and PSB (`writePsdFile`, so Layers to Files PSDs carry it too). Not written: AVIF, PDF, GIF, the CMYK and Lab exports, the banded PNG of a very large picture and the per-layer PNG, JPEG, TIFF and WebP of Layers to Files.

Reading: `readFileMeta(file)` (called from `decodeImage`, so a placed or opened picture, the colour-profile paths and batch all get it; the first picture opened into an empty window gives its File Info to the new document, `insertImages` and `openImage`) finds the packet in a PNG (iTXt), JPEG (APP1), WebP (`XMP `) or TIFF (tag 700) and parses it with the browser's DOMParser, taking elements or attributes as other programs write them and the x-default of a language alternative; the camera comes from the XMP when it has one, else from the Exif block (`io/exif.ts`: JPEG APP1, PNG eXIf, WebP EXIF, the TIFF's own directories; Make, Model, LensModel, ExposureTime, FNumber, ISO, FocalLength, DateTimeOriginal). A PSD reads its 1060 resource in `readPsdFile`. A 16 or 32-bit picture opened through the deep path, a Lab or CMYK file, a HEIC and a camera RAW take no File Info or camera data (the engine, not the page, decodes them).

Dialog (`file-info-dialog.ts`, `FileInfoDialog`, 580 px): every row is built once in the constructor, including the eight Camera Data readouts and the Created and Modified rows (empty readouts and a "no camera data" note in the section heading where there is none), so the dialog is one size from its first frame whatever the document holds, and the values are written before it opens; measured at 12 frames (see the verification). Rating is a select of None and 1 to 5 stars (the icon set has no star). Created and Modified read "Not recorded yet" until the document has File Info or came from a file that recorded them. The tab shows the copyright symbol (U+00A9) before the name through `tabName` when the status is Copyrighted; the tab is a fixed 168 px, so nothing shifts.

Command: `file-info` (File menu after Scripts, Alt+Shift+Mod+I as Photoshop's) with parameters title, author, author_title, description, rating (0 to 5), description_writer, keywords, copyright_status (unknown, copyrighted, public_domain), copyright_notice and copyright_url; given any, it sets those fields at once as one step with no dialog and returns the stored values; the catalogue's validator skips an empty string, so a single space clears a field (said in each description). Words in `command-meta.ts`. Removed code: none.

## QOI, Netpbm, TGA and ICO in File > Import and Export As, DEV_PLAN 34.1 · _v1.67.9 (io/images.ts, io/export-presets.ts, io/api.ts, io/pnm.ts new, io/links.ts, ui/panels/export-dialog.ts, ui/panels/tiff-pages.ts, app.ts, styles/dialogs.css)

The split follows DPX and TIFF: the engine reads and writes the four formats (`backend/app/services/qoi.py`, `pnm.py`, `tga.py`, `ico.py`), the page only routes. Opening: `.qoi .tga .icb .vda .vst .ico .pbm .pgm .ppm .pnm .pam` join `SERVER` in `images.ts`, so `decodeImage` sends them to `/io/decode` and drag and drop, Import Images, Place and the agent bridge all follow `IMAGE_ACCEPT` and `isImageFile`; `.ico` left `NATIVE` because a browser opens whichever entry it likes, and the engine opens the largest. A PGM, PPM or PAM above 8 bits opens as a 16-bit document through the existing `decodeDeep` path (the regex in `importFiles` that already sent 16-bit PNG, TIFF, HDR, EXR and DPX there gained the Netpbm extensions); at 8 bits the route answers depth 8 and the file opens the ordinary way. An ICO with more than one image is offered through `TiffPagesDialog` (retitled Icon Sizes, its three choices worded for sizes), which already lists pages from `/io/pages`; the engine lists icon images largest first so page 0 is the largest and the dialog's "largest only" and a plain decode agree.

Export As: `ExportFormat` gains `qoi`, `pnm`, `tga`, `ico`; `ExportSettings` gains `option` (one choice a format, `FORMAT_OPTIONS`: QOI colourspace flag, PNM kind, TGA 24 or 32 bits with or without run-length, ICO entries as PNG for 256 and BMP below or PNG for all) and `icoSizes` (the seven sizes of `ICO_SIZES`, `DEFAULT_ICO_SIZES` 16, 32, 48, 256 when none is ticked). `clampSettings` keeps `option` only for a format that has the list and falls back to its first choice, so changing format never leaves a stale value; presets and the remembered settings carry both. The dialog gets two rows that exist from the start (the Format options select, its choices patched in place by `sync`, and the size checkboxes in a wrapping `.cv-size-checks` row), both disabled and dimmed for other formats; the dialog's height is the same for every format. `formatOptions(s)` builds the JSON `api.encode` now sends as `options`. `exportName` names a PNM file by its kind (`.ppm`, `.pgm`, `.pbm`, `.pam`). A 16 or 32-bit document exported as PNM goes through `io/pnm.ts` (`pnmDeepBlob`, the DPX route: `composeDeep`, sRGB encoding from 32 bits, `/io/encode-pnm`) and keeps 16 bits at the document's own size, said so when a scale was set; QOI, TGA and ICO from a deeper document are written at 8 bits and a notice says so; a profile other than sRGB converts the pixels as for any format and a notice says the format carries none (`PROFILELESS`, which also turns off Embed the profile). No new command, so `command-meta.ts` is unchanged.

Not done: the agents' `export_image` still writes PNG, JPEG and WebP only (its bridge takes a MIME type); Layers to Files has no QOI, TGA, PNM or ICO.

Verified: tsc clean; unit 194 of 194 (the manual's own search test caught a first wording of the new MANUAL paragraph, which outranked Getting started for "open a very large picture", and it was reworded); Chromium against the dev server and engine: one file of each of QOI, TGA (RLE, 24 and 32 bit), PAM, PPM, PGM, PBM and an ICO opened through the Import Images input with exact pixels, a 16-bit PGM opened as a 16-bit document and exported as PGM and PPM at 16 bits matching exactly, an ICO of four sizes asked and opened the 64 by 64 (and each size as a document), and QOI (both flags), TGA (four options), PNM (four kinds) and ICO (three size sets, mixed and PNG) exported and decoded by Pillow or the reference decoders; `test_export_formats`, `test_export_as`, `test_export_size_label`, `test_tiff_pages`, `test_large_picture` and `test_openraster` pass. ## File > Scripts and Layers to Files, DEV_PLAN 30.1 and 29.1 · _v1.67.8 (engine/file-scripts.ts new, engine/index.ts, io/layer-export.ts new, ui/panels/layer-export-dialog.ts new, app.ts, automation/command-meta.ts, io/api.ts)

Scripts: `file-scripts.ts` holds pure planners over a `Doc` (`emptyLayerIds`, `bakeEffects`, `bakeMasks`); `Engine.deleteEmptyLayers`, `flattenAllEffects` and `flattenAllMasks` apply them in one `edit` each, named after the command, and report counts through `notice`. Delete All Empty Layers: a pixel layer with no raster or a fully transparent one goes, then every group left childless (repeated until stable); the Background, adjustment, fill, type, shape, smart and tiled layers, artboards and frames stay; layers clipped to a deleted base are unclipped. Flatten All Layer Effects: each styled layer is drawn alone through `renderDoc` at the document's size (its mask, clip, group, opacity and blend left out so the mask and opacity stay on the layer and are not applied twice; fill kept in the draw, then reset to 1), the effects cleared; a type, shape or fill layer is rasterized as Rasterize Layer does; smart objects and groups are left as they are. Layers to Files: `io/layer-export.ts` draws each layer with `Engine.renderLayerAlone` (effects and mask applied), optionally cut to its visible pixels, and encodes through the Export As paths (browser PNG and JPEG with `embedPng` and `embedJpeg`, engine `api.encode` for TIFF and a tagged WebP, `writePsdFile` for a one-layer PSD). Names are `prefix_NNNN_name`, the number counted from the top of the stack from 0000, characters outside letters, digits, space, dot, dash and underscore made `_`. Artboards use `artboardImage` and the same dialog (`show(true)`). Desktop: the engine writes into a folder under its exports folder (`/api/io/export` takes an optional `folder`); there is no folder picker, as no existing export has one. Browser: one zip. `export-layers` and `export-artboards-files` take parameters; any given runs without the dialog (agents). The older `export-artboards` stays as the instant PNG zip.

## Clarity, Dehaze, Texture and Light adjustment layers, DEV_PLAN 31.1 · _v1.67.8 (engine/adjust-params.ts, docs/MANUAL.md)

Four new `ParamKind`s, each a slice of Develop through `developSlice` in `adjust-params.ts`: a kernel that sets only the named `DevelopState` controls and runs `developImage` at `1 / unitsPerPixel`, so Clarity's 20 px and Texture's 3 px radii are in document units and look the same at any zoom. Dehaze is Develop's per-pixel dehaze (no local estimate), so it needs no radius. Light maps Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites and Blacks straight onto Develop's tone controls; Brightness has no Develop control (Develop's offset lifts every tone), so it is a midtone curve applied first, x + b * x * (1 - x), which keeps black and white fixed. The menus, Edit Adjustment panel, command catalogue (its words come from the `adj-` and `new-adj-` patterns), `.fmv` (labels), agent bridge and compositing all walk `PARAM_KINDS`, so nothing else names the kinds. PSD export leaves them out with a note, as it does Develop (no Photoshop key invented); 16-bit, CMYK and Lab take the generic kernel path Develop takes.

## Brush strokes on a deep buffer: flow by spacing, opacity per dab, pressure for size and opacity, DEV_PLAN 28.1 · _v1.67.6 (engine/dab-buffer.ts new, stroke.ts, brush-dynamics.ts, deep.ts, index.ts; extensions/tools/brush.ts)

Photoshop's model. `PixelStroke` lays each dab into a `StrokeBuffer` (`dab-buffer.ts`): coverage as a `Float32Array` over the stroke's window, and, only when the Opacity control follows pressure or Fade, a `Uint8Array` of the highest opacity any dab reached at each pixel. The tip's alpha is read once per stroke (`TipAlpha`, with a halving chain so a small dab samples a level near its size) and each dab is rasterised by inverse mapping, a separable fast path when the placement has no rotation. `compose()` draws the 8-bit paint surface from the buffer over the rectangle it updates, through a small scratch canvas (`putImageData` straight into a 4000 by 3000 canvas cost 28 ms a call, the scratch draw 0.1 ms), and the working copy takes it at full alpha: opacity is no longer a `globalAlpha` on the compose. A pixel shows min(coverage, ceiling); the ceiling is the stroke's Opacity, times the Opacity control, rounded down to a level so 50 percent never shows as 50.2.

Flow: each dab adds `1 - (1 - flow) ^ (spacing / quarter of the diameter)` times the tip's alpha, so a Flow lays the same build-up per quarter diameter of travel at 1, 10 or 25 percent spacing; Flow 100 is 1, which is the old dab exactly. The Airbrush's rest dabs count as a quarter diameter each. Pencil and Block dabs fill whole pixels of coverage 1. Strokes whose dabs differ in colour (Mixer, Color Dynamics) keep an `ink` canvas of the dab colours drawn as before, the buffer supplying alpha only. `ensure`, `toFull` and `release` carry the buffer and the ink with the window; a windowed stroke across 4,100 by 3,910 equals the same stroke on a layer under the window threshold, byte for byte, for plain, opacity-by-pressure, Fade and Color Dynamics strokes.

Dynamics: `BrushDynamics` gains `opacity`; the sensor `fade` (steps per spec, `fadeOption(steps, min, max)`) counts dabs, full at the first, the option's minimum after `steps`; PaintInfo carries `fade`. Built-in presets keep their size and flow dynamics, with Opacity off. Pen pressure is eased over a tenth of the diameter of travel (`smooth`), so a pen's first and last readings move the line gradually and a path's sparse samples pass as they are (a three-sample average had lagged Stroke Path's simulated taper). The engine starts with size following pressure (`pressureOption(0.1)`; 0.2 broke the Stroke Path taper test, whose end must be under 10 px); the Brush options gain `Pressure: opacity`. 16-bit documents: `strokeDeep` takes `cover`, the stroke's laid alpha (`PixelStroke.coverFor`), for plain strokes with the source-over or destination-out operation, in place of estimating coverage from the 8-bit before and after; 32-bit and CMYK still derive from the 8-bit result, which now carries the model.

Measured: Opacity 50, Flow 10, one stroke scrubbed 1, 3 and 9 times peaks at 32.9, 49.8 and 49.8 percent, by engine calls and by real pen events; Flow 20 at 1, 10 and 25 percent spacing and the default: 57.7, 57.8, 57.7, 57.7 (hard), 48.6, 48.6, 48.5, 48.6 (hardness 50); a pressure ramp 0.1 to 1 gives widths 14, 20, 26, 30, 36 px; pressure 0.3 once or nine times in one stroke 43.9 percent, then pressure 1 in the same stroke 100. `test_brush_flow.py` and the rest pass unchanged; its comments still describe the old 8-bit stall.

Removed from stroke.ts, index.ts and deep.ts:

```text
      if (flow < 1) this.paintCtx.globalAlpha = Math.max(0, flow);
      this.paintCtx.drawImage(this.dabTip(x, y), -rx, -ry, rx * 2, ry * 2);
      this.wetMark(mul(place, [1, 0, 0, round, 0, 0]), 0, 0, rx, ry);
      if (flow < 1) this.paintCtx.globalAlpha = 1;
    const ctx = this.paintCtx, col = this.style.color;
    ctx.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, -this.ox, -this.oy);
    ctx.fillStyle = `rgb(${col.r}, ${col.g}, ${col.b})`;
    w.globalAlpha = this.style.opacity;
    c.drawImage(this.paint, this.ox, this.oy);   // the window's paint at its place (1.60.6)
  brushDynamics: BrushDynamics = noDynamics();
    if (!this.room(first * (p.selection ? 3 : 2) + fresh, 'This stroke')) return false;
```

## Hidden scrollbars once, a throttled walk, and the Radial Blur freeze, DEV_PLAN 28.7 (styles/tokens.css, shell.css, panels.css, terminal.css; plugins/host.ts; ui/panels/filter-panel.ts, agent-panel.ts)

Scrollbars: `styles/scrollbars.css` is the one sheet; the copies in `tokens.css`, `shell.css` and `panels.css` are gone (the `overflow` each rule carried stays). Plug-in frames are sandboxed documents with no access to the page's sheets, so `plugins/host.ts` puts the same rules in a `<style>` (`FRAME_STYLE`) at the head of each frame's `srcdoc`.

The throttled walk (Chromium with `--hide-scrollbars` left off, so a drawn bar would measure; the iframe control without the sheet measured 15 px; CPU 4x, 400 ms and 62,500 B/s, cache off; a production build, since the dev server's hundreds of module requests are not what a person waits for): hard reload dark 0, light theme 0.0008 and with the dock and Claude panel left open 0.0030 before the fixes below; theme background `rgb(17, 17, 17)` and `rgb(236, 235, 230)` on the first revealed frame, Inter (400, 500, 600) and JetBrains Mono loaded at the reveal. All ten menus with their submenus, 17 dialogs and the Agent Connect panel 0. No element with a drawn or unhidden scrollbar in any state, with 50 layers in the Layers panel. Found and fixed: the Claude Code panel's log moved when the status line arrived and wrapped, or the install row appeared (the status row reserves two lines, the log is `visibility: hidden` until the first status, `is-loaded`; 0.0040 on open, 0.0011 twice on reload); the status bar's GPU and memory readouts had no width, so the hint beside them moved when they arrived (`min-width` 84 and 140 px). Not fixed, and not flashes: Window > panel toggles move the panels below (Navigator 0.030, Swatches 0.016, Properties 0.028, Brushes 0.036), and the terminal dock opening or closing moves the bottom-anchored colour swatches and the Home card (0.034 and 0.050 with the Home screen up, 0.003 to 0.007 over a document); with a real click or key Chromium flags every one `hadRecentInput`, so each is the re-layout the person asked for, in one frame. Opened by a command with no input before it (as an agent does), the same moves count. A tried `flex: none` on `.cv-tool` was taken out again: the rail's tools are 28 px by a later rule and never shrank.

Radial Blur then Surface Blur froze the window. Cause: `filterMargin` returned a fixed 2000 for Radial Blur, the distance the filter reaches past the layer, so applying it at the default Amount of 10 grew an 800 by 600 layer to 4,800 by 4,600 (22 million pixels, `[-2000, -2000]` offset) and ran the filter on all of it (33 s here); Surface Blur then ran its per-pixel loop on that layer (69 s). Each alone ran; Radial Blur after Surface Blur only grew the already small layer. Fix: `radialMargin(amount, method)` takes the reach from the settings (a spin moves a sample by at most `2 sin(k pi / 12)` of the distance from the centre, a zoom by `(k / 2) / (1 - k / 2)`, for content up to 2,000 px out); the default now grows the layer by 107 px and the pair runs in 4.4 s and 5.5 s. Removed from `ui/panels/filter-panel.ts`:

```text
    : kind === 'radialBlur' ? 2000 : isLibKind(kind) ? libMargin(kind, s.lib?.[kind]) : 0;
```

Removed from the sheets:

```text
* { scrollbar-width: none; }
*::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; width: 0; height: 0; }
.cv-tab-strip::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
.cv-options::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
.cv-rail::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
.cv-rail-tools::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
.cv-menu::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
(and `scrollbar-width: none;` from the .cv-tab-strip, .cv-options, .cv-rail, .cv-rail-tools, .cv-menu rules and the two in the narrow-screen block)
```

## One command catalogue, DEV_PLAN 28.3 (automation/catalogue.ts, automation/command-meta.ts new; ui/commands.ts, app.ts)

Decision: `Command` gains optional `group`, `description`, `when`, `params`, `mutates`, `risky`, and `run` may take a params object; the words for the hand-written and generated commands live in `automation/command-meta.ts` (one row per id, plus family rules for `filter-*`, `adj-*`, `new-adj-*`, `recent-N` and plugin commands) instead of 470 edits to `app.ts`. A command a row or rule does not cover is reported in `catalogueReport().missing`, mirrored to the engine, and `./formvis counts --commands --check` fails on it. A command can still carry its own fields, which win over the table.

`catalogue.ts` builds the list from the live registry: every registered command (not `recent-heading`, a disabled label), `tool.select.<id>` for each tool (words from `TOOL_WHEN`, a tool without a phrase is reported missing), `tool.options.<tool>.<option>` for each settable option of each tool's `options()` (range, number, toggle, segment, select, color; buttons and readouts are not options; the name is the camelCase label, a repeat gets a number), and seven actions that call existing engine paths only: `paint.stroke` (the active painting tool's own down, move and up with pressure), `select.rect`, `select.ellipse`, `select.lasso`, `layer.set`, `adjust.apply` (`dialogs.adjust.applySettings`) and `filter.apply` (`dialogs.filter.applySettings`, the library's `LibParam`s and a table of the core filters' controls). 755 ids in this build. `runCommands` opens one outer `History` step (`begin`/`end` nest by depth), so a list is one undo step; `layer.set` does the same for its properties. Errors say what to do next and lose their final full stop because `agent-bridge.ts`'s `catalogueTool` appends its own sentence.

`Commands` gains `call` (awaits `run`, returns its value) and `onChange` (the catalogue re-mirrors, debounced, to `POST /api/commands/catalogue` after any add or remove, so a plugin's commands appear). `window.formvis` now exists in every build with `catalogue` (the bridge reads it); the engine, commands and the rest stay DEV only.

Found, not fixed: `radialBlur` followed by `surfaceBlur` at default settings freezes the window's main thread, through the older `apply_filter` MCP tool as well as `filter.apply`; each alone, and the pair in the other order, run. Left to the filter-library owner.

## Color Settings, 16-bit Convert to Profile and DPX, DEV_PLAN 28.2 part 1 (ui/colour-settings.ts, ui/panels/colour-settings-dialog.ts, io/dpx.ts new; ui/panels/colour-dialogs.ts, ui/prefs.ts, io/api.ts, io/export-presets.ts, io/images.ts, io/links.ts, ui/panels/export-dialog.ts, engine/index.ts, styles/dialogs.css)

`engine.convertDeepDocument(plan)`: one step that replaces each pixel layer's channels with the engine's LittleCMS result and sets the mode, profile and depth (RGB, grayscale, CMYK with its tables, Lab). `convertDocumentDeep` in `colour-dialogs.ts` sends every layer's floats (a 16-bit layer's own, ink, Lab, or an 8-bit raster widened) to `/api/color/convert-deep`; Convert to Profile now lists RGB, CMYK, Gray and Lab destinations and uses it for 16-bit documents, any change of mode, Lab, and when dither is on. 8-bit RGB to RGB and 8-bit CMYK to CMYK without dither keep the table and ink paths they had; 32-bit keeps the linear matrix and refuses other spaces with a message. The old two-step Lab path (`engine.setRgbFromLab()` before the table) was dropped: Lab converts in one step.

Color Settings (`colour.settings`, Shift+Mod+K): working RGB, CMYK and Gray, a policy for each (preserve, convert, off), ask on mismatch and on a missing profile, intent, black point compensation, dither, LittleCMS shown as the only engine, and the chosen CMYK profile's total ink and black generation read-only from `/api/color/profile-info`. Saved in Preferences (`colour`, `colourPresets`); `profileMismatch` follows the RGB policy (`discard` added for Off) so the opening path in app.ts, which reads it, honours it. `MissingProfileDialog` is built and returned by `installColorSettings` but app.ts does not call it yet. Dither defaults off so plain conversions stay exact.

DPX: `.dpx` in `IMAGE_ACCEPT`, `isImageFile`, the linked-file picker and the engine decode list; Export As gains DPX with bit depth and transfer rows (kept in presets); `io/dpx.ts` `dpxBlob` writes the document at 16 bits through `encodeDpx`. The Export As path in app.ts sends the 8-bit canvas through `api.encode`, which writes 10-bit log; `dpxBlob` is the full one for app.ts to call when `s.format === 'dpx'`.

## Agent Connect and the catalogue tools, DEV_PLAN 28.4 (ui/panels/agent-connect.ts, automation/agent-bridge.ts, styles/terminal.css)

`AgentConnect` is a floating panel built once (master switch, a row per agent with its policy select, an approval sheet, the activity feed, Follow Agent, Stop); the engine's `/api/agents/stream` WebSocket patches rows, approvals and feed entries in place with `patchList`. `installAgentConnect(commands, engine)` registers `agent.connect.open`. Follow Agent moves the view to a layer or rectangle the step touched, or the active layer after a tool that adds one. In `agent-bridge.ts`, `catalogueTool` serves `list_commands`, `describe_command`, `run_command` and `run_commands` through `window.formvis.catalogue` and answers a clear error when it is absent; `get_selection` and `get_layer_tree` (a nested view of `get_document`) are cases of `run`.

## Vector masks, 27.7's second part · _v1.66.1 (engine/vector-mask.ts new; engine/index.ts, engine/renderer.ts, engine/types.ts, engine/paths.ts, ui/paths.ts, io/project-io.ts, app.ts)

DEV_PLAN 27.7. `Layer.vectorMask` (`VectorMask`: path in document pixels, enabled, linked, inverted). Document pixels rather than the layer's own, so operations that grow or re-render a layer's raster in place (filters that spread, smart object re-renders) never move it; the cost is that the linked case is carried explicitly: `followVector` at each user transform (move, nudge, align and distribute, flips, Free Transform), `distortVector` through Distort's homography, and `carryVectors` over every canvas change (crop, straighten, canvas and image size, the three rotations, flips, perspective crop, an artboard's export). While a move or transform is live, the renderers draw the cached coverage through `boxChange` (a matrix on `MaskInfo.mat`, and the GPU mask's matrix), so nothing is redrawn per frame. `vectorCoverage` caches one coverage per mask object and canvas size; empty and not inverted shows all (null), empty and inverted (Hide All) hides all. The Paths panel lists it (`maskEntry`, a `vmask:` id) over a working copy (`maskEdit`) that the tools change in place, so the stored path, shared with undo, is never mutated. Rasterize intersects the coverage into the layer mask in the mask's own pixels. Project records carry `vectorMask` with `pathData` subpaths.

Verified by a probe in the app: Hide All left the pixel at 0,0,0,0; Current Path over a rectangle showed white inside; a linked nudge of 10 moved the first anchor 20 to 30 and an unlinked one left it at 30; Rasterize made a layer mask and removed the vector mask; undo restored it. tsc, the build, 194 unit tests.

Noted: Warp, Puppet Warp and Perspective Warp leave a vector mask where it is; PSD files do not carry vector masks on pixel layers yet; the Layers panel shows no vector mask thumbnail yet (the Paths panel entry is how to reach it); moving a folder's members does not move the folder's own vector mask. The lines this release changed are not quoted here (the owner asked for fewer steps per release); the feat commit's diff holds them.

## Fill layers: New Fill Layer, Layer Content Options and Rasterize Fill Content, 27.7's first part · _v1.66.0 (engine/fill-layers.ts and ui/panels/fill-layer-dialog.ts new; engine/types.ts, engine/history.ts, engine/index.ts, io/project-io.ts, io/psd.ts, ui/layers.ts, automation/agent-bridge.ts, app.ts; docs/MANUAL.md, .docs/wiki/Project-Format.md, the project-format skill, NOTICE.md)

DEV_PLAN 27.7's first part, after Photoshop's Layer > New Fill Layer (Solid Color, Gradient and Pattern layers that fill the whole canvas, stay editable through Layer Content Options and come with a mask). fill-layers.ts: `gradientPosition(style, angle, scale, reverse, offset, frame)`, where a point falls along a gradient fill: the gradient runs through the frame's centre moved by the offset (fractions of the frame) at the angle, counter-clockwise from the right, and at 100 percent spans the frame's whole extent along that angle (its width times the cosine plus its height times the sine), Linear from one end of it to the other, Reflected out both ways from the centre, Radial and Diamond to half of it, Angle once round counter-clockwise from the angle, as Photoshop's documentation describes its angle gradient; its trigonometry is worked out once per drawing (a first version recomputed it per pixel); `ditherAt`, a fixed value per pixel from `mix32`, half a level either way; `fillFrame(l, W, H)`, the frame a fill is laid out in: with Align with Layer (a gradient) or Link with Layer (a pattern), the bounds of what the layer's mask shows, else the canvas; `renderFill(c, W, H, frame)`, the fill over a W by H canvas (a gradient through a 4,096 entry table of `colorAt` over its stops, dithered when asked; a pattern as a canvas pattern turned and scaled from the frame's corner when linked, moved by its phase), null when the pattern is not defined; `fillName` (Color Fill, Gradient Fill, Pattern Fill, as Photoshop names them); `fillContentFrom`, a saved fill read back with every field checked and clamped, null when it is not one.

Engine: `Layer.fillContent` (types.ts: `FillContent`, a solid colour, a gradient with `FillStop`s, style, angle, scale, reverse, dither, align and offset, or a pattern with its id, scale, angle, link and phase; Photoshop's own fields, so they travel in PSD files), the layer's `raster` being its drawing over the whole canvas at `docTransform`. `History.amend(snap)` replaces the last step's result while nothing is undone or open, and `dropRedo()` forgets the undone steps. index.ts: `newFillLayer(content)`, one New Fill Layer step: the layer above the active one, named as Photoshop numbers them, with Photoshop's default mask as the target, revealing all (a mask without pixels) or, with a selection, drawn from it on a canvas-sized mask, the selection used up; `previewFill(id, content)` shows a fill through the renderer's `source` override without recording anything, in a CMYK document through its inks (`deriveWhole`, `rasterFromChannels`); `setFillContent(id, content)`, one Modify Fill Layer step, nothing when unchanged; `amendNewFill(id, content, name)` puts the dialog's fill and name into the New Fill Layer step just made (`History.amend`), its floats or inks brought into step first as `edit` brings them (the first probe in CMYK showed the ink of the default black under a green fill, which a move then showed); `dropNewFill(id)` takes that step back with `undoNow` and `dropRedo`, as though never made. Fill layers are endless as Photoshop's: `pinFills(p)`, run by the step hook at the end of every step before the channels are derived, draws again every fill layer that was moved or transformed (back at `docTransform`, its mask taking the old place as its placement when it had none, so the mask moves and the fill stays over the canvas) or whose drawing is stale; `fillKeys` notes on each drawn raster what it was drawn for (`fillKey`: the content, the canvas size and, when the mask lays it out, the mask's state), so a raster read from a file, or one whose content, canvas or laying-out mask changed, is drawn again (`drawFill`); `deriveChannels` keeps that note on a fill layer's CMYK rendition (`shown`), which had otherwise been drawn again at every step. Painting: `paintable` lets a fill layer paint its mask when the mask is the target, and otherwise asks to rasterize it as a type or shape layer does ("Rasterize this fill layer?"); `smartLocked`, `averageFill`, `applyImageEdit` and `applyImageEditAsync` say `FILL_NOTICE` (Layer Content Options, the mask, or Rasterize > Fill Content); `bandedFilter` and `fadeStep` leave fill layers alone; Warp, Puppet Warp and Perspective Warp name fill layers among those to rasterize first. `rasterizeLayer` and `rasterizeLayers('fill' | 'layer' | 'all')` (Rasterize Fill Content) clear `fillContent`, as do Convert to Smart Object and Apply Redactions.

The window: `FillLayerDialog` (fill-layer-dialog.ts), titled Solid Color, Gradient Fill or Pattern Fill, its rows for the fill's kind chosen before it shows so it opens at its size: the name (for a new layer), and the colour; or Gradient (Current gradient when editing, then every preset, its stops resolved with the colours as they are), Style, Angle, Scale, Reverse, Dither and Align with Layer; or Pattern (with Missing pattern when the layer's is not defined here), Angle, Scale and Link with Layer. `showNew(kind)` makes the layer at once (the foreground colour, the Gradient tool's gradient at 90 degrees, or the Pattern Stamp's pattern) and shows the dialog over it; `showEdit(id)` shows the layer's own fill. Each change previews on the canvas at most once a frame; OK (or Enter in a text field) records it, Cancel or Escape takes a new layer back or ends the preview. app.ts: commands new-fill-solid, new-fill-gradient and new-fill-pattern (Solid Color..., Gradient..., Pattern...), layer-content-options (on a fill layer the dialog, on an adjustment layer its settings, as Edit Adjustment did) and rasterize-fill; Rasterize Layer and Rasterize All Layers count fill layers; the Layer menu has New Fill Layer before New Adjustment Layer and Layer Content Options after it, where Edit Adjustment... stood (the command stays, in Search and Keyboard Shortcuts), as Photoshop's; Rasterize has Fill Content after Shape; `cv:fill-options` shows the dialog. layers.ts: a fill layer's row is `is-fill`, counted with adjustments by the kind filter as Photoshop's, and a double-click on it outside its name and mask shows Layer Content Options. agent-bridge.ts: `get_document` names a fill layer's kind `fill:solid`, `fill:gradient` or `fill:pattern`. project-io.ts: `fillContent` written beside the layer's pixels, a pattern fill's pattern carried with the patterns the styles use, and read back through `fillContentFrom` on a layer with pixels. psd.ts: `psdPattern`, Pattern Overlay's adding of a pattern to the PSD's patterns made shared; `toPsdFill` writes a fill as Photoshop's `vectorFill` (a colour, a gradient with colour and opacity stops, style, angle, scale, reverse, dither, align and offset, or a pattern with its phase), noting a pattern fill's scale and angle, which it cannot write, and an unlinked pattern, since ag-psd's writer fails on the link flag ("Invalid integer value: true, key: Lnkd"); `fromPsdFill` reads one back (a gradient's opacity stops interpolated onto its colour stops; a pattern registered from the file's patterns), noting a noise gradient or a missing pattern, which open as pixels; a PSD layer with a fill and no shape path or stroke opens as a fill layer, drawn over the canvas when the file has no pixels for it.

Verified by scratch probes outside the repository, on a 400 by 300 document with a layer above the Background. New Fill Layer's three commands enabled with a document; Layer Content Options and Rasterize Fill Content not without a fill layer. Solid Color: the dialog 380 by 204, Name "Color Fill 1" and the foreground's black; red previewed on the canvas with nothing recorded; OK one New Fill Layer step, the layer 400 by 300 at 0, 0 with a mask without pixels as the target; Undo removed it and Redo brought it back red. Gradient: Cancel left the steps, the layers and Redo as they were; black to white at 90 degrees read 0 at the bottom row, 127 halfway and 255 at the top; Layer Content Options (380 by 369, Current gradient) to Radial, 50 percent, Reverse read 253 at the centre, 42 at 62 pixels out and 0 at the corner, one Modify Fill Layer step. Pattern: the checker from the canvas's corner. From a 100 by 100 selection at 100, 50: the mask drawn from it, the selection used up, the 0 degree gradient fitted to the selection (1 at its left edge, 129 halfway, 254 at its right); moved 50 pixels: the layer back at 0, 0, the mask placed at 50, the gradient laid out again (1, 129 and 254 at 150, 200 and 249). With the content as the target a brush stroke asked "Rasterize this fill layer?"; with the mask as the target it painted, one Brush step; Invert said the fill layer's notice. Canvas Size to 500 wide drew the red over the new area, Image Size to 250 by 150 drew it at that size; Rasterize Fill Content cleared the fill, one step. A project serialized and read back kept the four fills and their kinds; a PSD written and read back kept the solid colour, both gradients (Radial, 90, 50 percent, reversed; Linear, 0) and the pattern as fill layers, with no notes. In CMYK a green solid fill showed its CMYK rendition (102, 180, 56) after OK, kept its pixels through another step, was drawn again at the same rendition when moved and left alone after; at 16 and 32 bits and in Lab a fill kept its colour and was drawn again only when moved. No page errors. Screenshots: an Angle spectrum gradient previewed inside a selection while its dialog was open, the Pattern Fill dialog, and a checker at 300 percent turned 30 degrees, with the gradient fill's row showing its mask. Zero flash, under 6x CPU and network throttling after a hard reload, through the menus: Solid Color's dialog 380 by 204 from its first frame to its last, the new row added and the other two kept; the colour previewed and OK keeping the three rows; Gradient's dialog 380 by 409 throughout, its Style and Scale previewed keeping the four rows, Cancel removing only the new row (the rows below it moved by `patchList`, which removes a row that went only after placing the rest, kept as they were, as when any top layer goes); a double-click on Color Fill 1's thumbnail showing Layer Content Options at 380 by 164, the colour previewed and OK keeping every row, one Modify Fill Layer step; Layer Content Options from the menu and Escape the same; Pattern's dialog 380 by 312, its Scale previewed and Enter keeping the rows; Rasterize Fill Content changing its row's class in place; no layout shift anywhere. tsc, the build, 194 unit tests; 112 engine tests passed, 3 failing on this machine as before.     if (!info) {

```text
      info = { name: pat.name, id: guid(), x: 0, y: 0, bounds: { x: 0, y: 0, w, h }, data: new Uint8Array(rgba) };
      (info as PatternInfo & { formvis?: string }).formvis = pat.id;
      patterns.push(info);
    }
    e.patternOverlay = { ...on, opacity: po.opacity, blendMode: bm(po.blend), scale: po.scale, pattern: { name: info.name, id: info.id }, align: true };
  }
      if (!adj && (!pl.canvas || !pl.canvas.width || !pl.canvas.height)) continue;
      const w = pl.canvas?.width ?? 0, h = pl.canvas?.height ?? 0, raster = adj || !pl.canvas ? null : Raster.from(pl.canvas, w, h);
        : newLayer(name, doc, { raster, parentId, transform: { ...docTransform(w, h), x: pl.left ?? 0, y: pl.top ?? 0 }, visible: !pl.hidden, opacity: pl.opacity ?? 1, blend, ...fill });
const kindOf = (l: Layer): KindId => (l.adjustment ? 'adjustment' : l.text ? 'type' : l.vector ? 'shape' : l.smart ? 'smart' : 'pixel');
```

## Edit > Search, the command palette, and the Keyboard Shortcuts list in place, closing 27.6 · _v1.65.9 (ui/command-palette.ts new; app.ts, ui/app-dialogs.ts, styles/dialogs.css; docs/MANUAL.md, .docs/wiki/Keyboard-Shortcuts.md, NOTICE.md)

DEV_PLAN 27.6's last part, after Photoshop's Edit > Search. command-palette.ts: `fuzzyScore(query, text)`, how well a query names a text, or null when its letters are not all in it in order (case ignored): the best placing of the letters, found by a small dynamic programme over the two, each letter scoring 1, 7 more when it directly follows the one before and 5 more at a word's start (after a space or a mark, or a capital after a small letter), a hundredth less the further in it lies, less an eighth of the text's length so shorter names rank first. `CommandPalette`, a Dialog titled Search holding a field and a list. `show()` takes each command's place in the menus from the menu definitions (`pathsOf`: the first place a command appears, submenus joined with " > ", File's Open Recent as it reads then). `render()` scores each command on its name (a trailing "..." dropped), or failing that 10 behind on its name and menu path together, so a name match comes before a path match ("blur" puts Blur before Average, where one text of name and path together would tie them and order them by name); tools on their name and "tool", 2 ahead while something is typed; with nothing typed, what was last run from the palette first (twelve at most, newest first) and the rest by name; sorted by score, then name; the twelve best. The rows are twelve slots keyed by position, each filled in place (the name; the menu path and the keys after an interpunct; a tool's icon; dimmed with `is-off` and aria-disabled when the command cannot run, not the disabled attribute, since a disabled button swallows the press and the dialog took the focus from the field), so only trailing slots come and go. Up and Down move the selection (is-selected, aria-selected); Enter or a click runs the selected row when it can run, the palette closing first so a dialog the command shows takes the focus; a press in the list keeps the focus in the field. Escape and closing are the Dialog's. The first version keyed the rows by command, and under throttling typing moved the rows that stayed (layout shifts of 0.0051 and 0.0032, attributed to input); with slots, and the path in a fixed 250 pixel column aligned right, there were none.

app.ts: the search command (Search..., Mod+K, the key command palettes commonly take; Photoshop's Ctrl+F is formvis's Last Filter since 1.64.4) and `dialogs.palette`, made with the commands, a getter for the menus and the engine; the Edit menu has Search after Clear, between separators, as Photoshop's. Keyboard Shortcuts (app-dialogs.ts): `render()` built every row again with `replaceChildren` on each keystroke of its search and each change, as found at 1.64.9; it now patches the rows by command id (tool rows by their name) through `patchList`, a command's row brought up to date in place by `fillRow` (its name, its keys or the capture prompt, its buttons' labels and Remove's state), its Change and Remove handlers bound once when the row is made; the focus goes back to the row's first button only when it is not already in that row. Found while checking it, not from this release: since 1.53.4 the rows had no columns of their own and took the list rows' three (an 18 pixel icon column, the name, an auto column) for four children, so each name was squeezed into 18 pixels over several lines and Remove fell to a second grid line under the next row, where a pointer could not reach it (the probe's click on it timed out, the next row intercepting it); `.cv-keys-row` now has its own (the name, the keys in a fixed 210 pixels aligned right, the two buttons), tool rows two.

Verified by scratch probes outside the repository. Ctrl+K: the dialog 560 by 558, the field focused, twelve rows, by name from "16 Bits/Channel" with nothing typed. "gblur": Gaussian Blur first (Filter > Blur). "fit": Fit Image (File > Automate), then Fit on Screen (View · Ctrl+0), the two tied and ordered by name. "brush": Brush Tool (Tool · B) first; chosen with the arrows and run with Enter, the tool became the Brush; Ctrl+K again with nothing typed: Brush Tool first. "invert": Invert (Image > Adjustments · Ctrl+I); Enter applied it, one Invert step. "zzqx": no rows and "No command or tool matches.", the dialog the same size. "revert" on a document never saved: Revert dimmed and selected; Enter and a click left the palette as it was, the focus in the field. Escape closed it. The Edit menu: Clear Selection Pixels, a separator, Search... Ctrl+K, a separator, the Fill submenu; Search from it showed the palette; "image size" and a click showed Image Size. Ranking: "blur" Blur, Blur More, Box Blur, Field Blur, Gaussian Blur, Iris Blur; "hue" Hue/Saturation; "save" Save, Save As, Save a Copy; "rot 90" the two quarter turns; "lev" Levels. Keyboard Shortcuts: 467 rows; "fill" left 9, the same 9 nodes; Remove on Fill with Foreground showed "none", disabled Remove and put the focus on Change, all 9 kept; Change showed the prompt and Alt+Backspace set it back, all 9 kept; a screenshot showed each row on one line with both buttons. Zero flash, under 6x CPU and network throttling after a hard reload: Ctrl+K, typing g, a and u, Backspace, Down and Up, "invert" and Enter, Ctrl+K again and Escape: the dialog 560 by 558 from its first frame to its last, the twelve rows kept at every keystroke ("invert" left eight, the last four going; the next showing added four back), the Layers rows kept, no shift; Keyboard Shortcuts 620 by 468 throughout, typing "fill" keeping the nine rows that stayed, and Remove, Change and the new key keeping all nine, no shift. tsc, the build, 194 unit tests; 112 engine tests passed, 3 failing on this machine as before. The whole browser suite from a freshly started dev server and engine: 505 passed, 3 skipped, 24 failed, the 22 failing at 1.65.2, the tiled paging race of 1.65.6, and test_locked_pixels_refuse_painting_and_say_why, which reads the lock button's pressed state right after its click while the Layers panel draws on the next frame: it passed three times run alone, and nothing in this release touches the panel.

## File > Close All, Close Others, Save a Copy, Revert and Automate > Fit Image, 27.6's fourth part · _v1.65.8 (ui/panels/save-copy-dialog.ts new; engine/index.ts, app.ts, ui/dialogs.ts, ui/panels/size-dialogs.ts, ui/actions.ts, ui/panels/actions-dialogs.ts; docs/MANUAL.md, .docs/wiki/Keyboard-Shortcuts.md)

DEV_PLAN 27.6, fourth part, after Photoshop's File menu (Close All and Close Others closing documents without asking; Revert reading the saved file back as one history step that keeps the document's identity and tab name and leaves it saved; Save a Copy writing the document, or its flattened image, elsewhere; Fit Image scaling by the smaller of the two ratios through Image Size, refusing to enlarge when Don't Enlarge is ticked). Engine: `revertTo(doc, activeId, paths, timeline)` puts a document read back from the library in place of the current one's as one Revert step, built with the history's own begin and end so the step carries the paths and the timeline (frames and video) on both sides, as path and timeline steps do, and Undo brings every one back; the document keeps its id (filters' displacement maps name documents by it), its tiled layers get the engine's tile reader as opening gives them, the selection goes, the active layer is the saved one, the history is marked saved after the step, and the view is fitted again only when the size differs. `mergedDoc()`: the document flattened into one Background layer with everything else of it kept, refused past 268 megapixels a layer; `duplicateDocument` now takes its merged copy from it (the same layer and document as before). `fitImage(width, height, enlarge, quiet)`: the smaller of the two ratios, rounded sides at least one pixel; when the image already fits (or would only grow without `enlarge`) it says so unless `quiet` and answers true, so an action plays on; otherwise one Fit Image step around `resampleImage` (high quality, the same resolution; the history's nesting names it), after settling anything pending. `resampleImage` now refuses a document with a tiled layer: the first probe of Fit Image on a 40,000 by 30,000 document showed Image Size making the canvas 10,000 by 7,500 while the tiled layer kept its 40,000 by 30,000 tiles under a 10,000 by 7,500 transform.

The window: the Unsaved Changes question (dialogs.ts) gains an Apply to All check, hidden unless asked for before the dialog shows, so it opens at its final size; `ask(name, many)` answers the choice and whether it was ticked; `askSaveChanges` keeps its answer, and `askSaveChangesAll` asks with the check. `SaveCopyDialog` (save-copy-dialog.ts): the copy's name ("<name> copy" first) and Layers (ticked); Save, or Enter in the name, hands both to the app. `FitImageDialog` (size-dialogs.ts): Width and Height in pixels (the image's own size first, then the last box) and Don't Enlarge; OK closes, fits and reports the box for Actions, whether or not the image changed. app.ts: `readOpened(o)`, open's reading of a project from the engine moved out so Revert reads the same way; `saveCopy(name, layers)` saves the document or `mergedDoc()` under a new name after asking to replace one taken, leaving the document's name, library name and unsaved state alone, and moves the document's library version on only when it saved over its own file without a conflict; `revert()` reads the library's copy and hands it to `revertTo`, bringing the document forward if another took its place meanwhile, and takes the version read; `requestClose(id, answer)` now answers whether the document closed and takes an answer already given; `closeMany(keep)` closes every document but `keep` in turn, bringing each with unsaved changes forward and asking, with Apply to All when another is waiting, stopping at Cancel or a failed save, and brings `keep` back. Commands: save-copy (Alt+Mod+S), revert (F12 in the desktop app only, since browsers keep F12 for their developer tools; enabled for a library document with unsaved changes), close-all (Alt+Mod+W in the desktop app, where Close Tab keeps Mod+W alone; no key in browsers, where Alt+Mod+W is Close Tab), close-others (Alt+Mod+P; two documents or more) and fit-image. The File menu: Save a Copy and Revert after Save As; Close All and Close Others after Close Tab; Fit Image first in Automate's second group, as Photoshop orders them. Actions: the `fitImage` step (`w`, `h`, `enlarge`), read back from storage and JSON with its checks, played quietly by `runStep`; the Actions dialog's note names Fit Image.

Verified by scratch probes outside the repository. In a browser the keys are Close Tab Alt+Mod+W, Close All none, Close Others Alt+Mod+P, Save a Copy Alt+Mod+S, Revert none; with no document the five are disabled. Fit Image on a 400 by 300 white document with a red 200 by 150 block at its corner: 200 by 200 made 200 by 150, one Fit Image step, red at (50, 30) and white at (150, 100), undone to 400 by 300; 800 by 800 without enlarging left it and said "The image already fits within 800 × 800 px."; with enlarging 800 by 600; 400 by 300 added no step; 1000 by 150 made 200 by 150. Its dialog offered Width 400, Height 300 and Don't Enlarge off; 120 by 120 made 120 by 90 and was recorded as "Fit Image 120 x 120"; played from the Actions dialog on a 1000 by 500 document it made 120 by 60 ("Played "Fit probe", 1 step."), and on a 100 by 80 one 120 by 96; the dialog then offered 120 by 120 again. Save a Copy on a two-layer library document, 300 by 200, changed since its save: the dialog offered "<name> copy" with Layers ticked; Save said "Saved a copy as <name> copy.", the library's copy 300 by 200 with two layers, the document still named as before, changed, its library name unchanged; Layers off saved a one-layer copy; the same name again asked "Replace project?" and Cancel saved nothing. Revert on it: the square drawn since the save gone (white at (110, 110)), the saved blue at (20, 20), one Revert step, not changed, Revert disabled, the Art layer active; Undo brought the square back, changed, Revert enabled; Redo reverted again. After Image Size to 150 by 100 and a path added: Revert gave 300 by 200, no paths, the view fitted (zoom 2.35), and Undo 150 by 100 with the path. Close Others among eight documents, six changed: the first changed one (not the current) came forward and was asked about with Apply to All; Cancel left all eight; again from an unchanged one, Apply to All ticked and Don't Save: only that one left, no second question. Close All with one unchanged and one changed: the unchanged one closed, the changed one asked about without Apply to All; Don't Save left none, and Close All and Close Others disabled. A screenshot showed the question with Apply to All under its note, and the Save a Copy and Fit Image dialogs. Zero flash, under 6x CPU and network throttling after a hard reload, from the menus: the Save a Copy dialog 360 by 234 from its first frame, Layers unticked and Save keeping every Layers row; Revert, its Undo and its Redo keeping every row (the saved file's layer ids are the document's, so the rows update in place); the Fit Image dialog 360 by 259 and its OK keeping every row; Close Others' question 460 by 239 from its first frame with Apply to All, the rows those of the document asked about and then of the one kept; Close All's 460 by 211 without it, Cancel keeping everything; no shift. A second probe: Save a Copy, flattened, under the document's own library name asked to replace it and saved one layer there, the document still two layers and changed; Revert then read that one layer; after Undo, Save said "Saved <name>." with no conflict (the version moved on with the copy) and the library held two layers again; with the library file deleted, Revert said "Project not found." and changed nothing. On a 40,000 by 30,000 document Image Size now refused ("A document with layers past 268 megapixels cannot be resampled yet."), Fit Image answered false with no step, and Save a Copy without Layers refused to flatten. tsc, the build, 194 unit tests; 112 engine tests passed, 3 failing on this machine as before. The whole browser suite from a freshly started dev server and engine: 506 passed, 3 skipped, 23 failed, the 22 failing at 1.65.2 and the tiled paging race of 1.65.6; the menu walk ran the new commands without an error (export-exr's 500 its one, as before), Revert joining the commands none of its states enables (TEST_PLAN section 45).

## Toggle Last State, Paste Special and Edit > Stroke, 27.6's third part · _v1.65.7 (ui/panels/stroke-dialog.ts new; engine/index.ts, app.ts; docs/MANUAL.md, .docs/wiki/Keyboard-Shortcuts.md)

DEV_PLAN 27.6, third part, after Photoshop's Edit menu (Toggle Last State: redo when there is one, else undo; Paste Into: pasted centred on the selection's bounds behind a mask from the selection or its inverse, unlinked; Stroke: a band along the selection's edge). Engine: `toggleLastState()` redoes when the history can, else undoes. `pasteInto(outside, image)`: formvis's own clipboard, or a picture from another app given as `image`, pasted as a new layer (`newLayer`, `parentForNew`, `insertAboveActive`, as `insertRasterLayer` places one) centred on the selection's bounds, with a layer mask the size of the canvas (the selection drawn into it, or a white canvas with the selection cut out for Paste Outside), unlinked and placed at the canvas (`docTransform`), so the picture moves behind a mask that stays; the selection is used up, as Photoshop's; one Paste Into or Paste Outside step; without a selection or anything to paste, a notice. `strokeSelection(o)`: the edge is the selection's, or with none the active layer's pixels drawn into the work area through their placement, either taken at half coverage (128); the work area is the edge's bounds grown by the width and two pixels, past the canvas too, so pixels beyond the canvas count as outside and Select All strokes the canvas's border inside it; `distanceSquared` (matting.ts) from every inside pixel to the nearest outside one and from every outside pixel to the nearest inside one; a pixel's coverage is its distance within the band's reach (the width, or half of it for Center, on each side) plus one, clamped, so on a straight edge a whole width is exactly that many pixels (the edge lies half a pixel from each centre) and outer corners round; filled through `fillWith` with the band as its region, so mode, opacity, Preserve Transparency and a mask target behave as Edit > Fill's; one Stroke step; the selection stays. The first version took the band from `resizeMask` (Select > Modify's expand and contract), whose half-pixel soft edge left a half-covered pixel at every inner and outer edge; measured at 4 px on a rectangle it gave x 100 to 103 red and 104 half, and now 104 is untouched.

The window: `StrokeDialog` (stroke-dialog.ts): Width (1 to 250 px), Color (the foreground's when it opens), Location (Inside, Center, Outside; Center first), Mode (the blend modes Edit > Fill offers), Opacity and Preserve Transparency, the rest kept between uses; OK, or Enter in Width, strokes. Commands: toggle-last-state (Alt+Mod+Z; enabled when there is a step to undo or redo), paste-in-place (Shift+Mod+V; the same as Paste, which already puts formvis's own copy where it was), paste-into (Alt+Shift+Mod+V) and paste-outside, both with a selection, and stroke-dialog (with a selection, or a layer with pixels). `pasteFromMenu(outside)` and `pasteExternal(file, outside)` take Paste Into's or Paste Outside's side, reading the system clipboard as Paste does and falling back to formvis's own; `pasteInto` names its own refusals, so the menu adds none. The Edit menu: Toggle Last State after Redo; a Paste Special submenu after Paste; Stroke... after the Fill submenu, as Photoshop orders them. The Edit menu is now taller than the browser suite's 900 pixel window and scrolls, as the Layer menu has since 1.64.8.

Verified by scratch probes outside the repository, on a 400 by 300 document. Toggle Last State after a fill undid it (white) and again redid it (red). With a 60 by 40 red block copied and a 100 by 100 selection at (200, 150): Paste Into made Pasted Layer at (220, 180), its mask unlinked, enabled, 400 by 300 at (0, 0), the selection gone, one Paste Into step; red inside both, white outside the selection; moved to x 150, the picture hid outside the selection and showed inside; undone twice, two layers and the selection back. Paste Outside hid the picture inside the selection, one Paste Outside step. Without a selection both were disabled and refused. Stroke on a 100 by 80 selection at (100, 100): the dialog with Width 1, the foreground's colour, Center, Normal, 100 and no Preserve; 4 px Inside: x 100 to 103 red, 104 and 99 untouched, the top and bottom rows red, the middle untouched, the selection kept, one Stroke step; 4 px Outside in blue: x 96 to 99 blue, 95 and 100 untouched, the corner at (96, 96) untouched (rounded); 4 px Center in green at 50 percent: x 98 to 101 half green, 97 and 102 untouched; Select All, 3 px Inside in black: x 0 to 2 black at the left and the right and bottom edges black, x 3 untouched. No selection, on the layer with the red block: 2 px Outside black at x 18 and 19, 17 untouched, 21 still red. The menus as listed above (the Edit menu 892 pixels tall, scrolling 956). Zero flash, under 6x CPU and network throttling after a hard reload, each from the menus: Paste Into added its row and kept the others; Toggle Last State twice removed it and brought it back, the other rows kept; the Stroke dialog 360 by 356 from its first frame and its OK, every row kept; Paste in Place added its row; nothing shifted. tsc, the build, 194 unit tests; 112 engine tests passed, 3 failing on this machine as before. The whole browser suite from a freshly started dev server and engine: 506 passed, 3 skipped, 23 failed, the 22 failing at 1.65.2 and the tiled paging race of 1.65.6; the menu walk ran the new commands without an error (export-exr's 500 its one, as before), and the menu tests passed with the Edit menu scrolling.

## Edit > Transform: Again, Scale, Rotate, Skew, Distort, Perspective and the layer's quarter turns, 27.6's second part · _v1.65.6 (engine/distort.ts, engine/index.ts, extensions/tools/move.ts, ui/actions.ts, app.ts; docs/MANUAL.md, .docs/wiki/Tools.md and Keyboard-Shortcuts.md)

DEV_PLAN 27.6, second part, after Photoshop's Edit > Transform (Scale, Rotate, Skew, Distort and Perspective each a way of dragging the same transform's handles; Again repeating the last transform). distort.ts: `DistortMode` and `distortDragged(from, handle, dx, dy, mode)`, the corners after dragging a handle (0 to 3 the corners in handle order, 4 to 7 the middles of the top, right, bottom and left sides) from the corners the drag began with: Distort moves a corner, or both corners of a side, by the drag; Skew slides a side along itself (the drag projected on the side) and a corner along one of its two sides, whichever the drag follows more (the larger projection); Perspective moves a corner so and the other corner of that same side by as much the opposite way, its sides sliding as in Skew. `againQuad(from, to, corners)`: `corners` through the perspective that took `from` to `to`, in document space (the two homographies composed). Engine: `distortEdit` gains `mode` and `beginDistort(mode)`, default distort, so a Cmd-drag on a corner is as before; `moveDistortHandle(handle, from, dx, dy)` replaces `moveDistortCorner(i, pt)`, the Move tool keeping where the drag and the corners began, so constrained drags are measured from the start; `applyDistort` names its step by the mode (Distort, Skew, Perspective; with Layers after it for a group) and remembers the corners before and after. `beginDistortMode(mode)` switches a pending distortion's mode with its corners kept, or begins one on the Move tool; with a warp, puppet warp or perspective warp pending it says to finish that first.

The transform's memory: `lastTransform`, set by `endTransform` for any box committed (a move, a handle's scale or turn, a group's box, a placed mask's; not a floating selection's), by `setLayerTransform` (the options bar's values), by `flipLayers` (as a flip) and by `applyDistort` (the corners). `transformAgain(copy)` runs as one Transform Again step: with `copy`, `duplicateLayers` first, then a flip again, or `beginDistort` with its corners taken through `againQuad` and applied, or `beginTransform` with the box's draft `following(original, from, to)` (the recorded box change's own matrix applied in document space, so a layer turned about a point keeps turning about it, as Photoshop's step and repeat relies on) and `endTransform('Transform Again')`. Its inner steps nest inside the outer one (the history's depth), so the duplicate and the transform undo together; a position lock refuses it; `canTransformAgain` enables the commands. `endTransform(name)` takes the step's name from a command; its single-layer branch's local name became `step`, since the parameter now holds the given one. `rotateLayers(quarters)`: `beginTransform` in rotate mode, the box's rotation plus the quarter turns, brought into -180 to 180 degrees, committed as Rotate 90° Clockwise, Rotate 180° or Rotate 90° Counter Clockwise; several layers or a folder turn about their box's centre through the group path, a targeted placed mask alone, and no pixel is resampled. `transformConstraint` ('scale', 'rotate' or null), set by `beginTransformMode(kind)` after `transformCommand`, cleared by `endTransformMode` (Enter or Escape in the Move tool), by `transformCommand` (Free Transform) and by `setTool` changing the tool.
