DEV_PLAN 27.6, first part, after Photoshop's Image menu. adjust.ts: `autoLevels` and its `LevelRangeData` moved here from adjust-panel.ts unchanged but for the first line of its doc comment, which had lost its start and now says what it is, so the Levels dialog's Auto (adjust-panel.ts imports it) and the Image menu's Auto commands share one function. `desaturatePixels(d)`: each pixel grey at (max + min) / 2, Hue/Saturation's grey at -100. `equalizePixels(d, cov)`: one histogram over the R, G and B values of the visible pixels, each weighted by `cov`'s alpha when given (the selected area's), its cumulative count mapped so the first filled level is black and the last white, the same table for every channel (histogram equalisation, a soft selection edge weighing its pixels by its coverage). `ReplaceColorSettings` and `replaceColorPixels(d, o, apply)`: each pixel scored as Select > Color Range scores sampled colours (the nearest of `plus` full, none at `fuzziness` levels of distance over the square root of three, less the score from `minus`), and by that score its hue turned and its saturation and lightness pushed toward full or none (`toward`: that share of the way to 1, or to 0 for a negative percentage); with `apply` false only scored; returns the scores. `replacementFor(from, to)`: the Hue, Saturation and Lightness, in whole steps, that turn one colour into another through that push, for the dialog's Result picker.

Engine: `autoAdjust(kind)` builds a Levels kernel from `autoLevels` over the active layer's histogram, weighted by the selection's coverage when there is one (`targetCoverage`, `coverageFor` of the pixels `targetImage` read), so a selection's own histogram sets the levels as in Photoshop, and applies it through `applyImageEdit` within the selection: Auto Tone per channel ('color'), Auto Contrast one range for all three ('contrast'), Auto Color per channel with neutral midtones ('neutral'), each its own step name. `pixelAdjust('desaturate' | 'equalize')` the same way, Equalize with the coverage. `replaceColor(o, preview)` runs `replaceColorPixels` through `previewImageEdit` or `applyImageEdit` (Replace Color); `replaceColorScores(o, boxW, boxH)` scores the active layer's pixels (its mask's when targeted) fitted in a box, with no notices, for the dialog's preview. `rotateCanvasBy(deg)`: whole quarter turns go to `rotateCanvas`; a document with artboards is refused with a notice; otherwise the canvas grows to the turned canvas's bounds (`sizeOk` checked), every layer's transform (and a placed mask's) turns about the old canvas's centre and moves with the growth, its pixels untouched as `rotateCanvas` leaves them; the Background (by `backgroundLayer`, when unmasked and plain pixels, without float channels, smart object or vector) is redrawn canvas-sized over the background colour, turned, so the corners the turn opens take that colour, as Photoshop's do; alpha channels are redrawn turned (`alphasRedrawn`) and the selection drawn turned into a new mask; one Rotate Canvas step, the view fitted after. `cropToSelection()` crops to the selection's bounds through `cropTo` (one Crop step), or says to make a selection. `duplicateDocument(name, merged)`: refused for documents with tiled layers;       'image-size', 'canvas-size', 'content-aware-scale', { label: 'Image Rotation', items: ['rotate-180', 'rotate-90-cw', 'rotate-90-ccw', '-', 'flip-canvas-h', 'flip-canvas-v'] }, '-', 'trim', 'reveal-all', '-', 'generative-expand', { label: 'Upscale', items: ['upscale-2x', 'upscale-4x'] }] },
```text
import { antialiasMask, wandMask } from './kernels';
import { ADJUSTMENT_LABELS, defaultAdjustmentData } from './adjust';
import { fromGray, gaussianBlur, resizeMask, toGray } from './filters';
import { bandCentered, bandExclude, bandHandles, bandInclude, bandSetHandle, bandWeight, hsvAdjust, hueResponse } from '../../engine/adjust';
type LevelRangeData = { black: number; gamma: number; white: number; outputBlack: number; outputWhite: number };

/** each end clips 0.1% of a channel's histogram. Contrast shares one master interval
 *  across R, G and B so channel relationships hold; Color sets each channel; Color + neutral midtones also sets
 *  each channel's gamma so its mean maps to middle gray. `bins` is `histogram()`: composite, then R, G, B. */
function autoLevels(bins: Float64Array, mode: 'contrast' | 'color' | 'neutral'): LevelRangeData[] {
  const fresh = (black = 0, white = 255): LevelRangeData => ({ black, gamma: 1, white, outputBlack: 0, outputWhite: 255 });
  const ranges = [fresh(), fresh(), fresh(), fresh()];
  const endpoints = (c: number): [number, number] | null => {
    const o = c * 256;
    let total = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 256; i++) total += bins[o + i];
    if (!(total > 0)) return null;
    let sum = 0, low = 0, high = 255;
    for (let i = 0; i < 256; i++) { sum += bins[o + i]; if (sum > total * 0.001) { low = i; break; } }
    sum = 0;
    for (let i = 255; i >= 0; i--) { sum += bins[o + i]; if (sum > total * 0.001) { high = i; break; } }
    return low < high ? [low, high] : null;
  };
  if (mode === 'contrast') {
    const lims = [1, 2, 3].map(endpoints).filter((x): x is [number, number] => x !== null);
    if (lims.length) {
      const low = Math.min(...lims.map((x) => x[0])), high = Math.max(...lims.map((x) => x[1]));
      if (low < high) ranges[0] = fresh(low, high);
    }
    return ranges;
  }
  for (let c = 1; c <= 3; c++) {
    const e = endpoints(c);
    if (!e) continue;
    const r = fresh(e[0], e[1]);
    if (mode === 'neutral') {
      let total = 0, acc = 0;
      for (let i = 0; i < 256; i++) { const w = bins[c * 256 + i]; total += w; acc += Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (i - r.black) / (r.white - r.black))) * w; }
      const mean = acc / total;
      if (mean > 0 && mean < 1) r.gamma = Math.min(9.99, Math.max(0.1, Math.log(mean) / Math.log(0.5)));
    }
    ranges[c] = r;
  }
  return ranges;
}

export const VERSION = '1.65.4';
```

## Combine Shapes, New Artboard, Artboard from Group and Frame from Layers, 27.5 closed · _v1.65.4 (engine/paths.ts, engine/index.ts, ui/panels/artboard-dialog.ts, ui/actions.ts, app.ts; docs/MANUAL.md)

DEV_PLAN 27.5, its seventh and last part, after Photoshop's Layer > Combine Shapes (the operation of a shape's outlines after the first; Merge Shape Components tracing the coverage back into outlines) and Layer > New. paths.ts: `mapPath(vp, map)` takes every anchor and handle of a path through a point map, keeping each subpath's operation; `shiftPath` is now `mapPath` with a shift. The old `shiftPath` built each subpath from `closed` and `anchors` alone and so dropped `op`; every shape command that rebuilds the layer from its stored path through it (`recolorShape`, `setShapeStyle`, and `shapeEntry`, the working copy Direct Selection edits) lost the outlines' operations, a PSD shape's hole coming back filled. Found while combining shapes, whose operations must survive. Engine: `placedPath(l)` is a shape layer's outline where its pixels are now, the stored path less `origin` taken through `placement` of its transform, so a moved, scaled, turned or flipped shape (whose stored path no longer matches its pixels) combines where it is drawn. `combineShapes(op)` (op a `PathOp` or 'merge'): with several shape layers selected, the back (lowest) one's outlines first, then each front layer's in stacking order, each front outline taking `op`, except Unite (combine) and Merge, which keep the front outlines' own; with one layer, its outlines after the first take `op`, Unite removing it, and fewer than two outlines is refused with a notice. The front layers are removed (`normalizeClips` after), and the back layer is redrawn through `reshape`, so it keeps its name, fill, stroke, mask and style, as one Combine Shapes step; which layer's look Photoshop keeps was not checked here, and the back one is the shape the others act on. Merge Shape Components ('merge') unites them so and then `mergedOutline` bakes the operations: the path filled by `fillVector` at up to 4 times (16 megapixels at most), its alpha traced by `tracedOutline` and mapped back, one Merge Shape Components step. `tracedOutline` is Convert to Shape's loop, the tracer's loops each simplified within 1.5 of its units and smoothed except at corners, moved out of `selectionToShape` (which now calls it) unchanged; at 4 times the 1.5 is under 0.4 px of the document.

Artboards and frames: `nextArtboardRect(size)` and `nextArtboardName()` are where and how `newArtboard` placed and named the next artboard (over the canvas for the first, else 100 px right of the rightmost at the last one's top and size; Artboard N, the first free), taken out so the dialog shows them; `newArtboard` takes a `name` and uses them. `contentBounds(id)`: the document bounds of the visible pixels of a layer and those inside it (the alignment's measure). `artboardFromGroup(id, { name, w, h })`: a folder outside any other, not an artboard or frame, gets an artboard over its contents (the canvas when it holds no pixels), transparent behind as Artboard from Layers makes them, renamed when a name is given, one step. `frameFromLayers()`: each selected pixel layer outside a frame gets a new frame folder, Frame N, made as the Frame tool's (`newFrameLayer`: a rectangle `frame` and a document-size mask white inside it), fitted to its visible pixels, in the layer's own folder, the layer moved inside it and the folder's entry just above it; one step, the last frame selected. The window: `NewArtboardDialog` (artboard-dialog.ts), titled New Artboard (Name, Width, Height, Background) or New Artboard from Group (no Background row, hidden by its attribute, which `.cv-dialog [hidden]` keeps hidden over the field's grid). Commands: new-artboard-dialog (Artboard..., in the menu where the dialogless New Artboard was, which stays as a command), artboard-from-group, frame-from-layers, and shapes-unite, shapes-subtract, shapes-intersect, shapes-exclude and shapes-merge under Layer > Combine Shapes after Arrange, enabled with two selected shape layers or one of two outlines (Merge also for one whose outlines carry an operation); all but the dialogs recordable.

## Lock Layers, Link Layers and Select Linked Layers, 27.5's sixth part · _v1.65.3 (engine/types.ts, engine/index.ts, io/project-io.ts, io/psd.ts, ui/layers.ts, ui/panels/layer-dialogs.ts, ui/actions.ts, styles/panels.css, app.ts; docs/MANUAL.md)

DEV_PLAN 27.5, sixth part, after Photoshop's Layer menu (Link Layers, Select Linked Layers, Lock Layers). The model: `Layer.link`, an id the layers linked together share. A link one layer holds alone links nothing, so nothing has to tidy links when layers are deleted, merged or flattened: whatever reads a link counts its holders. Engine: `withLinked(p)` is the selection plus every layer holding a link a selected layer holds. `groupMembers` takes it in place of the selection, so the Move tool's drag and free transform (`beginTransform`), its free distort (`beginDistort`) and the group box (`groupBox`) carry linked layers as they carry several selected ones; when one layer's unlinked, painted mask is targeted, the mask still moves alone. `nudge` moves them all. A linked layer outside the selection whose position is locked refuses the move with the lock's notice (`beginTransform`, `nudge`), since the person did not pick it; the selected layers keep the rule they had (the active layer's lock alone). `selectionLinked`: the selected layers all hold one link that another layer holds too, which makes Link Layers read Unlink Layers. `linkLayers()` gives the selected layers a new link or, when `selectionLinked`, takes theirs away, then drops any link left to one layer, as one Link Layers or Unlink Layers step. `selectLinkedLayers()` sets the selection to `withLinked`, the active layer kept, emitting as Select > All Layers does, not a step. Duplicates: Duplicate Layer and the panel's Alt-drag give the copies made together one new link per link copied (a map per operation), so copies of linked layers are linked to each other, and a lone copy to nothing, never to the layers they copy. `setLocks(patch, deep)`: `deep` adds the layers inside selected folders (Lock All Layers in Group).

Files: `serialize` writes `linkID` and `deserialize` reads it (a string, at most 120 characters); the wiki's Project-Format table gains the key. PSD: Photoshop keeps linked layers as a group number per layer record in image resource 1026, with resource 1072's flags saying whether each is on; ag-psd reads and writes them as `linkGroup` and `linkGroupEnabled`. `writePsdFile` numbers each link that two or more layers hold, from 1, and `readPsdFile` gives each enabled non-zero number a new link (`linkOf`), folders included.

The window: `LockLayersDialog` (layer-dialogs.ts) with Transparency, Image, Position and All, each ticked when every selected layer has it; OK sets all four on the selection through `setLocks`, deep for a folder, the dialog then titled Lock All Layers in Group. Commands: lock-layers (Mod+/, Photoshop's key; labelled Lock All Layers in Group... with a folder selected), link-layers (Link or Unlink Layers by `selectionLinked`; enabled for two or more selected, or a linked selection) and select-linked (enabled when a selected layer shares its link); in the Layer menu after Flip, and the last two in the layers' context menu after Create Clipping Mask. The Layers panel: each row gains `.cv-layer-linked`, the link icon, shown when another layer holds its link (the holders counted once per render, `links`), and `.cv-layer-locked`, the lock icon, `is-partial` and dimmed unless All is locked, each shown by its `hidden` attribute; the foot gains a Link Layers button first, wired by its `data-cmd`, whose tooltip and label follow the command's. Link Layers and Select Linked Layers are recordable. Align and Distribute still move only the selected layers.

Verified by scratch probes outside the repository, on a 300 by 200 document with 40 by 30 pixel layers A, B and C and a folder F holding D. Link Layers disabled with A alone, enabled with A and B, one Link Layers step giving both one link, the item and the foot button then reading Unlink Layers, the chain on A and B only. From A, Select Linked Layers selected A and B, A still active; a 5 px nudge moved A and B and not C, one Nudge step; a Move tool drag of (10, 15) moved both, one Transform Layers step. With B's position locked, a nudge and a drag from A were refused, the lock's notice shown, nothing moved. Unlink Layers removed both links and chains, one step, and undo restored them. A, B and C linked: after deleting C, A and B stayed linked; after deleting B too, A showed no chain, and Link Layers and Select Linked Layers were disabled. Duplicating A and B gave copies sharing a new link, the originals keeping theirs; duplicating A alone gave a copy whose link no other layer holds, no chain; an Alt-drag of A and B the same as the first. With A's painted mask unlinked and targeted, a drag moved the mask 10 px and neither layer. A project kept the links; a PSD written and read back had A, B and C linked and D and F not, with no notes. Lock Layers with A and C: titled so, four boxes unticked; Position and OK locked both, one Layer Locks step, their rows with the dimmed lock; reopened, Position ticked. With F selected: Lock All Layers in Group..., titled so; All locked F and D, full locks. Mod+/ opened the dialog. A recorded action held Link Layers and Select Linked Layers as command steps. The Layer menu lists Lock Layers... (Ctrl+/), Unlink Layers and Select Linked Layers between Flip and Merge Down; it scrolls within a 900 pixel window as it did before (1,162 pixels of rows in 890). Zero flash, under 6x CPU and network throttling after a hard reload: linking from the menu, unlinking and linking from the foot button changed only the chains' hidden attribute and the button's tooltip and label; the Lock Layers dialog one size from its first frame (320 by 237); its OK changed only the lock marks and the lock buttons' state; Select Linked Layers only a row's selection; every row kept, nothing shifted. tsc, the build, 194 unit tests; 112 engine tests passed, 3 failing on this machine as before. The whole browser suite from a freshly started dev server: 506 passed, 3 skipped, 23 failed, the 22 failing at 1.65.2 and the tiled paint suite's undo of tiles paged to disk, which read a tile still on disk after the undo; the tiled paint suite run three more times after, that test passed each time (the suite's one known failure aside), so it is taken as a race in the paging, not from this release.

## Layer Style complete, 27.5's fifth part · _v1.65.2 (ui/panels/style-dialogs.ts new; engine/types.ts, engine/renderer.ts, engine/style-extras.ts, engine/index.ts, engine/video-timeline.ts, io/project-io.ts, io/psd.ts, ui/panels/layer-style-dialog.ts, ui/layers.ts, ui/actions.ts, styles/panels.css, app.ts; docs/MANUAL.md)

DEV_PLAN 27.5, fifth part, after Photoshop's Layer Style submenu and dialog. The model: `BevelEffect.style` gains `stroke`, and optional `technique` (`chiselHard` or `chiselSoft`; absent is Smooth), `contour` (`BevelContour`: on or off, a contour id, a range of 0.01 to 1) and `texture` (`BevelTexture`: on or off, a pattern id, scale 0.01 to 10, depth -10 to 10, invert); `LayerEffects` gains `hidden`. `effectsActive` now means present and not hidden, so every path that draws (the renderer and its GPU parts, compose-float, the deep and colour-mode checks, the ORA writer's plain-layer test) leaves a hidden style out with no change of its own; the old test is `effectsPresent`, used wherever a style counts though hidden: Copy and Clear Layer Style, the fx badge, `setLayerEffects`, saving (`serialize`, the PSD writer) and `effectsFromData`'s answer, which now reads `hidden`, the technique, the contour and the texture, each held to its range. The bevel's height in `bevelMaps`, which now takes the coverage as floats and the layer's corner within the maps: Smooth as before, the blurred coverage; a chisel, `chiselHeight`, an even slope by each pixel's signed Euclidean distance from the half-coverage edge (`distanceSquared` from matting.ts, less half a pixel, positive inside): inner rising over Size from the edge, outer falling over Size outside it, emboss and pillow straddling it at half the size each side; Chisel Soft blurs that over an eighth of the size (`blur1`'s radius is half its reach). Then the Contour, `contourHeight`, the curve read at the height over its range and flat past it, `contour(min(h / range, 1))`; but a Smooth bevel's height is 0.5 at the edge, so an inner bevel shades only the upper half of it and an outer bevel the lower, and the curve taken over the whole height gave an inner bevel only the second half of a Cone: all shadow on the lit side, an inverted bevel, where a ridge is expected (Krita's PSD-compatible bevel, as remembered and not checked here, ramps an inner bevel from 0 at the edge). For Smooth inner, stroke and outer bevels the curve is taken over that half (`half`), the other half moved to meet it so nothing steps at the edge, which leaves Linear at 100 percent exactly as no contour; the chisels' heights already run 0 to 1 on their side and take the curve whole. Then the Texture, `textureHeight`: the pattern's luminance times its alpha, tiled from the layer's corner at its scale times the view's, added at depth over size, so a full step at 100 percent slopes as the bevel does at its depth. Stroke Emboss: the coverage is the first stroke that is on, its ring found as the strokes find theirs (`resizeMask` outward, inward or both by position), shaded inside it as an inner bevel; with no stroke on it draws nothing.

Create Layers: `FxPart` gains `name` and `kept`, kept meaning held to the silhouette (the overlays, satin, inner glow and shadow, an inside stroke and an inner bevel's two parts), and `effects()`'s callback carries both, each `lay` naming its part as Photoshop names the layers. `effectParts(..., exact)` skips the half-resolution fast path and the cache and, for a kept part, divides the silhouette's alpha back out (`unkeep`), since the new layer gets that alpha again from its clipping base: without it the soft edge of an ellipse at 70 percent opacity came out 41 levels off. `effectLayers(layer, doc)` gives those parts with the document's light in. `Engine.effectsToLayers()` refuses a clipped layer, a style that draws nothing, and an unkept part above when layers clip to this one (it would split their clipping group); parts below go below at their alpha times the layer's opacity; kept parts above clip to the layer at their alpha (the clip brings the opacity); unkept parts above stand above it at alpha times opacity; each blend comes from the part's operator (`lighter` as Linear Dodge); the layer's style is cleared; one Create Layers step. `effectsShown` (some layer's style draws) and `setAllEffectsHidden(hidden)`, one step over every layer with a style. `scaleEffects(k)`: the selected layers' styles through `scaledEffects` (style-extras.ts: sizes, distances and soften rounded to whole pixels; pattern, gradient and texture scales multiplied) and back through `effectsFromData`, which holds each to its limits, one step.

Files: `serialize` now carries a pattern used only by a bevel's texture, found while checking the texture's round trip (a pattern of one's own would have come back as Missing pattern). PSD: Stroke Emboss and the technique are read and written; a style switched off in Photoshop (`disabled`) opens hidden, where it was dropped with a note, and a hidden style is written `disabled`; a bevel's Contour or Texture is noted on export, and a PSD bevel using Photoshop's (`useShape`, `useTexture`) on import, the reader giving neither's settings. The video timeline's colour fade on a hidden style now starts from an empty style, found while auditing what reads `effects`: the clone kept `hidden`, so the fade's overlay would have been hidden with it.

The window: the Layer Style dialog's Bevel & Emboss gains Stroke Emboss, Technique, Contour (its shape and range) and Texture (its pattern, kept in place as the instance pickers are, scale, depth and invert). `show(focus)` drops `hidden` (editing a style shows it, as Photoshop's dialog does), turns the focused effect on, opens with that section's first control focused (the effect's checkbox, or Blending Options' Knockout) and scrolls the body so the section's first row is at its top, all in the task that opens it, so its first painted frame is already there; `SECTIONS` names each effect's first row. The focus matters: the dialog's first control is the global light's angle, which would sit scrolled out of sight while the arrow keys turned it. New `style-dialogs.ts`: `GlobalLightDialog` (Angle and Altitude, to `setGlobalLight`) and `ScaleEffectsDialog` (Scale, 1 to 1000 percent). app.ts: style-blending and the ten style-<effect> items, global-light, create-layers, hide-all-effects (labelled Hide or Show All Effects by `effectsShown`) and scale-effects; Copy and Clear Layer Style enabled by `effectsPresent`; the Layer menu's Layer Style submenu in Photoshop's order (the layers' context menu keeps its Layer Style item). The Layers panel's fx badge shows for any style and takes `is-off`, dimmed and struck out, while hidden. Create Layers and Hide All Effects are recordable; like the other toggles recorded, a Hide All Effects step replays as a toggle. The manual's new sentence first said "opens the Layer Style dialog", and the manual search, which ranks sections by word frequency, then answered "open a very large picture" from Painting and retouching rather than Getting started; it says "shows".

Verified by scratch probes outside the repository, on a 120 by 80 grey square at (60, 40) lit from the left at 30 degrees, along a row across its left edge: Smooth at size 12 shades from 253 down to 121 over x 60 to 78; Chisel Hard lights x 60 to 71 evenly (254), 211 at 72 and the flat top (120) from 73; Chisel Soft softens that line (240, 218, 188, 159, 137, then 120 by 79). Contour: Linear at 100 percent equals no contour pixel for pixel; Cone a ridge, lit at x 60 to 63 and shaded at 65 to 71, back up to 120; Linear at 50 percent the slope halved; on an outer bevel Cone's ridge lies outside (shaded at 56 to 59) with no line at the edge; Chisel Hard and Emboss take the curve whole. Texture: the checker at 400 percent depth lit and shaded its cells' edges across the flat top (171 and 0 where the plain top is 120). Stroke Emboss: nothing without a stroke; with an 8 px outside stroke, the ring at x 52 to 59 shaded (220 down to 0) and the layer's pixels left at 120. A project kept Stroke Emboss, Chisel Soft, a Ring contour at 40 percent and an inverted checker texture at 200 and -150 percent; a PSD kept Stroke Emboss and Chisel Soft, its export noting the Contour and Texture. A pattern of one's own used only as a texture went into the project's patterns, and not with the texture off. Create Layers on the square with ten effects at once: Drop Shadow (Multiply, 0.8), Outer Glow (Screen, 0.6) and Outer Stroke below; Pattern, Gradient and Color Fill, Satin, Inner Glow, Inner Shadow and the Inner Bevel's Highlights and Shadows clipped above; the picture unchanged (largest difference 0), one step, undone exactly. An outer bevel and a center stroke stood above, unclipped, the picture unchanged; on a soft-edged ellipse at 70 percent opacity three styles came out within 2, 1 and 1 levels. Hide All Effects: one step, the item then reading Show All Effects, Copy enabled and Create Layers disabled, the badge shown with `is-off`; a project and a PSD kept it hidden; Show All Effects gave the picture back exactly. Scale Effects at 200 percent: distance 5 to 10, size 4 to 8, stroke 3 to 6, bevel 12 to 24 and soften 2 to 4, pattern scale 1 to 2, one step. Global Light: the dialog at 120 and 30, then 45 and 60 set as one step. The items for Satin, Bevel & Emboss and Drop Shadow opened with that row at the top of the dialog and its box ticked, Blending Options at its note, Cancel leaving no style. The video timeline: a hidden drop shadow under a Fade With Black gave the fade's overlay at 0.8 at frame 0 and no shadow; shown, both. Zero flash, under 6x CPU and network throttling after a hard reload, each from the menus: Hide and Show All Effects changed only the badge's class; Create Layers kept both rows and added four, and undo removed them; Satin opened at its row from its first frame (scrolled 2105 throughout), its checkbox focused, and Blending Options at 72 on Knockout; the Global Light and Scale Layer Effects dialogs kept one size from their first frame; nothing shifted. tsc, the build, 194 unit tests; 112 engine tests passed, 3 failing on this machine as before (the README's line counts brought up to date first). The whole browser suite from a freshly started dev server: 507 passed, 3 skipped, 22 failed, the same 22 as at 1.65.1. After the contour change, the effect instances, GPU styles, layer fill, layer style depth, offered options, preferences, menus and PSD suites from a fresh server: 20 passed and the 2 known failures; after the manual's rewording, the Help suite and three style suites: 10 passed.

## Load and Save Selection with alpha channels, 27.5's fourth part; remove_background over MCP · _v1.65.1 (engine/alphas.ts and ui/panels/selection-dialogs.ts new; engine/types.ts, engine/index.ts, engine/history.ts, io/project-io.ts, ui/channels.ts, ui/stage.ts, ui/panels/background-panel.ts, ui/actions.ts, styles/panels.css, app.ts; docs/MANUAL.md, docs/AGENT_EVALS.md, docs/LOCAL.md)

DEV_PLAN 27.5, fourth part, after Photoshop's two dialogs. The document holds its alpha channels as `Doc.alphas`, each an `AlphaChannel` of id, name and `mask`: a `SelectionMask`, null when the channel selects nothing. A save keeps the selection's own immutable mask and a combine makes a new one, and every change replaces the doc, so undo and redo carry the channels with nothing added to the history; `History.retained` counts the bytes of channels the current document no longer holds, and no longer counts a past selection that lives on as a channel. Engine: `alphaDocuments()` is this document, then the open ones of its size. `saveSelection({ doc, channel, name, op })`, after `settle`: refused with a notice in a document past one canvas; with no channel, a new one named as given or "Alpha N", the first number free (`nextAlphaName` in the new `alphas.ts`); into a channel, `SelectionMask.combine`, formvis's own selection arithmetic (its subtract multiplies by the inverse, as the selection tools' does), an empty channel taking the selection for replace and add and staying empty otherwise; one step in the target document through `editOn`, so another document's history takes it. `loadSelection({ doc, channel }, invert, mode)`: an alpha channel's mask, or `coverage` of that document's active layer (its pixels' alpha at their place, or its mask's white at the mask's placement; an adjustment layer, or a mask with no pixels, covers the canvas), inverted over the canvas when asked, through `applySelection` as one Load Selection step; nothing to load says "That channel selects nothing." `deleteAlpha` and `renameAlpha` are Delete Channel and Rename Channel. The view: `alphaViews` per document, `shownAlphas` and `showAlpha(id, on)` (null hides all), emitting overlay, never a step. The canvas operations carry them: `alphasMoved` turns, flips or shifts each mask for Rotate, Flip and every `resizeCanvas` (Canvas Size, Crop, Trim, Reveal All, Generative Expand); `alphasRedrawn` draws each anew for Image Size (scaled, smoothed unless Nearest), Straighten (turned about the frame's centre before the crop, as the layers turn) and Perspective Crop (each mask warped by `warpRaster` as a mask through the same homography). Project file: `serialize` writes each channel as `alpha-N.png`, a grey picture the canvas's size (`alphaGrey`), and `manifest.alphas` its id, name and file; `deserialize` reads up to 100, leaving out one whose file is missing, unreadable or of another size, and giving a repeated id a new one. The engine service keeps any picture in `images/`, so it needed no change; the wiki's Project-Format table gains the key.

The window: `SaveSelectionDialog` (Document, the open ones of this size; Channel, New or one of that document's; Name, for a new one; Operation, its first item reading New Channel, disabled, or Replace Channel) and `LoadSelectionDialog` (Document; Channel, from `loadSources`: the alpha channels, then "<layer> Transparency" for a layer with pixels or an adjustment layer and "<layer> Mask" for one with a mask; Invert; Operation, Add, Subtract and Intersect disabled with nothing selected); their selects kept by `syncOptions`, changing only what differs. Commands: load-selection (enabled when any of those documents has something to load), save-selection and save-selection-channel (the last recordable), Load and Save Selection in the Select menu beside Make Selection from Path, which keeps the menu within a 900 pixel window, now opened from its top. The Channels panel: a second row list, `.cv-ch-alphas`, patched by `syncAlphas` with `patchList` from `apply`, so every event that redraws the panel keeps it; each row is the colour rows' eye, thumbnail and name, with a delete button. Its thumbnail is drawn when the row is made and redrawn in place only when its mask or the canvas size changes (`drawn`), so a new row never shows an empty box. A click shows the channel (never hides it, so a double-click to rename does not flicker the canvas), the eye toggles it, clicking the composite row hides them all; Cmd- or Ctrl-click loads it with Photoshop's modifiers (`clickMode`: Shift adds, Alt subtracts, both intersect), which the colour rows now take too; a double-click renames in place, as the Paths panel does. Its foot holds Load Selection and Save Selection as Channel, wired by their `data-cmd` like other panel buttons. `apply` now walks `.cv-ch-row[data-ch]`, the colour rows alone. The stage draws each shown channel as Quick Mask's tint, red at half strength where it selects nothing (`alphaTint`, cached per channel object), under the ants. Found while looking at the panel: since 1.54.2 its CMYK rows, and since 1.56.4 its Lab rows, showed in RGB documents, the rows' `display: flex` overriding their `hidden` attribute; `.cv-ch-row[hidden]` now hides them.

From the bug bounty of 6 and 7 October 2026 (its 0004 and 0005, each made again by hand on this code): the agents' `remove_background` awaited `removeBackground('auto')`, which found the subject and then opened the Remove Background dialog to wait for OK, so the agent was told the background was removed while the layer had no mask and the dialog sat open. `removeBackground(method, agent)` now, for an agent, lays the mask down through `BackgroundPanel.applyNow` (the dialog's current settings, `matte` at full size and `applySubjectMask`, the same step as OK, the dialog never opened) and throws what fails so the bridge answers it as an error: no pixels on the active layer, the layer changed while the model ran, or the person's own dialog open, which is left as it was. The menu commands still open the dialog. The manual, AGENT_EVALS and LOCAL said agents get 39 tools; tools/list gives 50, and the manual's list names the video timeline.

Verified by scratch probes outside the repository. Engine: Save Selection made Alpha 1 of the 40 by 30 selection, one step, the selection kept; a name trimmed; Add, Subtract, Intersect and Replace into it gave 2,600, 1,100, 100 and 1,500 pixels where they should, each undone; an Intersect that met nothing left an empty channel; Load Selection gave the 1,200 pixels back, inverted 18,800, and added to, subtracted from and intersected with a selection 11,200, 2,400 and 600; a 30 by 20 layer's transparency 600 pixels where it lies, its mask's 10 by 10 white 100, an empty layer nothing with its notice; the channel followed Rotate 90 degrees, both flips, Canvas Size, Crop, Image Size at twice, Straighten at 45 degrees and two perspective crops, each exactly where the canvas took it, and came back on undo; Rename and Delete each one step, a rename to the same name none; another open document of the same size took a saved channel into its own history and gave it back, and one of another size was not offered; a project serialized and read back kept the channel's id, name and pixels, and a manifest naming a missing file and a channel with no file read the rest. In the window: the panel's foot buttons enabled with their names; the footer's save adding a row whose thumbnail showed the channel white on black; a click showing the red tint outside the channel and the eye hiding it; the RGB row hiding all; Cmd-click, Cmd+Shift and Cmd+Alt loading, adding and subtracting; renaming in place, Escape keeping the name, Enter renaming as one step; the Save Selection dialog's fields as described, Add into Sky and a new Ring by name; the Load Selection dialog listing Sky, Ring and Background Transparency with three operations disabled, Ring inverted loaded; Delete and its undo. The Select menu's two items in place, the menu 885 pixels from top 4, unscrolled. Zero flash, under 6x CPU and network throttling after a hard reload: each save added one row, its thumbnail drawn before it was first painted, every other row kept; show, eye, the RGB row and Cmd-click changed only the rows' and eyes' classes; renaming swapped the name for its field and back; a save into an existing channel, the Load dialog and a canvas rotation changed no node; delete and undo removed and added one row; shifts only after input. Over MCP: remove_background on an opened photo answered in 14.5 s with the layer masked (subject 254, corner 0), one Remove Background step, no dialog or preview left; with the person's dialog open the agent was told and nothing applied; on an empty layer it was told to choose a pixel layer. tsc, the build, 194 unit tests; 112 engine tests passed, 3 failing on this machine as before. The channels, menus, selection tools, crop, perspective crop, colour modes, session, guides, notes, shortcut and layout suites passed (33) before the fixes, and the MCP agents, agent consent and Select Subject suites (5) after them. The whole browser suite from a freshly started dev server: 507 passed, 3 skipped, 22 failed, each among the 23 failing at 1.65.0 (a docking test of those passed this time).

## The Select menu's Reselect, Grow, Similar, Transform Selection, Convert to Shape, Find and Isolate Layers, 27.5's third part · _v1.65.0 (engine/index.ts, engine/selection.ts, ui/layers.ts, ui/panels/layer-dialogs.ts, ui/actions.ts, app.ts; docs/MANUAL.md)

DEV_PLAN 27.5, third part, after Photoshop's Select menu. Reselect: `applySelection` records, per document (`lastSelections`, a WeakMap), the selection a step replaced with none, and `reselect` applies it again as a step named Reselect, enabled (`canReselect`) only while nothing is selected. It takes no key: Photoshop's Shift+Ctrl+D is the key the Keyboard Shortcuts test binds to Duplicate as a free one. Grow and Similar (`growSelection(contiguous)`): the range of each channel and of alpha over the pixels at least half selected, widened by the Magic Wand's Tolerance; Grow floods four-connected from the selection into pixels inside that range, Similar takes every such pixel; the pixels are read as the Magic Wand reads them (the active layer drawn at document size, or the whole picture with Sample All Layers), the result hard-edged then anti-aliased when the wand is. Transform Selection of the outline (`beginOutlineTransform`): the floating-selection machinery that carries selected pixels (`floatSel`) now has an `outline` flag; the selection is drawn into a temporary layer, Selection Outline, at opacity 0 above the active one, so the Move tool's handles, the Properties fields and `floatingOutline`'s live ants all work on it unchanged, while the source layer's pixels are not cut (the render override is skipped). `commitSelectionTransform` draws the selection through the outline's transform into a new selection, removes the temporary layer and closes the step; unchanged, or with Escape, the step is aborted (`restoreSelectionTransform`, its focus now null when no layer was active). Convert to Shape (`selectionToShape`): `traceOutline` takes an optional sink with Path2D's moveTo, lineTo, closePath and rect, so the ants' tracer also gives the loops as points, each run of the pixel staircase a corner; each loop is simplified within 1.5 px (`simplify`), points turning by more than about 51 degrees kept as corners and the rest smoothed (`smoothAnchors`), and filled by the non-zero rule, the tracer's holes running against its outer loops so they cut; a shape layer in the foreground colour, one step. Find Layers (`findLayers`, through `FindLayersDialog`): names holding the text in any case, top first, selected and their folders opened; none found says so. Isolate Layers: the Layers panel keeps, per document, the layers selected when it was chosen (`isolation`), listing them with the folders holding them and what isolated folders hold; choosing it again lists all, and it ends by itself once none of its layers is left; the menu item shows it checked. Reselect, Grow, Similar and Convert to Shape are recordable. Load and Save Selection need the document's alpha channels and come next.

Verified by scratch probes outside the repository. Engine, through the commands: Reselect disabled with a selection, enabled after Deselect, the 40 by 30 rectangle back exactly as one step, disabled again; Grow from a 20 by 20 square inside a red disc of radius 50 selecting the disc (7,740 pixels, its box 20 to 119 by 50 to 149) and not a second, slightly different red disc, Similar both (12,633 pixels); Transform Selection with the temporary layer above the active one and the ants' matrix following a move of 100 px, the selection moved to x 110 to 149 with the picture unchanged pixel for pixel, one step, undone exactly, a resize to 80 by 60 giving 4,800 pixels, Escape restoring the rectangle and leaving no layer; Convert to Shape giving a rectangle four corner points in the foreground colour, an ellipse sixteen smooth points, a ring two loops with its middle transparent and the ring opaque; Find Layers finding Sky and sky copy for "SKY", the higher active, and nothing for "water" with its notice; Isolate Layers listing the two selected layers, checked, then all four again. In the window: the Select menu in Photoshop's order with its keys, 825 pixels tall from its button, inside a 900 pixel window. Zero flash, under 6x CPU and network throttling after a hard reload, each command from the menus (Deselect, Reselect, Grow, Transform Selection and its Escape, Convert to Shape, Isolate Layers on and off, Find Layers through its dialog): no Layers panel row that stayed was rebuilt, nothing shifted, the dialog one box from its first frame. tsc, the build, 194 unit tests; 112 engine tests passed, 3 failing on this machine as before. The whole browser suite from a freshly started dev server: 506 passed, 3 skipped, 23 failed, the same 23 as at 1.64.8, each failing as before or for this machine.

## Layer Mask, Mask All Objects, Matting and Rasterize, 27.5's second part · _v1.64.9 (engine/matting.ts and ui/panels/matting-dialog.ts new; engine/index.ts, io/api.ts, ui/actions.ts, app.ts; docs/MANUAL.md)

DEV_PLAN 27.5, second part. Layer Mask takes Photoshop's five ways to add a mask: `addMask(hide, fromSelection)` gains its second argument, so Reveal All and Hide All (`mask-reveal-all`, `mask-hide-all`) ignore a selection where the Layers panel's button, `add-mask`, still uses it; Reveal Selection and Hide Selection need one; the selection stays, as the button leaves it. From Transparency (`maskFromTransparency`): `alphaToMask` in the new `matting.ts` gives the layer's alpha as a mask (white at that alpha, the house form of a mask) and its pixels opaque, both new rasters, so the step's snapshot keeps the old ones; the picture is unchanged and the mask becomes the target. Delete, Apply, Enable and Link were there already. Matting (`matting(kind, width, amount, radius)`, through `regionEdit` with no region, so the whole layer and its patches, declined with a notice while the mask is targeted): Defringe and Remove Black and White Matte, as Photoshop's. Defringe: visible pixels within the width of transparency (alpha 2 or less), by exact Euclidean distance (`distanceSquared`, Meijster's two-pass transform), take the mean colour of their eight neighbours already settled, starting from the pixels further in and growing outward a ring of whole-pixel distance at a time; alpha is kept. Remove Black Matte divides a partly transparent pixel's colour by its alpha; White Matte first takes away the white it was blended with. Color Decontaminate runs Select and Mask's `decontaminate` with the layer's enabled mask, drawn into the layer's pixels, or else its alpha, the radius as its scale over six. The Matting dialog (`MattingDialog`) asks Defringe's width (1 to 200 px) or Decontaminate's amount (0 to 100) and radius (1 to 100 px), keeping the last values; its rows are hidden before it opens. ## The Filter Gallery and its Artistic effects · _v1.64.5 (engine/filters-lib/gallery-fx.ts, fx-artistic.ts, filter-gallery.ts and ui/panels/gallery-view.ts new; engine/filter-library.ts, engine/index.ts, ui/panels/filter-panel.ts, styles/dialogs.css, app.ts)

DEV_PLAN 27.4, second part. The Filter Gallery is one library filter, `filterGallery`, whose single parameter is the stack: a new parameter kind, `effects`, holding effect layers `{filter, values, visible}` (`LibEffect`, now one of the `LibValue`s). The parameter carries its own sanitizer, `clean`, handed the library's `sane` so each effect's values are checked as any filter's are; that keeps the gallery's catalogue out of `filter-library.ts` and its imports one way. The sanitizer takes an effect by key or by name, its values from `values`, from `params` or beside `filter`, keeps at most 64 layers and drops unknown ones; no stack at all becomes one Colored Pencil layer. Being a library filter, the gallery takes the Filter dialog's whole apply path: smart filters, actions, Last Filter, Fade, the worker, bands (its reach is the sum of its shown effects' reaches) and agents. `LibFilter` gains `width` (the dialog's width while it shows that filter), `ownPreview` (the filter previews inside its dialog, so the Filter dialog skips the canvas preview and hides its Preview check box) and `invalid` (a reason the settings cannot apply, given as the notice and refusing the apply in `missingImage`: an empty stack lists the keys, a stack with every layer hidden says so). Each effect paints a `Plate`: the window's colour, straight and in floats from 0 to 1, with the alpha kept aside, in the image's own pixels, where the window lies in the document, the frame's centre and the swatches; sizes given in document pixels are multiplied by the preview's scale, and every grain, stroke, texture and cell is a function of document coordinates measured from the canvas's origin, so bands and previews draw the same pattern. Under partly or wholly transparent pixels the colour is that of what lies around them, so effects that read neighbours do not pull in black. An effect declares how far it reads (`reach`), the sum of its blurs' three deviations, its runs' half lengths and its moves; nothing reads the window as a whole, so the gallery runs in bands. `gallery-fx.ts` holds the shared operators: a Gaussian exact to a deviation of 2.5 and three box passes beyond (`soften`), running means along rows, columns and either diagonal (`streak`), Sobel slopes, Kuwahara smoothing over box means (`flatten`), unsharp masking, positional grain, value noise and its octaves, stroke textures made from grain softened and run along a direction and rescaled to one spread whatever their sizes (`noiseField`, `strokesOf`), relief shading of the procedural surfaces (canvas, brick, burlap, sandstone) lit from the eight directions (`texturize`, supersampled when a preview shrinks them), jittered cells with each point's distance to its cell's border (`Cells`) and drawing between the ink and paper colours. The Artistic folder: Colored Pencil, Cutout, Dry Brush, Film Grain, Fresco, Neon Glow, Paint Daubs, Palette Knife, Plastic Wrap, Poster Edges, Rough Pastels, Smudge Stick, Sponge, Underpainting and Watercolor, with Photoshop's parameters, ranges and defaults; the foreground and background colours the dialog captures stand for Photoshop's (Colored Pencil's paper, Neon Glow's shades). The section, `GalleryView`: a preview pane drawn from the target's pixels through `Engine.targetCrop` (a region of the layer or its mask at a scale, with that region's frame) and `targetSize`, which, unlike `paintable`, never ask to rasterize or post a notice; at Fit in View or 25 to 200 percent, rendered in the worker at the device's pixel ratio (capped at 2) with an apron of the stack's reach at that scale, and dragged by pointer to pan. The folders hold a thumbnail per effect, made on the main thread a few per frame from a quarter-width crop of the layer's middle at 160 by 112. Settings sections are built when an effect is first chosen and kept, one shown at a time. The effect layers are a list patched in place, top first, with New (a copy above the selected), Delete, Move Up, Move Down and the eye. The four areas have fixed sizes, so nothing in the dialog moves as effects, layers and settings change; the preview and thumbnails are cleared while the dialog is hidden and drawn once ready. Filter > Filter Gallery... heads the dialog filters after Last Filter.

Verified by scratch probes outside the repository. Engine: each of the 15 at its defaults, on a 480 by 320 scene, changed 50 (Smudge Stick, its darker half) to 100 percent of the pixels, kept every alpha and repeated byte for byte; on a 300 by 400 scene, 48-row bands with the declared apron matched the whole run exactly for all 15; a half-scale run against the full result reduced differed by a mean of 0.1 to 9.2 levels, and by 12 to 14 for Colored Pencil, Sponge and Rough Pastels (their fine strokes, pores and relief alias at half scale); warm on 3 MP, 0.37 seconds (Smudge Stick) to 1.7 (Underpainting). ## Distort and Pixelate; the filter's frame · _v1.64.1 (engine/filters-lib/distort.ts and pixelate.ts new; engine/filter-library.ts, filters-lib/shared.ts, other.ts, video.ts, noise.ts, engine/filter-jobs.ts, filter-worker.ts, engine/index.ts, ui/panels/filter-panel.ts, app.ts)

DEV_PLAN 27.2: nine Distort filters (Displace, Pinch, Polar Coordinates, Ripple, Shear, Spherize, Twirl, Wave, ZigZag) and seven Pixelate filters (Color Halftone, Crystallize, Facet, Fragment, Mezzotint, Mosaic, Pointillize). Photoshop centres a distortion on the selection's bounds, or the canvas without one, and leaves pixels outside them alone; a filter in formvis sees the whole layer, so it needs to be told that rectangle. That is the frame: `LibFrame` (`area`, the selection's bounds or the canvas, and `canvas`), in the pixels of exactly the image the filter receives, made by `Engine.filterFrame` from the target's placement and handed to every run: the scaled preview (`previewImageEdit`, scaled with the preview and shifted by its growth), the whole-layer paths (`applyImageEdit`'s region, `grown`, and `applyImageEditAsync`, where `sourceForEdit` now also returns the placement of the pixels it made, the layer or the layer grown to the canvas), and the worker (`FilterJob.frame`). Runs without one (bands, smart filters, the smart object being its own picture) take the whole image. `LibContext` gains `area`, `canvas` and the swatches `fg` and `bg` (Pointillize's dots sit on the background colour, as in Photoshop); the swatches are captured in the settings when the dialog opens or a recorded filter runs (`completed`), so a smart filter re-renders and an action replays with the colours it was made with. Two parameter kinds join the library: `seed` (Wave's Randomize, a stored number, so an action replays the same waves) and `image` (Displace's map: an open document chosen in the dialog, captured by `Engine.mapImage` as its red and green channels at most 256 pixels a side over mid grey, base64 in the settings, so the map travels with actions and smart filters; `libValues` checks its sizes; agents name a document and `completed` captures it). A filter that needs an image and has none is refused with the reason (an engine notice, which agents receive as their error) and the dialog stays open. The remap (`remap`) is a backward map sampled bilinearly in premultiplied alpha with Photoshop's undefined-area choices, folding taps into the area; Wave's sideways shift depends on the row only and its vertical shift on the column only, so each is summed once per row and column (Wave allows 999 generators, which per pixel would be far too slow). Color Halftone caches each screen cell's mean, and a dot covers the share of its cell that mean asks for (`DOTS`, the radius whose circle, less the caps the cell's sides cut off past the inscribed circle, covers that share). Facet takes the commonest colour family (16 levels a channel) within its radius and that family's mean colour, so like colours settle into flat facets. Position-bound filters (all of Distort, Color Halftone, Crystallize, Mezzotint, Mosaic, Pointillize) declare no reach and run whole; Facet and Fragment are local and run in bands. Using the frame, Offset now wraps within the selection or the canvas (it wrapped around the layer, as 1.64.0 noted), and De-Interlace's fields and Reduce Noise's JPEG grid follow the canvas's origin. Found while checking smart filters: the Filter dialog would not open on a smart object (the engine's `targetImage`, through `paintable`, asked to rasterize it), so filters with a dialog could not become smart filters from the menu, and editing one from the Smart Filters window failed the same way; `show` skips that check for a smart target, which shows no live preview (its Preview box unchecked and disabled, as editing a smart filter already worked), and Shake Reduction's estimate is skipped there. A comment on a line this release changed (`filterPeak(kind) + 2`, "its peak, and the copies to and from the worker (1.61.1)") moved here.

Verified by scratch probes outside the repository. Each kernel against a reference: Twirl at 90 degrees moves a point at radius 20 exactly where the formula puts it, the centre and corners kept; Pinch within 1 level of the formula; Spherize exact, and Horizontal only keeps rows; Ripple exact; Polar Coordinates keeps a flat colour to the corners, its bottom row stretched into them; a one-generator square Wave shifts rows by exactly 5 pixels; ZigZag at 0 changes nothing; Shear's middle row moves a quarter of the width and wraps; Displace with a mid-grey map stays within 1 level, a white map at 100 percent moves exactly 128 pixels, no map changes nothing; Color Halftone keeps white white, black black and grey at 127 to 130; Crystallize keeps a flat colour, and a gradient's mean at 127.5; Facet keeps a flat picture and a hard edge; Fragment puts four quarter-strength copies 4 pixels out; Mezzotint gives only 0 and 255 with grey's mean at 126 to 130 across its types; Mosaic's cells are their block's mean; Pointillize leaves background between dots; Offset and Twirl inside a frame leave everything outside it alone; every filter runs at half scale; sanitised seeds, maps and colours. In the app: all 16 commands with their dialogs and fields, each one step undone exactly (Shear's straight default changes nothing); Twirl inside an 80 by 60 selection changes 2,819 pixels inside and none outside, previewed within 0.4 s; Displace lists the open documents, refuses OK without a map with its reason and stays open, applies with one; an action of Twirl, Wave (Randomize), Mosaic and Facet replayed through the Actions window equal byte for byte; on a smart object Gaussian Blur and Pinch opened and became smart filters, and Edit reopened Twirl with its value and changed it; worker and main-thread results equal byte for byte with a frame; Facet and Fragment banded equal to whole; in a 16-bit document Twirl, Mosaic, Facet and Crystallize each one step changing its channels; agents applied Twirl, Mosaic, Facet, Pointillize, Wave and Displace by a document's name, and Displace without a map answered with its reason. The 1.64.0 checks rerun: every bandable filter banded equal to whole, the action replay equal. Zero flash, under 6x CPU and network throttling after a hard reload: Wave, Displace and Color Halftone opened, reopened and edited, each dialog's box the same in every frame; Randomize and the sliders changed no nodes; a document opened between two Displace dialogs added one option in place before the dialog showed; the only layout shift the status bar's known 0.0008 before any dialog. tsc, the build, 194 unit tests; 112 engine tests passed, 3 failing on this machine (no EXR codec; LaMa not downloaded; the SAM device read as onnx); 52 browser tests across filters, offered options, menus, panel and native menus, smart and linked smart objects, MCP agents, agent editing, the Blur Gallery, Develop, Camera Raw and adjustments: 49 passed, 3 failing on this machine as at 1.64.0 (OpenEXR export, Image > Mode's list, generative fill without LaMa).

## The filter library and 21 filters · _v1.64.0 (engine/filter-library.ts and engine/filters-lib/ new; engine/index.ts, engine/filter-jobs.ts, engine/filter-worker.ts, ui/panels/filter-panel.ts, ui/panels/controls.ts, ui/panels/actions-dialogs.ts, ui/actions.ts, styles/dialogs.css, app.ts)

DEV_PLAN 27.1, the first stage of Phase 27 (filter and editing parity; the itemized inventory is in the planning sidecar). A filter is now declared rather than wired by hand: `filter-library.ts` holds `LIBRARY`, each `LibFilter` an id, a label, its menu group, its parameters (a range with the slider's span and a typed `limit` past it, a select, a check, or a square integer matrix), `reach` (how far its effect reaches at a given scale, or null when its result depends on where a pixel is, so it never runs in bands), `grows` (whether its effect spills past the layer, so a layer without a selection grows as it does for Gaussian Blur) and `run` on ImageData. Everything else reads the registry: the filter panel builds a dialog section from the parameters the first time a filter opens (`libSection`, inserted before the dialog opens and reused after), the worker runs `runLib`, `bandApron` and `filterMargin` take `libApron` and `libMargin`, the commands and the Filter submenus are generated from it (alphabetical within a group, as Photoshop lists them), so a later filter is one more entry. Settings live under `settings.lib[kind]`; `libValues` holds every stored value to its parameter (a range to its limit, an unknown choice to its default, a matrix cell to an integer in range), so settings from actions, smart filters and agents never reach a kernel out of range, and `settingsOf` keeps only the applied filter's entry in what actions and smart filters store. The kernels (`filters-lib/`): Shape Blur's kernel is its shape's pixels as runs along each row (`spans`), each run summed from running row totals (`spanMean`), so a wide shape costs its height rather than its area; Smart Blur averages the pixels within its radius whose brightness is within the threshold; Median and Dust & Scratches slide a 256-level histogram along each row; Reduce Noise smooths brightness with a sampled bilateral filter in YCbCr (rings of taps, a range that narrows as Preserve Details rises), blurs the chroma planes and sharpens brightness back with an unsharp mask; High Pass is each colour's difference from its exact Gaussian around mid grey; Maximum and Minimum keep a running queue of candidates along each line, so any radius costs the same, Roundness the best of eight rectangles that make a disc; then Offset, Custom's 5 by 5 kernel, HSB/HSL, De-Interlace's fields and NTSC Colors' chroma limit in YIQ (the composite signal kept between -0.1 and 1.0). The blurs work in premultiplied alpha so colours do not darken where opaque meets transparent. Blur, Blur More and the three Sharpen filters use an exact separable Gaussian (`exactGaussian`, `unsharpExact`): formvis's three-box Gaussian does nothing below a sigma of about 0.7, which had left Sharpen changing nothing. Average is an engine operation (`averageFill`), not a library filter: a filter sees the whole layer and the selection only blends its result, but Average needs the selection's own average, weighted by its coverage and alpha. Reduce Noise's JPEG deblocking follows the picture's 8-pixel grid, so with it on the filter's reach is null (the whole layer at once, never bands, whose origins need not fall on the grid). Actions: `filter-average` joins RECORDABLE (it changes the document at once, with no dialog); the Dialog toggle shows only on steps whose filter has a dialog (`asks`). The agent bridge's `applyFilter` wraps a library filter's flat settings as `{ lib: { [kind]: settings } }` and runs `average` through `averageFill`. `matrixRow` is Custom's 5 by 5 grid of number inputs, each labelled by its row and column.

Verified by scratch probes outside the repository. Each kernel against a reference: a box-blurred dot gives 10 throughout its radius; Median removes salt; Dust & Scratches at threshold 255 keeps everything; Maximum and Minimum square and round; Offset wrapping, transparent and repeating; Custom's identity unchanged, and doubled plus 10; HSB and HSL there and back within 3 levels; High Pass of a flat image 128; NTSC red 255,0,0 to 189,28,28; De-Interlace both ways; Smart Blur keeps edges, and Edge Only; Shape Blur's circle 81 taps and square 121 at radius 5; Reduce Noise's deviation 17.2 to 10.0; stored values clamped. In the app: every command's label and state; each filter without settings one step, undone exactly; every dialog's fields, OK one step, Cancel none; the live preview; Average in a selection across red and blue 128,0,128 inside and the outside untouched; smart filters storing only their own settings; an action of Median 2, Box Blur 3, Sharpen and Average recorded, undone and played through the Actions window, equal byte for byte; every bandable library filter on a 300 by 1,100 layer forced into bands equal to the whole-layer result byte for byte, growing ones included; on a 120 MP tiled layer Median and High Pass through `bandedFilterTiled` equal to the direct run, their undo streamed back exactly; in 16 and 32-bit, Lab and CMYK documents Median, Sharpen, Box Blur, HSB/HSL and NTSC Colors each one step that changes the document's own channels, as Lens Blur does; the agent tool applying Box Blur and Average. Zero flash, under 6x CPU and network throttling after a hard reload: the Box Blur, Custom and Shape Blur dialogs opened, reopened and edited; each dialog's box the same in every frame from opening; sliders, matrix cells and the shape choice changed values in place, no rows rebuilt, each section built once before its dialog first opens; the only layout shift, 0.0008, was the status bar's hint as the document opened, before any dialog (noted, not from this change). tsc, the build, 194 unit tests; 111 engine tests passed, 4 failing on this machine (no EXR codec in its OpenCV; the LaMa and SAM ONNX models not downloaded; the SAM device read as onnx); the browser suites for filters, menus, native and panel menus, offered options, the tiled filter, MCP agents, agent editing, smart objects and large documents 18 passed, 3 opt-in skipped, 4 failing on this machine (Export OpenEXR, the codec again; Image > Mode's list, which expects five modes and has had six since Lab at 1.56.4; the tiled filter test, whose 120 MP document fits one canvas on this 8 GB machine, and the same path passed by probe with the budget lowered; generative fill without LaMa).

## 600 MP edited whole: four faults found and fixed · _v1.63.0 (engine/tiled.ts, engine/stroke.ts, engine/index.ts, io/api.ts, app.ts; e2e/test_large_document.py)

DEV_PLAN 26.6h, closing M5. e2e/test_600_megapixels_edited_whole (opt-in, FORMVIS_LARGE=1): fine stripes on all 150 tiles of a 30,000 by 20,000 document, a brush stroke across several tiles on a second layer (checked whole: no stroke-stopped notice, paint at its end), a Gaussian Blur over the whole background, undone and redone, saved to the library, closed, reopened, exported; the same recorded pixels checked exactly at every step. It found four faults, each fixed and measured. (1) A tile sent to disk kept its memory: the browser records a drawImage and keeps a snapshot of its source until the canvas next draws for real, so each preview held its whole 16 MB tile; the page was killed by the system at 2.28 GB while striping. The preview (and the GPU's reduced copy, `levelOf`) is now drawn at once by a one-pixel read: six rows of paging ended at 625 to 708 MB instead of 1,660 to 1,869 (in isolation, paging with a fake store grew the same way, so it was not the network). (2) Uploads of typed arrays stayed in the page past garbage collection (30 uploads of 16 MB kept about 190 MB, measured four ways in fresh browsers: Uint8Array and ArrayBuffer kept it, a Blob by fetch or XMLHttpRequest did not): `undoPut` and `bandsPut` send Blobs. (3) A stroke on a giant layer grew its window by half the stroke's size again on every side, several picture-sized copies for a long stroke (the first run's diagonal stroke was cut unnoticed by the test, though the user is told): a fixed 1,024-pixel margin on tiled layers. (4) Closing a document whose undo held the whole-layer blur dropped about 34,000 stored keys one request each, and a browser's six requests at a time to one server kept the reopen behind them for many minutes (the engine opened the project in 0.15 s, the window reopened it directly in 120 s): `dropKeys` sends them in one request (`undoDropMany`, chunks of 20,000) on closing and on trimming, and a tiled layer's `dropAll` too. The passing run, on the 4 GB test machine: striped and painted 27 s, blurred 661 s, undone and redone exactly by 1,197 s, saved by 1,395 s, reopened exactly, exported equal to the composite at every recorded pixel by 1,704 s; the memory budget at most 65 percent used; no process killed; closing in 3 batch requests. Three earlier runs did not fail but were stopped: twice by the machine resetting between turns, once by my editing version.ts while the run used the development server, which reloaded the page (a rule now: nothing the window's server watches is touched during a browser run). Noted, not fixed: undo of a filter over a whole 600 MP layer takes about 5 minutes each way (many small requests); a stroke across nearly the whole picture can still be cut on a small machine (it says so); a photograph, which compresses far less than these stripes, needs several GB of free disk for a filter over the whole layer. Removed lines taken after the version edit. Removed from frontend:

## A giant document on the GPU, a texture per tile · _v1.62.9 (engine/tiled.ts, engine/index.ts, ui/stage.ts; e2e/test_tiled_gpu.py new, e2e/test_tiled_document.py)

DEV_PLAN 26.6g. `gpuLayers` takes the view, and a giant document's tiles in view go to the GPU display (it had kept them on the CPU since 1.62.3): `tileSpecs` hands each visible tile over as its own texture (2,048 a side, within any GPU's limit) at the level suiting the view's scale (`TiledRaster.levelOf`: the tile itself at half size or more, else a reduced copy at a half, a quarter, down to a sixteenth of its side, made when first asked and kept until the tile changes or leaves memory; reduced copies count in its resident bytes), so a frame's textures stay about one screen's worth at any zoom; an empty tile as the base colour, a 1-by-1 picture stretched over it (`baseSurface`, never under a real tile, which would double its opacity); a tile on disk as its preview, asked back at more than a sixteenth of actual size; each shown tile stamped as `drawTo` stamps those it draws (`touchView`), so paging never sends what is on screen to disk. Tiles do not overlap, so each drawn with the layer's opacity and blend equals the layer drawn whole. A mask, clipping mask or style on a tiled layer keeps the document on the CPU with its reason; asked without a view (the bench), it stays on the CPU and says so. The stage passes the view it draws with. Verified through the bench's WebGL2 `renderToPixels` against the CPU's drawing of the same view, on 120 MP with a rectangle across tile edges and a brush stroke on a second layer at 70 percent in Multiply: actual size where four tiles meet, largest difference 1 level, all within 4; an eighth, 2.5 MB of textures, largest 1; the whole document, 0.6 MB of textures, 99.75 percent within 4 (at edges the CPU's one-step shrink and the GPU's sixteenth-size copies filter differently, as the bench notes for ordinary documents at a quarter); tiles on disk asked back by a GPU frame and then drawn within 4. ## Filters on a giant layer, their undo streamed from disk · _v1.62.7 (engine/index.ts, engine/history.ts; ui/panels/filter-panel.ts; e2e/test_tiled_filter.py new)

DEV_PLAN 26.6e, completed. A bandable filter (Gaussian, Motion, Surface and Lens Blur, Unsharp Mask) on a giant layer runs through `bandedFilterTiled`: in place, a band of about 2 MP at a time (at least as tall as the filter's reach), each band's tiles brought back first and the next band's source read before this band is written (the ordering that keeps 26.4's in-place bands exact); each changed 512-pixel tile is written into the tiles and its before and after sent at once to the engine's store, kept as keys (`PixelPatch.disk`), so a whole-layer filter's undo (up to 2.4 GB a side at 600 MP) never sits in memory; tiles behind are paged out after each band. Its step is `streamed`: undo and redo apply it a tile at a time from the store (`bringBack`; `undoNow` and `redoNow` skip what is already in), undo paging leaves such patches alone, and trimming and closing drop both sides. While it runs, edits, strokes, undo and closing wait with a message (`busyWith`, `waiting`). A blur's spill past the canvas is not kept on a giant layer (an ordinary one grows to keep it). The filter panel sends bandable filters on a giant layer there, awaited on the background path (agents, the closed dialog) and started from the open dialog. Found while testing: the closing drops are one request per stored side, sent without waiting, and a page closed at once abandons those still in flight (the engine empties its store at its next start, so none outlives the session); the test waits for them, and a single batch drop is noted for later. ## A giant document's tiles on the engine's disk · _v1.62.4 (engine/tiled.ts, engine/index.ts; e2e/test_tiled_paging.py new)

DEV_PLAN 26.6c. Past the tiles' share of memory (40% of the budget; `tileShareOverride` for checks), `pageTiles` sends each tiled layer's least recently used tile out of view to the engine's store (the undo store since 1.60.8) after edits settle: `TiledRaster.pageOut` keeps a preview at a sixteenth of the tile's side and frees the canvas only once stored, abandoning (the stored copy dropped) a tile drawn into meanwhile (per-tile versions) or come into view. `drawTo` draws a tile on disk as its preview and, when the view needs more than the preview (scale above a sixteenth), asks for it (`onMissing`), which `bringTile` answers with `pageIn` (fetched once however many ask, the stored copy then dropped) and one redraw; the tiles a full-detail view drew are recorded and never paged while on screen, and a small view (the Navigator's) neither asks nor counts. A tile on disk is never read as empty nor drawn over as new: `tileAt` throws for it, and an operation brings its tiles back first with `ensure`. Closing a document drops its stored tiles. `bytes` (the memory count) is the tiles in memory and the previews; `residentBytes` is what the share bounds. Verified with the share at four tiles on a 600 MP document: twelve tiles of distinct patterns written, four stayed and eight went to the store (previews under 1 MB in all); reading a tile on disk refused; the view over tile 0 brought it back and showed every byte as written; ensure brought tile 11 back for an exact read; closing emptied the store of them; e2e/test_tiled_paging.py passed, with the tiled raster, tiled document and GL display suites (39 in all); unit 194; no errors. ## A layer as tiles · _v1.62.2 (engine/tiled.ts and engine/tiled.test.ts new; e2e/test_tiled_raster.py new)

DEV_PLAN 26.6a, the first stage of tiled layers (the register's M5 closes with 26.6). A browser canvas holds at most 2^28 pixels, so past 268 MP a layer cannot be one canvas; `TiledRaster` keeps 2,048-pixel tiles made only where something is drawn (an empty tile costs nothing: a 600 MP layer is 150 tiles, held only as they are used), with `read` and `write` across tile edges as one picture, `drawOn` (a drawing call on every tile a rectangle touches, in layer coordinates) and `drawTo` (the layer drawn out through a transform); `tilesIn` is the tile arithmetic, a plain function. Nothing uses it yet: documents up to 2^28 pixels keep their single-canvas layers, and the stages after this give tiled layers to the compositor (26.6b), the disk (c), painting (d), filters and export (e), undo (f) and the GPU display (g), with the 600 MP test (h). Found on the way, and kept in the code's notes rather than hidden: `drawOn` is exact for axis-aligned fills, but not for antialiased paths, because the browser may draw a path cut by a tile's edge another way than the whole path (measured on 1,200 by 800 over white with 64- and 512-pixel tiles: 99.8% of values within 2 levels, at most 45 at a few edge pixels; the differences lie along the shapes' edges, not the tiles', and were first mistaken for a CPU against GPU rasteriser difference, which a run at four tile sizes ruled out), so antialiased drawing will go through one scratch canvas and be written into tiles, which is exact; `drawTo` at a scale other than 1 can seam at tile edges, for 26.6b's one-pixel apron. Also caught while writing the tests: the comment's 144 tiles for 600 MP (it is 15 by 10, 150), and a test write at (4,000, 4,000) said to touch one tile that crosses 4,096 both ways. Verified: unit 194 (the six tile-arithmetic tests new); in the browser, 5 passed: 40 random writes (some partly outside) and reads equal to one canvas over every byte, fills exact, antialiased shapes within 2 levels for at least 99.5% of values over white, drawTo at actual size exact from the same pixels, and a 600 MP layer holding exactly the three tiles written into. ## Filters in bands on large layers · _v1.60.9 (engine/index.ts, engine/history.ts, engine/stroke.ts; ui/panels/filter-panel.ts)

DEV_PLAN 26.4, the filters' half. On a layer past 16 megapixels (`bandFrom`, settable for checks), a filter whose effect reaches a bounded distance and is the same wherever it is (`bandApron`: Gaussian, Motion, Surface and Lens Blur and Unsharp Mask; Smart Sharpen was not equal banded and runs whole) runs in bands of at least 512 rows, each read with the filter's reach of rows around it, so no whole-layer copy is made in or out (`bandedFilter`). As the whole-layer path does: with no selection or mask the layer grows by the filter's reach and keeps the spill (`bandedGrow`: each band drawn from the old layer onto transparent at the same offset, its middle rows written into the larger layer, one step, the old layer kept for undo); otherwise in place through the selection (each band's own coverage, blended by `blendThrough` tile by tile), each changed 512-pixel tile's undo its before only (`lazy`: its after read from the layer when undone, halving a filter's undo), the step's tiles then sent to the undo store at once (`pageNewest`; paging keeps a tile undone meanwhile). Smaller layers, masks, smart and shape layers, and deep, CMYK and Lab documents keep the whole-layer path. When memory refuses, `bandedFilter` says 'refused' and the callers report failure with the engine's reason. Found on the way: the first version declined the common growing case, which a probe calling the whole path without growth (as the panel never does) hid; in place, a band's apron above was read after the band above it had been written (each band's source is now read before the band above is written, bands at least as tall as the apron); a refusal had been reported as done (Gaussian Blur over MCP said Applied on the 150 MP document and changed nothing). Measured: the whole-layer path's peak is about eleven layer-sizes, its room check counts two, so the filters that cannot band need their count set from measurement (next). ## Older undo kept on the engine's disk · _v1.60.8 (engine/history.ts, engine/index.ts, io/api.ts, app.ts; backend routers/undo.py new, main.py)

DEV_PLAN 26.3, second part, so 26.3 is done. The engine keeps an undo store (`/api/undo`: put, get, drop; zlib-deflated in a session folder emptied when it starts), which the app hands the engine core as `undoStore` once the engine answers (the core makes no network calls itself). Once a document's undo tiles hold more than its share of memory (15% of the budget; `undoShareOverride` for checks), `pageOut` sends the oldest (`History.pageable`, the last two steps spared) to the store a tile at a time after edits settle (0.8 s after `refresh`), and lets a tile's pixels go (a pixel's worth kept, the patch marked `paged` with its key and size) only once the store has them; a tile whose document closed or whose step was trimmed while it was on its way has its key dropped rather than attached. Undo and redo run in the order asked through one queue (`historyOp`, `drainHistory`): at once when the step is in the window and nothing waits, else after `pageIn` brings its tiles back (each fetched once however many ask, then dropped from the store); the History panel's jump goes through the same queue. Closing a document and the History trimming a step (`History.onDrop`) drop their stored tiles. Found on the way: the first version let each queued undo run when its own fetch finished, which is only partly ordered (a redo pressed meanwhile on a step still in the window ran at once, before earlier undos), so six quick undos had reached step 2 of 1 after 3 seconds; one queue fixed it. A paging round still uploading when its document closed left 10 tiles in the store; checked after each upload now. Verified in the browser with an 8 MB share, six strokes on a 4,000 by 3,000 layer, each layer compared by hashing every byte: 47 of 70 tiles paged, the window's undo from 122 MB to 41; three undos and a redo pressed quickly over paged steps ending exactly after stroke 4 (1.4 s); four more undos exactly before any stroke (2.9 s), the store emptied as they came back; six redos exactly after stroke 6; the History panel three steps back after paging again exactly after stroke 3; closing the document left no tiles in the store; no errors. ## A stroke's undo as the tiles it changed · _v1.60.7 (engine/stroke.ts, engine/index.ts)

DEV_PLAN 26.3, first part (carried from 26.2). `PixelStroke.commitTiles` writes the stroke into the layer a 512-pixel tile at a time, reading each tile before and after and keeping it for undo only if it changed (`sameBytes`, four bytes at a time), so a stroke keeps the tiles it painted rather than the whole rectangle it spanned, and no rectangle-sized copy is made while committing. `endStroke` uses it for a plain stroke on pixels in an 8-bit RGB document; healing, Remove, masks, and 16-bit, 32-bit, CMYK and Lab documents keep the whole patch, which their steps after it read. Undo and redo apply the tiles as they applied the one patch. Next, 26.3's second part: older undo kept on the engine's disk.
